myopia.title: Twelve-Month Efficacy and Visual Tolerability of MyoPi Spectacle Lenses in Childhood Myopia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
myopia.summary: In children with myopia, MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses slowed 12-month axial elongation and cycloplegic refractive progression compared with single-vision spectacles, with acceptable overall safety and visual tolerability.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the 12-month efficacy, safety, and visual tolerability of MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses compared with conventional single-vision spectacle lenses (SVLs) in children with myopia. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, single-masked, parallel-group clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 116 eligible children were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or SVLs. Eligible participants were 8 to 13 years of age with bilateral cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.75 to -5.00 diopters (D). METHODS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or single-vision spectacle lenses and were followed at baseline, week 1, month 3, month 6, and month 12. myopia.title: A novel progressive defocus rigid gas permeable contact lenses for controlling axial elongation in myopic children: a retrospective study.
myopia.summary: Daily wearing of the DRGP lenses significantly curbs axial elongation in children when compared with SV lenses.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the efficacy of progressive defocus rigid gas permeable (DRGP) contact lenses in slowing down myopic progression and analyze the factors may influence axial length (AL) elongation in myopic children. METHODS: This was a retrospective study conducted on school-age children with myopia of -5.00 D or higher who were fitted with DRGP lenses. A matched control group wearing single-vision (SV) spectacles was selected based on comparable baseline age and refractive error. The AL was measured at baseline and at 6-month intervals thereafter. Changes in AL were compared between the groups. RESULTS: The DRGP lenses group comprised 56 subjects (39 females, mean age 11.96±2.32y), the SV spectacle group comprised 53 subjects (29 females, mean age 11.09±2.33y). myopia.title: Development and external validation of a prediction model for suboptimal orthokeratology control in adolescents.
myopia.summary: The study constructs a risk prediction model to forecast the likelihood that myopic adolescents will not achieve the ideal control effect after wearing OK lenses, offering proactive and effective guidance for frontline clinical practitioners in devising diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To develop and externally validate a risk prediction model for adolescents wearing orthokeratology (OK) lenses to predict the probability of suboptimal control effects. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of myopic children who used OK lenses consistently for at least 18mo between January 2021 and March 2023 were conducted. Various ophthalmic examinations and recorded baseline parameters were performed. A risk prediction model was developed using multifactorial logistic regression analysis, and the model's discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Brier score. RESULTS: The modeling group included 228 eyes (mean age, 10.46±1.99y; 55.7% males), with 120 right eyes (52.6%) and 108 left eyes (47.4%), and the validation group included 100 eyes. myopia.abstract: High myopia in children risks irreversible visual impairment, yet optimal interventions remain debated. This multicenter double-blind, randomized-controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect and safety of different atropine eyedrops for myopia control in children with high myopia, conducted in Shanghai Eye Diseases Prevention and Treatment Center, Shanghai General Hospital and Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital. Recruitment started on July 4th, 2021 and final follow-up was August, 21st, 2024. 219 children aged 6-12 years with myopia of at least -5.0 diopter (D) were recruited and randomly assigned to use either 0.01%(N = 76), 0.04%(N = 72), or 0.10%(N = 71) atropine eyedrops once nightly for both eyes over 24 months, and 182 participants completed trial; 219 (76:72:71) randomized cases were analyzed. myopia.summary: Vergence and accommodation of young myopic adults following the cessation of long-term atropine therapy for myopia progression differed from that of young myopic adults with no prior atropine use. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopia is a worldwide health concern due to its increasing prevalence and associated pathology, visual dysfunction, societal and quality of life impacts. Despite widespread use of atropine in Taiwan to manage myopia, its prevalence has increased. It has been suggested that the efficacy of atropine in slowing myopia progression may be limited by binocular vision (BV) function. Furthermore, the long-term impacts of atropine are unknown. This study aimed to contrast the BV profile of young myopic adults following cessation of atropine therapy for myopia control, relative to myopic adults without this history. METHODS: From a pool of young myopic adults attending a vision screening (n = 1320), 204 myopic (≤-0.50 dioptres, D) adults were invited for further clinical evaluation. myopia.summary: Myopia prevalence and visual behavior patterns in preschool children in Shunyi District are homogenized between urban and rural areas. In this age group, parental myopia is the only statistically significant independent predictor of childhood myopia (OR = 4.87). …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate urban-rural differences in refractive status among children aged 3-6 years in Shunyi District, Beijing, and their associations with daily visual behaviors, as well as to ascertain the relative contributions of familial risk and environmental factors in this population. METHODS: A total of 1,142 children (527 in urban areas and 615 in townships) from 11 kindergartens in Shunyi District were selected through stratified cluster random sampling. After fully paralyzing the ciliary muscle with 1% cyclopentolate, computerized refraction was performed to calculate the spherical equivalent (SE). Standardized questionnaires were used to obtain eye-use duration, eye-use distance, outdoor activity time and parental myopia history. myopia.title: Effects of Orthokeratology Versus Single-Vision Spectacles on Choroidal Structure and Microcirculation in Adolescents With Myopia.
myopia.summary: Compared with SV, OK lenses suppress AL elongation and SE progression. There are increases in ChT and 3D-CVI associated with this suppression, suggesting that ChT and 3D-CVI may serve as biomarkers for evaluating the efficacy of myopia-control interventions and supporting further investigation of their role in mechanism of myopia control.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the longitudinal effects of single-vision spectacles (SV) and orthokeratology (OK) lenses on choroidal structure and microcirculation in adolescents with myopia, and to analyze differences in responses between the two correction modalities. METHODS: This prospective, nonrandomized cohort study enrolled myopic patients aged 8 to 15 years. Axial length (AL), spherical equivalent refraction (SE), choroidal thickness (ChT), and three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index (3D-CVI) in nine macular sectors within concentric rings of 1, 3, and 6 mm in diameter were measured at baseline and at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after lens wear. Within-group and between-group differences were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 116 myopic patients aged 8 to 15 years were enrolled, including 62 in the SV group and 54 in the OK group. myopia.abstract: BackgroundMyopia is an increasing global public health concern, particularly in East Asia. Cylindrical Annular Refractive Element (CARE) spectacle lenses aim to slow myopia progression by inducing peripheral myopic defocus. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of CARE lenses versus single-vision spectacle lenses in children.MethodsWe conducted a systematic search for randomized controlled trials comparing CARE spectacle lenses to single-vision lenses in children with myopia. Primary outcomes were mean change in spherical equivalent refraction and axial length. All analyses were performed using R software. myopia.summary: This prospective cohort study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of modified posterior scleral reinforcement (PSR) combined with comprehensive therapy versus conventional optical correction for controlling myopia progression in patients with high and pathologic myopia. …
myopia.abstract: This prospective cohort study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of modified posterior scleral reinforcement (PSR) combined with comprehensive therapy versus conventional optical correction for controlling myopia progression in patients with high and pathologic myopia. A total of 203 patients aged 8-18 years were allocated, based on preference, to either the combination therapy group (n = 111; receiving modified PSR plus low-concentration atropine and/or peripheral defocus optical correction) or the conventional control group (n = 92; fitted with rigid gas-permeable contact lenses only). After accounting for 10 withdrawals during the study period, 193 patients completed the 24-month follow-up (combination group, n = 102; control group, n = 91) and were included in the final analysis. myopia.summary: In this computational model, both BF and AR lens designs produced measurable changes in simulated RGC temporal activity relative to SV, with AR inducing greater and more configuration-independent modulation. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To computationally evaluate how single vision (SV), concentric bifocal (BF), and a contact lens with non-refractive opaque elements (AR) lens designs modulate retinal ganglion cell (RGC) activity. METHODS: Wide-field retinal simulations were generated using a schematic myopic eye corrected with SV, BF, and AR designs across three stimuli (Lena image, logMAR chart, dynamic gratings), three pupil diameters, and three residual accommodative error configurations. For each configuration, retinal image montages emulating blink-induced on-eye lens movement over one second were processed through a multilayer biomimetic virtual retina model to simulate RGC spike trains, quantified using median absolute deviation (MAD) and up-crossing rate (UCR). myopia.title: Atropine, red-light therapy, and lenslet spectacles for premyopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
myopia.summary: Available randomized evidence suggests that some interventions may reduce early refractive change in children classified as premyopic, while effects on axial elongation remain less certain. Atropine had the largest evidence base, but certainty was low for SE and very low for AL. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Earlier onset of childhood myopia is associated with greater subsequent progression and a higher risk of high myopia and related ocular complications. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether low-concentration atropine, repeated low-level red-light therapy (RLRL), and study-specific lenslet-array spectacle designs reduce refractive change and axial elongation in non-myopic children classified as premyopic. METHODS: This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252431) and conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 17 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials with follow-up ranging from 3 to 24 months that included children meeting study-specific criteria for premyopia and reported cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE) and/or axial length (AL). myopia.title: Efficacy of Combined Highly Aspherical Lenslet Target (HALT) Spectacles and Low-Dose Atropine in Children with Poor Response to Atropine Monotherapy over 24 Months.
myopia.summary: Objectives: To evaluate the 24-month efficacy of combining highly aspherical lenslet target (HALT) spectacle lenses with low-dose atropine (LDA) in children with poor response to atropine monotherapy. …
myopia.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the 24-month efficacy of combining highly aspherical lenslet target (HALT) spectacle lenses with low-dose atropine (LDA) in children with poor response to atropine monotherapy. Methods: This prospective interventional cohort study included myopic children aged 6-11 years who continued to progress despite LDA (0.01-0.025%). Fifty children completed 12 months of follow-up and 48 completed 24 months. At 12 months, atropine dosage was maintained, reduced, or increased according to clinical discretion. Cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) and axial length (AL) were measured at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Results: Myopia progression during the first year (SER: -0.07 ± 0.45 D; AL: 0.13 ± 0.14 mm) was markedly lower than during the 6 months before treatment (SER: -0.61 ± 0.39 D; AL: 0.24 ± 0.12 mm). myopia.abstract: Background/Objectives: Repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) therapy has recently emerged as a promising treatment for childhood myopia. Choroidal thickening has been proposed as a key biological mechanism underlying its therapeutic efficacy; however, evidence regarding its effects on subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), particularly in children with premyopia, remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate the effects of RLRL therapy on SFCT in pediatric patients with myopia and premyopia. Methods: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were systematically searched from database inception through 29 September 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing RLRL therapy with controls in participants younger than 18 years were included. The primary outcome was the change in SFCT at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. myopia.summary: Background/Objectives: To ascertain if the residual decentration of contact lenses with peripheral retinal defocusing geometry could be associated with alterations in the astigmatic refractive component over a six-month period of wear in children. …
myopia.abstract: Background/Objectives: To ascertain if the residual decentration of contact lenses with peripheral retinal defocusing geometry could be associated with alterations in the astigmatic refractive component over a six-month period of wear in children. Methods: A total of 39 eyes from 39 participants (mean age: 11.1 ± 1.54 years, ranging from 6 to 13 years) were included. Participants underwent an eye examination and were assigned to one of three studied lenses: multifocal contact lenses with either non-adjustable (Biofinity Multifocal) or adjustable parameters (Gentle 80 Multifocal), or a contact lens designed for myopia control (MYLO). After six months of lens wear, a refractive assessment was performed and topographic images of the eye with the contact lens fitted were taken. myopia.title: The economic burden of myopia diagnosis and treatment: A cross-sectional cost-of-illness study in Yantai, China.
myopia.summary: Myopia imposes a substantial economic burden in Yantai, especially among younger individuals, those with early-onset myopia, individuals with lower educational attainment, and those using expensive correction methods.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia has become a major global public health and economic issue. Population-based cost-of-illness evidence from prefecture-level cities in China remains limited. This study aimed to quantify the direct economic burden of myopia diagnosis and treatment among individuals aged 6 to 55 years in Yantai, China, and to identify factors associated with per-capita direct myopia expenditure. METHODS: A cross-sectional cost-of-illness study was conducted between September and November 2021 in Yantai. A multistage sampling strategy was used to recruit students and their parents from primary schools, middle schools, high schools/vocational schools, and universities. Questionnaire data on demographic characteristics, myopia status, correction methods, healthcare utilization, and costs were collected. myopia.summary: The global myopia epidemic, especially among children, poses a major public health burden. Orthokeratology (OK) is an established intervention for slowing myopia progression, yet its conventional practice is constrained by variable treatment responses, an experience-dependent fitting process, and the need for vigilant long-term safety mon …
myopia.abstract: The global myopia epidemic, especially among children, poses a major public health burden. Orthokeratology (OK) is an established intervention for slowing myopia progression, yet its conventional practice is constrained by variable treatment responses, an experience-dependent fitting process, and the need for vigilant long-term safety monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an approach to enhance precision, efficiency, and accessibility across the entire OK care cycle. This review assesses AI applications in OK, encompassing pre-treatment efficacy prediction, AI-assisted lens fitting and automated fit assessment during treatment, and post-treatment safety monitoring with complication risk alert. myopia.title: Retinal Sensitive Areas in Myopia Control: Identifying the Potential Retinal 'Sweet Spot'-A Scoping Review.
myopia.summary: Myopia control may involve targeting the peripheral retina to slow eye growth; however, there is no consensus on the optimal lens design, and treatment effects remain variable. This scoping review explored whether a specific retinal region is sensitive to visual manipulation, which could inform more effective treatments. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia control may involve targeting the peripheral retina to slow eye growth; however, there is no consensus on the optimal lens design, and treatment effects remain variable. This scoping review explored whether a specific retinal region is sensitive to visual manipulation, which could inform more effective treatments. A literature search was conducted in December 2025, with updates in March and June 2026 using PubMed, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library. Full manuscripts in English in animals and humans were included and screened by title, abstract, and full text for relevance. A total of 134 studies were identified, with 22 meeting inclusion criteria (13 human, 9 animal studies). Evidence across studies suggests that both the extent and location of defocus influence axial elongation. myopia.abstract: An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9-14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. myopia.title: Effectiveness of a School-Centered Intervention for Myopia and Obesity Comorbidity in Children: A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
myopia.summary: The rising comorbidity of myopia and overweight/obesity (OWOB) in children shares modifiable behavioral pathways, yet evidence for integrated prevention remains limited. We conducted a cluster-randomized, hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation trial in 36 pair-matched Beijing schools. …
myopia.abstract: The rising comorbidity of myopia and overweight/obesity (OWOB) in children shares modifiable behavioral pathways, yet evidence for integrated prevention remains limited. We conducted a cluster-randomized, hybrid type I effectiveness-implementation trial in 36 pair-matched Beijing schools. Of 4991 enrolled students in Grades 1-4 and 7, 3426 (68.6%) completed the 12-month follow-up. The school-centered "22510SS" intervention targeted outdoor activity, screen time, diet, sleep, and health monitoring. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in spherical equivalent or BMI change, or in the prevalence of myopia, OWOB, or their comorbidity. The intervention improved the overall behavior-improvement rate (39.7% vs. 33.7%; OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.00-1.80). myopia.title: Effects of myopia control interventions on myopia progression and strabismus-related outcomes in children with intermittent exotropia: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
myopia.summary: INTRODUCTION: Intermittent exotropia frequently coexists with childhood myopia. Myopia-control interventions may affect accommodation, convergence or binocular function but evidence specific to children with intermittent exotropia has not been synthesised. …
myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intermittent exotropia frequently coexists with childhood myopia. Myopia-control interventions may affect accommodation, convergence or binocular function but evidence specific to children with intermittent exotropia has not been synthesised. This review will assess efficacy in randomised trials and comparative effectiveness and safety in non-randomised studies considering both myopia progression and strabismus-related outcomes. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 statement. myopia.title: Early Axial Length Response Predicts Long-Term Myopia Control in Children Undergoing Orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Early AL change after 6 months of OK wear is a useful biomarker for risk‑stratifying long‑term myopia control response. Children with ΔAL₆m ≤ 0.07 mm were much more likely to achieve a favourable AL response, whereas those with ΔAL₆m ≥ 0.09 mm had an elevated risk of poor AL response.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether early axial length (AL) change after 6 months of orthokeratology (OK) wear serves as a clinically meaningful biomarker for predicting long-term myopia control after 2 years. METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 101 children from a multicentre OK cohort who completed 24 months of follow‑up, with AL measured at baseline and at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months. Early AL shortening was defined as a ≥0.01 mm reduction after 6 months. Longitudinal AL change was assessed using linear mixed‑effects models. To evaluate predictive utility, separate logistic regression models were fitted using the 6-month AL change (ΔAL₆m) as a continuous predictor for two predefined AL outcome categories: favourable AL response (ΔAL₂₄m ≤ 0.30 mm) and poor AL response (>0.59 mm). myopia.summary: Low-concentration atropine demonstrated a dose-response relationship for reducing cumulative myopia incidence and slowing refractive progression in pre-myopic children, but no such relationship on axial length. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the dose-response relationship and individual efficacy of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops for preventing myopia onset in pre-myopic children. DESIGN: Twelve-month randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial conducted in Shanghai primary schools (March 2023-December 2024). METHODS: Children aged 6-10 years with cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction of -0.50 to + 0.75 diopters (D) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo or 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine once daily. Primary outcome was 12-month cumulative myopia incidence (SER ≤ -0.50 D in the worse eye); secondary outcomes were changes in SER and axial length of the worse eye. Children with ocular or systemic diseases, prior orthokeratology use, or other myopia control interventions were excluded. myopia.title: Axial Length Stabilization and Scleral Curvature Changes following Repeated Low-level Red-light Therapy in Children with High Myopia.
myopia.summary: RLRL therapy was associated with AL stabilization in highly myopic eyes. Although apparent scleral curvature change was observed, it was a post hoc analysis in a small number of eyes and its association with choroidal thickness and the shortening of the AL needs further investigation.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence and extent of axial length (AL) shortening after 12 months of repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) therapy in highly myopic eyes. In addition, to investigate the relationship between the AL shortening and changes in the posterior scleral curvature in the swept-source optical coherence tomographic (SS-OCT) images. METHODS: Thirty participants aged 8 to 18 years with high myopia were studied. The spherical equivalent of refractive error (SER) and AL were measured, and SS-OCT images were recorded at baseline, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after beginning RLRL therapy. RESULTS: Twelve months of RLRL therapy led to an average reduction in myopic SER by 0.29 D (95% CI, 0.10 to 0.49 D; P < 0.05) and stabilization of AL, with a mean change of -0.03 mm (95% CI, -0.09 to 0.04 mm; P = 1.00). myopia.title: From Corneal Epithelium to Endothelium: Long-Term Corneal Changes in Myopic Children Wearing Daily Disposable Hydrogel Soft Contact Lenses.
myopia.summary: Long-term wear of daily disposable hydrogel SCLs in children did not alter CET and CST significantly over a minimum 10-year period. Corneal endothelial integrity and pleomorphism were maintained, with higher polymegethism observed only in two peripheral regions. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the long-term impact of soft contact lens (SCL) wear on the cornea in children. METHODS: Twenty-one participants who had worn daily disposable hydrogel SCLs for over 10 years (≥10 h/day, 6 days/week) since ages 8-12 years were recruited, together with age-matched controls without contact lens wear. Corneal epithelial (CET) and stromal thickness (CST) were measured using anterior segment optical coherence tomography in central (2 mm), mid-peripheral (2-5 mm) and peripheral (5-6 mm) annular regions. Corneal endothelium was imaged with a non-contact specular microscope to calculate corneal endothelial cell density (ECD), coefficients of variation of cell size (polymegethism, CV,%) and percentage of hexagonal cells (pleomorphism, HEX,%) in the central and six peripheral regions. myopia.title: Diffractive Soft Contact Lenses for Modifying Ocular Longitudinal Chromatic Aberration.
myopia.summary: This study presents the first demonstration of a soft contact lens capable of manipulating ocular LCA, including sign reversal. LIRIC diffractive contact lenses offer a practical platform for tuning the eye's chromatic defocus cues and warrant further investigation as a novel myopia control strategy.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Childhood myopia prevalence is increasing rapidly worldwide, underscoring the need for effective strategies to slow its progression. Longitudinal chromatic aberration (LCA) has been identified as an optical cue for the sign of defocus that may guide childhood eye growth and emmetropisation. Reversing the sign of ocular LCA has been proposed as a myopia control strategy, yet no wearable devices have demonstrated this capability. Here, diffractive soft contact lenses fabricated using laser-induced refractive index change (LIRIC) are introduced to modify ocular LCA. METHODS: Contact lenses were made with four diffractive powers (1.5, 2.0, 3.0 and 6.0 D) using LIRIC, a femtosecond laser writing technique that modifies the internal refractive index of a soft contact lens without altering external geometry. Lens LCA was characterised using a custom multi-wavelength Badal optical bench

myopia.title: Cost-effectiveness of monotherapy and combination therapy for myopia control in Chinese children.
myopia.summary: Under limited budget conditions, outdoor activities and defocus spectacles represent advantageous cost-effective treatment options. When the budget is sufficient, RLRL may be considered a promising option pending confirmation of its long-term safety and effectiveness, and 0.01% atropine combined with DIMS is the preferred cost-effective o …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia poses a major public health and economic burden in China, necessitating cost-effectiveness evaluations of control strategies. We aimed to assess cost-effectiveness of single/combined myopia control in children and adolescents to optimise strategies. METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of myopia control interventions in Chinese children (aged 6-18 years). Annual changes in axial length (AL) and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) were the primary outcomes. Additionally, we used a decision-analytic Markov model with clinical and cost data from China to evaluate 16 myopia control strategies for eight-year-old children over eight years from a patient perspective, with 3% discounting. myopia.title: Combination therapy for myopia control using defocus incorporated multiple segments spectacles in children refractory to higher-dose atropine.
myopia.summary: Combination therapy of atropine and DIMS was effective in myopia control in children with poor response to atropine treatment alone. Further large-scale and long-term studies are needed to confirm these observations.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To explore the efficacy of myopia control by adding defocus incorporated multiple segments (DIMS) spectacles in children who are refractory to higher-dose atropine control. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included children aged 6-14 who had previously used ≥0.125% atropine for at least one year and were later treated with DIMS plus atropine for over six months. Annual axial length (AL) changes during monotherapy and combination therapy were compared using paired t-tests. Generalized estimating equations were used to analyze correlations with outcome variables. RESULTS: In total, 57 eyes from 29 patients (mean age 9.8 years) were included in our final analysis. METHODS: The right eyes of 10 young adult myopes were corrected with standard single vision (SV, Proclear 1 day, CooperVision, Inc.) and DF (MiSight 1 day, CooperVision, Inc.) contact lenses. myopia.abstract: The rising prevalence of myopia in children has become a major concern due to its long-term effects on eye health and vision. This increase has prompted extensive research into the environmental and biological factors influencing eye development. Recent studies highlight the critical role of specific light wavelengths, particularly violet (360-400 nm) and blue (400-500 nm), in regulating eye growth. Violet light is thought to support choroidal health by activating photopigments in the retina, helping to maintain proper eye growth and reduce the risk of myopia. Conversely, the elimination of blue light through blue-blocking lenses has been linked to changes in the refractive dynamics of the eye, potentially contributing to excessive axial elongation a key characteristic of myopia. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included first time D.S.D.O. spectacle lens users with no documented prior myopia control lens wear and bilateral follow up of at least 12 months. Repeated axial length measurements from March 2022 through July 2026 underwent prespecified longitudinal quality control. The primary mixed effects model adjusted for age, sex, baseline axial length, baseline spherical equivalent, and any recorded atropine use. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the one-year efficacy of novel partition multipoint defocus optics technology (PMDOT) lenses in slowing myopia progression, compared to lenses with highly aspherical lenslets (HAL). METHODS: This is a 1-year interim analysis of an ongoing 2-year, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial, in which 194 children ages 8 to 13 years with spherical equivalent refraction (SER) of -0.75 to -4.5 diopters (D) were randomized to either the PMDOT or HAL group. The primary outcome of the full trial was the mean between-group difference in SER change at 2 years, and the non-inferiority margin was -0.3 D. Secondary outcomes included changes in axial length (AL), choroidal thickness (ChT), and other biometric parameters, as well as best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at 2 years and subjective visual experience. Lens parameters were adjusted to optimize the fitting: the power of the alignment curve was reduced by 0.25 D, the toricity was increased, the sagittal depth of the reverse curve was raised by 20 μm, and the peripheral curve was upgraded by one step. myopia.summary: In this study, DIMS lenses were associated with greater efficacy than 0.01% atropine in reducing myopia progression, particularly in children aged 6-11 years. Differences in adherence between the interventions should be considered when interpreting these findings. …

This study evaluated the effectiveness of Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacle lenses versus 0.01% atropine eye drops in slowing myopia progression in European children over two years. METHODS: A total of 110 Polish and Ukrainian children aged 6-16 years without significant ocular pathology were randomised to single-vision spectacles plus nightly 0.01% atropine (group A) or DIMS lenses plus nightly placebo (group B). Primary outcomes were changes in cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) and axial length, assessed at 6-month intervals. RESULTS: At 24 months, mean axial elongation was lower in group B (0.22 ± 0.22 mm) than in group A (0.32 ± 0.29 mm), particularly among children aged 6-11 years (0.30 ± 0.23 mm vs 0.48 ± 0.31 mm). MATERIALS & METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study enrolled 14 young, healthy emmetropic participants aged 18 to 22 years with no ocular or systemic diseases. Comprehensive eye examinations were conducted, and mfERG recordings were obtained using six different condition scenarios. myopia.summary: Both low-dose atropine concentrations resulted in short-term choroidal thickening in Egyptian myopic children, with a stronger response in the 0.05% group. METHODS: This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 92 myopic children aged 6-12 years. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 0.05% atropine, 0.01% atropine, or placebo eye drops nightly for 16 weeks. Only one eye (the right eye if both were eligible) was included per participant to avoid inter-eye correlation bias. Comprehensive ophthalmic examination was performed at baseline and at 4, 8, 12, and 16 weeks. SFCT and anterior scleral thickness were measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT). myopia.summary: Routinely recorded baseline factors did not provide clinically useful individual-level prediction of the first-year progression category. With this predictor set, observing early on-treatment progression remains the practical way to identify children who may need escalation.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine whether routinely recorded baseline clinical factors, alone or combined with machine-learning predictive modeling, can provide individual risk stratification for myopia control by identifying children who will progress more than 0.25 diopters (D) during their first year of low-dose atropine treatment. METHODS: From a 555-child source cohort treated initially with atropine 0.01% or 0.02%, 468 children had qualifying 9- to 15-month follow-up; 427 children started atropine monotherapy without a baseline optical adjunct. A child was classified as poorly responsive if either treated eye progressed more than 0.25 D of spherical equivalent refraction from baseline to the qualifying visit. myopia.summary: Orthokeratology effectively slowed axial elongation in children with low myopia. Specialty-designed ortho-k lenses with altered corneal reshaping characteristics demonstrated greater inhibition of axial elongation.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Orthokeratology (ortho-k) is widely used for myopia control in children. Specialty-designed ortho-k lenses with a modified corneal reshaping profile may offer an alternative approach for myopia control through altered lens design characteristics. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this lens design in slowing axial elongation and myopia progression in children with low myopia, and to explore ocular structural predictors of the treatment response. METHODS: This prospective, randomised, double-masked clinical trial enroled 80 children aged 8-14 years with low myopia (-1.00 to -3.00 D). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to wear either standard-design ortho-k lenses or specialty-designed ortho-k lenses designed to produce a reduced corneal central zone moulding area for 12 months. myopia.summary: In this selected high-risk cohort, questionnaire-derived behavioural scores did not provide robust adjusted associations or clinically useful cross-school prediction. The findings should not be used for individualized risk stratification or causal behavioural claims. …

METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of 200 myopic schoolchildren from 10 schools who had been selected for the intervention stage of a parent study after rapid progression (>=1.0 D/year). Parent-study documentation indicates a 12-month follow-up and progression calculated from the change in spherical-equivalent refraction (SE). Effectiveness of 0.02% and 0.04% Atropine Therapy for Myopia Control in Czech Children: The MARS Trial.
myopia.summary: Nightly 0.02% and 0.04% atropine reduced axial elongation and myopia progression over 12 months compared with placebo. The trial was not designed or powered to establish equivalence between the active doses; within this sample, no statistically significant difference was detected between them.
myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Low-dose atropine eye drops slow childhood myopia progression, but randomized evidence in European children and for intermediate concentrations remains limited. This study evaluated 0.02% and 0.04% atropine for 12-month myopia control in Czech children. METHODS: The MARS study was an investigator-initiated, phase IIIb, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial. Children aged 6-11 years with documented accelerated prerandomization axial length (AL) elongation and cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.50 to -4.75 D were randomized 2:1:1 to nightly 0.02% atropine, 0.04% atropine, or placebo. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare refractive progression between myopic and premyopic eyes within the same children and evaluate the potential role of low-dose atropine on premyopia progression. METHODS: This 12-month randomized controlled trial enrolled children aged 4-12 years with one myopic and one premyopic eye. Participants were assigned to three groups: no atropine intervention (NI), 0.01% atropine in myopic eye (MI), or bilateral intervention (BI). Spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL) were measured at 3-month intervals. Linear mixed-effects models included all randomized participants, while generalized estimating equations with multiple imputation and Cox regression assessed myopic shift (ΔSE ≤ -0.50 D/year) and myopia onset. myopia.title: [Myopia in children].
myopia.summary: Myopia is a refractive anomaly, a global public health issue, mainly due to an increase in axial length of the eyeball. Myopia is increasing worldwide with the appearance of a "myopia global growing epidemic". …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a refractive anomaly, a global public health issue, mainly due to an increase in axial length of the eyeball. Myopia is increasing worldwide with the appearance of a "myopia global growing epidemic". In children under 6 years old, 20 % have abnormalities, the most common of which are primarily refractive abnormalities, followed by strabismus and amblyopia. Myopia presents a major risk of complications, correlated with its severity, such as retinal detachment, retinal neovascularization, early cataracts and glaucoma. In children with high myopia, syndromic myopia must be explored. Early detection of myopia onset and progression is essential to myopia control strategies. The most promising treatments include outdoor activities, defocusing corrective lenses, defocusing contact lenses, orthokeratology and pharmacological treatments with low-dose atropine.

myopia.title: Overnight orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. …
myopia.abstract: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. The modern orthokeratology lens has a substantial history from its origins of attempting to flatten the corneal curvature with a spherical rigid contact lens to sophisticated gas permeable lenses, designed to reshape the cornea. These lenses are predominantly prescribed for children to slow myopia progression and limit axial elongation of the eye. This article reviews the peer-reviewed literature on the efficacy of orthokeratology for myopia control, sustainability after treatment is discontinued, and the safety concerns of overnight contact lens wear. Future avenues of research are discussed.

myopia.summary: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. …
myopia.abstract: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. These two epidemics are linked, since the increasingly early onset of myopia, combined with high progression rates, naturally generates an epidemic of high myopia, with high prevalences of "acquired" high myopia appearing around the age of 11-13. The major risk factors identified are intensive education, and limited time outdoors. The localization of the epidemic appears to be due to the high educational pressures and limited time outdoors in the region, rather than to genetically elevated sensitivity to these factors. myopia.summary: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. …
myopia.abstract: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. Although there is still uncertainty in the risk factors underlying differences in myopia prevalence between ethnic groups, rates in children of East Asian descent are typically higher regardless of where they live. Mounting evidence also suggests that myopia prevalence in children increases with age. Earlier commencement and more rigorous education systems in these countries, resulting in more time spent on near-work activities and less time on outdoor activities, may be responsible for the earlier age of myopia onset. myopia.summary: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. …
myopia.abstract: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. Despite many publications dedicated to the topic, little attention has been devoted to understanding 'efficacy' in myopia control and its application. Treatment effect has been expressed in multiple ways, making comparison between therapies and prognosis for an individual patient difficult. Available efficacy data are generally limited to two to three years making long-term treatment effect uncertain. From an evidence-based perspective, efficacy projection should be conservative and not extend beyond that which has been empirically established. myopia.summary: The 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops reduced myopia progression along a concentration-dependent response. All concentrations were well tolerated without an adverse effect on vision-related quality of life. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Low-concentration atropine is an emerging therapy for myopia progression, but its efficacy and optimal concentration remain uncertain. Our study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-concentration atropine eye drops at 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% compared with placebo over a 1-year period. DESIGN: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 438 children aged 4 to 12 years with myopia of at least -1.0 diopter (D) and astigmatism of -2.5 D or less. METHODS: A 2-year double-masked randomised controlled trial was carried out in 183 Chinese children aged 8-13 years, with myopia between -1.00 and -5.00 D and astigmatism ≤1.50 D. myopia.abstract: Myopia is not a simple refractive error, but an eyesight-threatening disease. There is a high prevalence of myopia, 80% to 90%, in young adults in East Asia; myopia has become the leading cause of blindness in this area. As the myopic population increases globally, the severity of its impact is predicted. Approximately one fifth of the myopic population has high myopia (≥-6 diopters), which results in irreversible vision loss such as retinal detachment, choroidal neovascularization, cataracts, glaucoma, and macular atrophy. The increasing prevalence of school myopia in the past few decades may be a result of gene-environment interactions. However, earlier school myopia onset would accompany faster myopia progression and greater risk of high myopia later in life. myopia.summary: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. Despite a plethora of myopia research, the molecular/cellular mechanisms underlying the development of myopia are not well understood, preventing the search for the most effective pharmacological control. Consequently, several approaches to slowing down myopia progression in the actively growing eyes of children have been underway. So far, atropine, an anticholinergic blocking agent, has been most effective and is used by clinicians in off-label ways for myopia control. myopia.abstract: Myopia is the commonest ocular abnormality but as a research topic remains at the margins of mainstream ophthalmology. The concept that most myopes fall into the category of 'physiological myopia' undoubtedly contributes to this position. Yet detailed analysis of epidemiological data linking myopia with a range of ocular pathologies from glaucoma to retinal detachment demonstrates statistically significant disease association in the 0 to -6 D range of 'physiological myopia'. The calculated risks from myopia are comparable to those between hypertension, smoking and cardiovascular disease. In the case of myopic maculopathy and retinal detachment the risks are an order of magnitude greater. This finding highlights the potential benefits of interventions that can limit or prevent myopia progression. myopia.abstract: To avoid complications of high myopia the best solution would be to prevent myopia development from the very beginning. Many studies have suggested that the frequently quoted myopia boom is related to changes in visual experiences during more demanding education and not due to changes in genetic factors. To avoid myopia development it would therefore be best to carry out a better control of visual experience of children. In this article new approaches are described to record and improve visual habits in children, e.g. new sensors attached to the spectacle frames to document brightness, reading distance and reading duration, changes in text contrast polarity during reading, potential role of smartphones and some not yet fully explored orally applied substances to inhibit myopia.

Preventing Myopia.
myopia.summary: Effective pharmacological and optical measures are now available to lessen the progression of myopia. The increasing prevalence of myopia should motivate pediatricians, parents, and schools to pay attention to risk factors such as close-up work and lack of daylight exposure, particularly in view of the increased use of digital media.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nearsightedness (myopia) has become more common around the world recently, mainly because of changes in visual, educational, and recreational behavior. The question arises how the risk of myopia and its progression can be reduced. This would lessen the prevalence and severity of myopia and also lower the risk of secondary diseases that impair visual acuity. METHODS: The PubMed/Medline database was selectively searched for pertinent literature. RESULTS: The risk of myopia is lowered by exposure to daylight and increased by activities performed at short visual distances (close-up work). A person with little exposure to daylight has a fivefold risk of developing myopia, which can rise as high as a 16-fold risk if that person also performs close-up work. myopia.summary: We proposed an explanation for the underlying optical mechanism for the clinically observed increase of straylight with axial myopia, when corrected with glasses. Our model predicts that the increase can be as high as 0.12 log units for a myopic eye with 10 dioptres, which agrees with prior observations.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Straylight refers to an optical phenomenon that takes places in the eye and leads to a deterioration of the retinal image. Past clinical findings suggest an increase of straylight with the eye's axial length, but the aetiology of the phenomenon was unclear. The purpose of this work is to demonstrate, through raytracing, simple geometrical optics, and the well-established inverse-angle square law for the angular distribution of straylight, why straylight increases when a myopic eye is corrected with spectacles. METHODS: The angular dependence of straylight is investigated using geometrical optics. An expression relating the eye's 2nd nodal point, the ocular axial length and the eye's straylight parameter S is found. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This single-masked randomized clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of orthokeratology (ortho-k) for myopic control. METHODS: A total of 102 eligible subjects, ranging in age from 6 to 10 years, with myopia between 0.50 and 4.00 diopters (D) and astigmatism not more than 1.25D, were randomly assigned to wear ortho-k lenses or single-vision glasses for a period of 2 years. Axial length was measured by intraocular lens calculation by a masked examiner and was performed at the baseline and every 6 months. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00962208. RESULTS: In all, 78 subjects (37 in ortho-k group and 41 in control group) completed the study. The average axial elongation, at the end of 2 years, were 0.36 ± 0.24 and 0.63 ± 0.26 mm in the ortho-k and control groups, respectively, and were significantly slower in the ortho-k group (P < 0.01). METHODS: Children in the placebo group (phase 1) were switched to receive 0.05% atropine from the beginning of the second-year follow-up, whereas those in the 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine groups continued with the same regimen. The aim of this study was to compare efficacy and visual side effects of 3 lower doses of atropine: 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01%. DESIGN: Single-center, double-masked, randomized study. DESIGN: Randomized, double-masked clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 400 children originally randomized to receive atropine 0.5%, 0.1%, or 0.01% once daily in both eyes in a 2:2:1 ratio. METHODS: Children received atropine for 24 months (phase 1), after which medication was stopped for 12 months (phase 2). Children who had myopia progression (≥-0.50 diopters [D] in at least 1 eye) during phase 2 were restarted on atropine 0.01% for a further 24 months (phase 3). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Change in spherical equivalent and axial length over 5 years. myopia.abstract: The review summarizes experimental and clinical data attesting to the important role the choroid plays in the development of refraction through optically oriented thickness changes and the release of growth factors. Because of its unique anatomical position, the choroid can influence the transmission of a cascade of chemical signals from the retina to the sclera and thereby affect the growth of the eye. Understanding the relationship between the optical defocus and the response of the choroid to it will help uncover the fundamental mechanisms for controlling eye growth and develop new strategies for preventing the progression of myopia.

myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This review arms practitioners with the evidence-based information they need to fully manage myopia. RECENT FINDINGS: The recent peer-reviewed literature is critically evaluated to provide a comprehensive analysis of the safety and efficacy of behavioural, optical and pharmaceutical myopia management. Importantly, the paper addresses not only who to treat, but how to treat them, and when to stop or modify treatments. Finally, the paper discusses expectations for treatment and why slowing myopia by even 1 dioptre improves long term health outcomes. SUMMARY: The management of an individual child should be underpinned by the evidence-based literature and clinicians must stay alert to ongoing myopia research that will undoubtedly result in an evolution of the standard of care for the myopic and pre-myopic child.

METHODS: A total of 214 residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota (118 girls and 96 boys; median age, 11 years; range, 6 to 15 years) received atropine for myopia from 1967 through 1974. myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Many clinicians have noted that patients demonstrate a myopic refractive change following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). This apparent myopic shift disappears with cycloplegia, yet stubbornly reappears as soon as the pharmaceutical effect wears off. We propose that this shift is secondary to an irritative lesion that affects the parasympathetic innervation, resulting in ciliary body contracture. The dilemma for the clinician is whether to provide the immediate relief of clear distance vision by prescribing additional minus lenses, or to work toward attempting to re-establish the baseline refractive error. myopia.abstract: This review summarises some recent aspects of myopia research. The following conclusions have been drawn. As long as myopia progression is visually controlled, at least three different interventions are possible: (i) spectacles/contact lenses which correct only the centre of the visual field and leave the periphery somewhat myopic, (ii) outdoor activity or equivalent temporary increase in illuminance, (iii) pharmacological intervention of retinal growth signals that are transmitted to the underlying sclera. Options (i) and (ii) can be used without risks although there is still room for improvement of the variables. Option (iii) has re-entered a new phase of orientation with new searches for candidate targets after previous testing with muskarinic antagonists (pirenzepine) in children did not enter phase 3 level. myopia.abstract: Myopia is a worldwide public health problem. However, its understanding is incomplete, and many of its preventative and therapeutic aspects remain controversial. Nearwork is a primary, environmentally based factor in the aetiology of permanent myopia (PM), with nearwork-induced transient myopia (NITM) being a possible contributory component. A relationship between PM and NITM has been suggested, but that connection has remained somewhat indirect and elusive. However, based on recent converging evidence from clinical, laboratory and modelling studies, a five-fold argument will be advanced for a possible link between PM and NITM.

myopia.abstract: Current knowledge of the refractive shifts (twilight myopia, night myopia, dark focus) that occur as the luminance is progressively lowered from photopic levels is reviewed. In complete darkness, myopic changes of the order of 1 dioptre are typical in young adult subjects. These gradually diminish as presbyopia is approached. The possible role of these refractive changes in causing visual difficulties for young drivers on the road at night is considered. It is concluded that high mesopic levels (about 1 cd/m2) of road luminance produced by street and vehicle lighting are normally too great to allow significant refractive shifts to occur, although acuity will be reduced due to light-dependent neural changes. myopia.abstract: Esophoria has been associated with onset and progression of myopia in children. The induction of myopia by optical defocus shown by animal models suggests that a high lag of accommodation during near work may contribute to myopia in children. This paper examines the relationship of nearpoint phoria and accommodative response in a sample of children with myopia. Accommodative response was measured under binocular conditions with the Canon Autoref R-1 autorefractor with a 40 cm viewing distance. Phorias were measured with the von Graefe method using a 40 cm test distance. In the statistical analysis exophoria was scored as a negative number and esophoria was scored as a positive number. myopia.abstract: It is well established that refractive development is regulated by visual feedback. However, most optical treatment strategies designed to reduce myopia progression have not produced the desired results, primarily because some of our assumptions concerning the operating characteristics of the vision-dependent mechanisms that regulate refractive development have been incorrect. In particular, because of the prominence of central vision in primates, it has generally been assumed that signals from the fovea determine the effects of vision on refractive development. However, experiments in laboratory animals demonstrate that ocular growth and emmetropization are mediated by local retinal mechanisms and that foveal vision is not essential for many vision-dependent aspects of refractive development. myopia.summary: Myopia is a significant public health problem and its prevalence may be increasing over time. The main treatment options of single vision spectacle lenses, contact lenses, and refractive surgery do not slow the accompanying eye growth or retard the physiological changes associated with excessive axial elongation. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a significant public health problem and its prevalence may be increasing over time. The main treatment options of single vision spectacle lenses, contact lenses, and refractive surgery do not slow the accompanying eye growth or retard the physiological changes associated with excessive axial elongation. High myopia is a predisposing factor for retinal detachment, myopic retinopathy, and glaucoma, contributing to loss of vision and blindness. The high prevalence of myopia and its prominence as a public health problem emphasize the importance of finding effective treatments that slow myopia progression and axial elongation. Treatments that have been investigated include various types of spectacle lenses and contact lenses, as well as pharmaceutical agents such as atropine and pirenzepine. myopia.abstract: The choroid of the eye is primarily a vascular structure supplying the outer retina. It has several unusual features: It contains large membrane-lined lacunae, which, at least in birds, function as part of the lymphatic drainage of the eye and which can change their volume dramatically, thereby changing the thickness of the choroid as much as four-fold over a few days (much less in primates). It contains non-vascular smooth muscle cells, especially behind the fovea, the contraction of which may thin the choroid, thereby opposing the thickening caused by expansion of the lacunae. It has intrinsic choroidal neurons, also mostly behind the central retina, which may control these muscles and may modulate choroidal blood flow as well. myopia.abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) was one of the biggest advances in ophthalmic imaging. Building on that platform, OCT angiography (OCTA) provides depth resolved images of blood flow in the retina and choroid with levels of detail far exceeding that obtained with older forms of imaging. This new modality is challenging because of the need for new equipment and processing techniques, current limitations of imaging capability, and rapid advancements in both imaging and in our understanding of the imaging and applicable pathophysiology of the retina and choroid. These factors lead to a steep learning curve, even for those with a working understanding dye-based ocular angiography. All for a method of imaging that is a little more than 10 years old. myopia.abstract: Purpose We provide a standardized set of terminology, definitions, and thresholds of myopia and its main ocular complications. Methods Critical review of current terminology and choice of myopia thresholds was done to ensure that the proposed standards are appropriate for clinical research purposes, relevant to the underlying biology of myopia, acceptable to researchers in the field, and useful for developing health policy. Results We recommend that the many descriptive terms of myopia be consolidated into the following descriptive categories: myopia, secondary myopia, axial myopia, and refractive myopia. To provide a framework for research into myopia prevention, the condition of "pre-myopia" is defined. myopia.title: A global perspective on hantavirus ecology, epidemiology, and disease
myopia.summary: Hantaviruses are enzootic viruses that maintain persistent infections in their rodent hosts without apparent disease symptoms. The spillover of these viruses to humans can lead to one of two serious illnesses, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. …
myopia.abstract: Hantaviruses are enzootic viruses that maintain persistent infections in their rodent hosts without apparent disease symptoms. The spillover of these viruses to humans can lead to one of two serious illnesses, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. In recent years, there has been an improved understanding of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and natural history of these viruses following an increase in the number of outbreaks in the Americas. In this review, current concepts regarding the ecology of and disease associated with these serious human pathogens are presented. Priorities for future research suggest an integration of the ecology and evolution of these and other host-virus ecosystems through modeling and hypothesis-driven research with the risk of emergence, host switching/spillover, and disease transmission to humans.

myopia.summary: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal dystrophy caused by the loss of photoreceptors and characterized by retinal pigment deposits visible on fundus examination. Prevalence of non syndromic RP is approximately 1/4,000. …
myopia.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal dystrophy caused by the loss of photoreceptors and characterized by retinal pigment deposits visible on fundus examination. Prevalence of non syndromic RP is approximately 1/4,000. The most common form of RP is a rod-cone dystrophy, in which the first symptom is night blindness, followed by the progressive loss in the peripheral visual field in daylight, and eventually leading to blindness after several decades. Some extreme cases may have a rapid evolution over two decades or a slow progression that never leads to blindness. In some cases, the clinical presentation is a cone-rod dystrophy, in which the decrease in visual acuity predominates over the visual field loss. myopia.title: Hantaviruses: a global disease problem
myopia.summary: Hantaviruses are carried by numerous rodent species throughout the world. In 1993, a previously unknown group of hantaviruses emerged in the United States as the cause of an acute respiratory disease now termed hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). …
myopia.abstract: Hantaviruses are carried by numerous rodent species throughout the world. In 1993, a previously unknown group of hantaviruses emerged in the United States as the cause of an acute respiratory disease now termed hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). Before than, hantaviruses were known as the etiologic agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, a disease that occurs almost entirely in the Eastern Hemisphere. Since the discovery of the HPS-causing hantaviruses, intense investigation of the ecology and epidemiology of hantaviruses has led to the discovery of many other novel hantaviruses. Their ubiquity and potential for causing severe human illness make these viruses an important public health concern; we reviewed the distribution, ecology, disease potential, and genetic spectrum.

myopia.summary: The history, taxonomy, geographic distribution, clinical disease, and therapy of the pathogenic nonpigmented or late-pigmenting rapidly growing mycobacteria (RGM) are reviewed. Community-acquired disease and health care-associated disease are highlighted for each species. …
myopia.abstract: The history, taxonomy, geographic distribution, clinical disease, and therapy of the pathogenic nonpigmented or late-pigmenting rapidly growing mycobacteria (RGM) are reviewed. Community-acquired disease and health care-associated disease are highlighted for each species. The latter grouping includes health care-associated outbreaks and pseudo-outbreaks as well as sporadic disease cases. Treatment recommendations for each species and type of disease are also described. Special emphasis is on the Mycobacterium fortuitum group, including M. fortuitum, M. peregrinum, and the unnamed third biovariant complex with its recent taxonomic changes and newly recognized species (including M. septicum, M. mageritense, and proposed species M. houstonense and M. bonickei). myopia.title: Ocular drug delivery systems: An overview
myopia.summary: The major challenge faced by today's pharmacologist and formulation scientist is ocular drug delivery. Topical eye drop is the most convenient and patient compliant route of drug administration, especially for the treatment of anterior segment diseases. …
myopia.abstract: The major challenge faced by today's pharmacologist and formulation scientist is ocular drug delivery. Topical eye drop is the most convenient and patient compliant route of drug administration, especially for the treatment of anterior segment diseases. Delivery of drugs to the targeted ocular tissues is restricted by various precorneal, dynamic and static ocular barriers. Also, therapeutic drug levels are not maintained for longer duration in target tissues. In the past two decades, ocular drug delivery research acceleratedly advanced towards developing a novel, safe and patient compliant formulation and drug delivery devices/techniques, which may surpass these barriers and maintain drug levels in tissues. contactlens.summary: Future studies should prioritize direct comparisons of novel platforms with standard therapy and establish whether improved delivery maintains concentrations above pathogen-specific inhibitory thresholds and translates into superior clinical outcomes.
contactlens.abstract: PURPOSE: Infectious keratitis remains a leading cause of corneal blindness worldwide despite effective antimicrobial agents. Conventional topical therapy is limited by rapid precorneal clearance, restricted corneal penetration, and inadequate stromal drug exposure, resulting in subtherapeutic drug concentrations. These pharmacokinetic barriers are particularly important in fungal, protozoal, deep stromal, and antimicrobial-resistant keratitis, where prolonged or targeted exposure is essential for successful treatment. This review evaluates emerging ocular antimicrobial delivery strategies through a pharmacokinetic framework, emphasizing the relationship among delivery platform, depth of corneal involvement, pathogen-specific requirements, and clinical feasibility. contactlens.abstract: We report the first case of confirmed Acanthamoeba-Cladosporium coinfection keratitis in a soft contact lens (CL) wearer without any history of ocular trauma, and to highlight its diagnostic and therapeutic implications. A healthy 23-year-old woman with a 10-year history of daily-disposable soft CL wear and no ocular trauma presented with 3 days of acute ocular pain and conjunctival injection in the right eye. Slit-lamp examination revealed a 2.0×2.0-mm paracentral corneal infiltrate with an irregular margin, mild corneal oedema, and an anterior chamber reaction. Corneal scraping with Gram staining demonstrated typical Acanthamoeba cysts, and Sabouraud dextrose agar culture with lactophenol cotton blue mounting confirmed Cladosporium species. contactlens.abstract: Micro- and nano-plastics (MNPs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants originating from the degradation of plastics and direct release from consumer products. Global plastic production is projected to nearly double by 2050, intensifying human exposure through inhalation, ingestion, and direct ocular contact. This review synthesizes current evidence on the presence, distribution, and health impacts of MNPs in human ocular tissues, their toxicological effects in animal and cellular models, underlying pathological mechanisms, and contributions from ophthalmic materials. contactlens.abstract: The ocular surface microenvironment (OSM), which is regulated by the lacrimal functional unit and the external environment, is highly dynamic and determines the health of the ocular surface (OS). In this review, we first highlight the importance of physiological parameters, namely, oxygen tension, osmolarity, and pH of the OSM on the health of the OS. The mechanisms leading to their imbalance and consequent dysfunctions of the ocular tissues are discussed next. Understanding the pathophysiology of these disorders for the development of treatment modalities requires tools for accurate, sensitive, and rapid measurement of the physiological parameters in a clinical setting. Fusarium and Aspergillus were the most common pathogens reported. Greater etiological diversity is reflected by increasing recognition of dematiaceous fungi, uncommon molds, and cryptic species. Additional relevant studies were identified by screening the reference lists of key publications. However, long-term surgical success is often limited by recurrent fibrosis from chronic inflammation. This narrative review examines the graft materials, surgical techniques, and medical management used in fornix reconstruction. Here, we establish an integrated engineering-characterization-function platform that quantitatively resolves buried nanocoatings and directly correlates their architecture with interfacial performance. Using silicone hydrogel contact lenses as a representative biomedical substrate, robust semi-interpenetrating polymer network (semi-IPN) nanocoatings are fabricated and characterized by gas cluster ion beam X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (GCIB-XPS), time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), and a newly developed atomic force microscopy (AFM) modulus-based algorithm. contactlens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ocular dryness and discomfort are commonly reported by contact lens wearers, particularly among young adults. This study evaluated self-reported ocular symptoms among Palestinian university students and compared contact lens users with nonusers. METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Palestinian university students using dry eye symptom (DES) items, the Contact Lens Dry Eye Questionnaire-8 (CLDEQ-8), and the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Descriptive, comparative, and multivariable analyses were performed to examine ocular symptoms and their associations with contact lens use and relevant participant characteristics. RESULTS: A total of 408 students participated, of whom 202 (49.5%) were contact lens users and 87.7% were female. contactlens.abstract: Chronic infectious keratitis represents a distinct clinical entity characterized by indolent progression, diagnostic difficulty, and prolonged therapeutic courses. Unlike acute bacterial keratitis, chronic infections often present with subtle inflammatory signs, recurrent episodes, or poor response to empirical antimicrobial therapy. Among the most important causes are herpetic keratitis, acanthamoeba keratitis, Microsporidial stromal keratitis, and atypical (non-tuberculous) mycobacterial keratitis. Herpes simplex virus keratitis may manifest as recurrent epithelial disease or immune-mediated stromal inflammation resulting from viral latency and reactivation, frequently leading to corneal scarring and neurotrophic complications. contactlens.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the immediate visual correction provided by scleral lens insertion and short-term changes in ocular surface parameters associated with one month of scleral lens wear in patients with keratoconus in Saudi Arabia. METHODS: This prospective observational study included 18 participants with keratoconus (18 study eyes). Scleral lenses were fitted bilaterally, while one eye per participant was selected for ocular analysis; when both eyes were eligible, the eye with the higher Kmax was selected. Participants were instructed to wear ONEFIT MED® scleral lenses for at least 8 h per day for one month. Outcomes included logMAR visual acuity, Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), Schirmer I test, and invasive tear break-up time (ITBUT). Paired-samples t-tests were used for paired comparisons. contactlens.abstract: Background: Moderate-to-high refractive error generates long-term direct and indirect costs through corrective devices, complications, and productivity losses. The economic value of implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery relative to contact lens (CL)-based correction with backup spectacles remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the 25-year cost-effectiveness of posterior chamber phakic ICL implantation versus CL-based correction across four refractive subgroups from a Norwegian societal perspective. Methods: A Markov cohort model followed patients aged 25-50 years with high myopia, high myopia with astigmatism, high hyperopia, or high hyperopia with astigmatism. Health states incorporated surgical complications, microbial keratitis (MK), cataract, explantation, and death. contactlens.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) released from contact lenses during wear can persistently contact the ocular surface through tear circulation, thereby posing a threat to ocular health. Combining thermal analysis with mass spectrometry enables accurate quantitative detection of low-concentration MPs from contact lenses, supporting exposure risk assessment. In this study, a hyphenated device consisting of a mini-pyrolyzer and a time-of-flight mass spectrometer (Py-TOFMS) was developed to enable rapid quantitative detection of MPs released from contact lenses. Compared with conventional Py-GC/MS, which typically requires approximately 30 min per sample, the proposed Py-TOFMS method eliminates the GC separation step and completes the analysis in 15 min, thereby simplifying the detection workflow and reducing the risk of sample loss and contamination. contactlens.title: Comparison of the Influence of Two Types of Silicone Hydrogel Daily Disposable Contact Lenses on Clinical Signs of Allergic Conjunctivitis Symptoms.
contactlens.summary: These findings suggest that verofilcon A may be associated with more favorable clinical signs of allergic conjunctivitis than narafilcon A in CL wearers with CL discomfort.
contactlens.abstract: PURPOSE: Contact lens (CL) wear can exacerbate allergic conjunctivitis. This study compared the effects of narafilcon A and verofilcon A on clinical signs of allergic conjunctivitis in CL wearers. Our previous studies using the same crossover cohort examined subjective CL comfort and related symptoms and tear-film stability and surface wettability. In contrast, the present study specifically evaluated objective clinical signs of allergic conjunctivitis, which were not the primary outcomes of those previous studies. METHODS: The study included 62 CL wearers, comprising 124 eyes, who experienced CL discomfort. Participants were randomized to a cross-over design, wearing narafilcon A and verofilcon A each for 2 weeks. contactlens.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the effect of anti-inflammatory drug classes, delivery methods, and personalized regimens on ocular surface health in dry eye patients, providing evidence-based support for optimizing medication regimens. METHOD: We systematically reviewed 127 studies (2013-2023; 368 datasets). Multiple linear regression analyzed tear film breakup time (TBUT) predictors. Four pharmacokinetic models (zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, Ritger-Peppas) fitted drug release; robustness and subtype heterogeneity were evaluated. contactlens.summary: Both lenses showed high and comparable clinical and subjective performance over one week. While minor statistical differences were observed, none were clinically meaningful, indicating similar performance across handling, fit, vision, tear stability, and wearer-reported outcomes.
contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical performance and wearer experience of two contemporary spherical daily disposable silicone hydrogel lenses, somofilcon A and verofilcon A. METHODS: In this prospective, double-masked, bilateral, randomized, crossover study, habitual contact lens wearers were recruited at a single site. Participants wore somofilcon A or verofilcon A lenses bilaterally on a daily disposable basis for one week, then crossed over to the alternate lens. The primary endpoint was participant-reported handling (insertion and removal) at the 1-week follow-up. Secondary outcomes included lens fit, surface wettability and deposits, non-invasive tear break-up time (NITBUT), visual acuity, subjective comfort, satisfaction, preference, diary ratings, and slit-lamp ocular health. METHODS: Test lenses were exposed to an artificial tear solution to simulate in vitro deposition.
