contactlens.title: Challenges of Scleral Lens Practice in Yemen: Insights from a Tertiary Referral Eye Center in Sana'a.
contactlens.summary: While scleral lenses provide effective visual rehabilitation and excellent wearing comfort for patients with complex ocular surface diseases and irregular corneas, evidence regarding their delivery in resource-limited settings remains scarce. …
contactlens.abstract: While scleral lenses provide effective visual rehabilitation and excellent wearing comfort for patients with complex ocular surface diseases and irregular corneas, evidence regarding their delivery in resource-limited settings remains scarce. This narrative commentary highlights the major challenges of establishing and maintaining scleral lens services in Yemen, based primarily on clinical experience at a tertiary eye center in Sana'a. In our setting, healthcare infrastructure, supply chains, and access to specialized eye care are compromised. Here, we discuss the impact of financial constraints, restricted access to advanced fitting technologies, interrupted supply chains, misconceptions, and lack of patient awareness, as well as the difficulties in ensuring continuity of care and long-term follow-up. contactlens.title: Recent Advances in Ophthalmic Drug Delivery: Current Status and Future Perspectives.
contactlens.summary: Vision impairment is a significant global health issue, affecting people of all ages and notably influencing quality of life. One of the major challenges in treating eye diseases is the effective delivery of drugs, as the eye possesses unique anatomical and physiological barriers. …
contactlens.abstract: Vision impairment is a significant global health issue, affecting people of all ages and notably influencing quality of life. One of the major challenges in treating eye diseases is the effective delivery of drugs, as the eye possesses unique anatomical and physiological barriers. Structures such as tear drainage, the tightly packed corneal epithelium, and the blood‑ocular barriers often hinder medications from reaching therapeutic concentrations. Conventional treatments such as eye drops, ointments, and oral medications frequently exhibit poor bioavailability and limited penetration into target sites, particularly in posterior segment diseases. This often leads to minimal therapeutic relief or requires frequent dosing, which can compromise patient comfort and adherence. contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the impact of subacute preservative-containing eye drop usage on the ocular surface and to observe the clinical progression and management of medication-induced persistent corneal epithelial defects (MI-PCED). METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated 60 cases (60 eyes) diagnosed with MI-PCED from January 2020 to January 2024. Data on the type, frequency, and duration of topical medication usage were collected. A multidisciplinary pharmacovigilance assessment evaluated causality, severity, and preventability of the adverse events. Upon diagnosis, the offending medications were discontinued and replaced with low-toxicity, preservative-free alternatives. contactlens.abstract: A 14-year-old female patient presented to the Department of Ophthalmology, the First Affiliated Hospital of Xiangnan University with a 3-year history of blurred vision while wearing single-vision spectacles for bilateral myopia. The patient demonstrated satisfactory corrected visual acuity, rapid myopia progression, no manifest strabismus, and well-preserved fusional function and stereopsis; therefore, orthokeratology was administered. Grade 2 central corneal staining developed at one month. Lens parameters were adjusted to optimize the fitting: the power of the alignment curve was reduced by 0.25 D, the toricity was increased, the sagittal depth of the reverse curve was raised by 20 μm, and the peripheral curve was upgraded by one step. contactlens.abstract: Müller muscle-conjunctival resection (MMCR) has traditionally been regarded as a posterior approach for mild-to-moderate blepharoptosis in patients with good levator function and a positive response to phenylephrine. Its contemporary role, however, is considerably broader. Accumulating evidence supports the use of MMCR in selected patients with limited or absent phenylephrine responsiveness, more severe ptosis, postoperative eyelid asymmetry, and carefully chosen congenital, neurogenic, or neuromuscular forms of ptosis. In parallel, modifications that incorporate tarsectomy, simplified suturing, conjunctiva-sparing approaches, perioperative bandage contact lenses, and targeted hemostatic maneuvers have sought to improve predictability, comfort, and safety. Despite extensive investigations - including conventional cultures, impression cytology, in vivo imaging, and repeated targeted PCR from corneal and aqueous samples - the aetiology remained unclear, with all tests persistently negative. Progressive inflammation, enlarging hypopyon, stromal melt and rising intraocular pressure necessitated anterior chamber (AC) washout followed by therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty with extracapsular cataract extraction. contactlens.summary: Paediatric IK represents an important ocular morbidity in the UK. Contact lens wear was the most common risk factor and was strongly associated with P. aeruginosa infection, highlighting the need for improved awareness, education, and prevention. …
contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterise the clinical features, microbiological profiles, and outcomes of paediatric infectious keratitis (IK). METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included paediatric patients (≤18 years old) who presented with presumed IK and underwent corneal sampling at two UK tertiary ophthalmic centres. RESULTS: We included 42 cases in this study; median age was 13.3 years (IQR 10.1-16.1). Contact lens wear (15, 35.7%) and ocular surface disease (15, 35.7%) were the most common risk factors. Twenty-five (59.5%) cases were microbiologically positive (MP), with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (5, 16.1%), Staphylococcus aureus (5, 16.1%), and Serratia marcescens (5, 16.1%) being the most commonly isolated bacteria. contactlens.summary: Among students who participated in screening at two secondary schools, a small subgroup had pinhole-improvable reduced distance visual acuity suggestive of an uncorrected refractive component. …
contactlens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Uncorrected refractive error (URE) is a primary cause of visual impairment (VI). Although URE causes VI and increases the risk of amblyopia in school-going children, no studies have examined barriers to uptake of refractive eye-care services among secondary school students in Uganda. This study reports the perceived reasons for the poor uptake of refractive eye care services among students at two secondary schools in Kampala, Uganda. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in two secondary schools in Kampala between March 2019 and April 2019. Students' presenting distance visual acuities (DVA) were measured. Participants with a DVA worse than 6/9 were reassessed using a pinhole. Those not using spectacles or contact lenses who had pinhole-improvable reduced distance visual acuity suggestive of uncorrected refractive error were administered a structured questionnaire.

contactlens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The healthy ocular surface microbiome consists of Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria, and Firmicutes phyla, with Corynebacterium, Propionibacterium, and Staphylococcus as dominant genera. This microbial environment is essential for maintaining immune homeostasis and barrier integrity. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize existing evidence on how periocular skincare and cosmetic products affect the ocular surface microbiome, tear film stability, and downstream ocular surface disease. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus using Boolean MeSH term strategies. Studies from 2010 to present evaluating microbial composition of the ocular surface and the effects of exogenous exposures (cosmetics, contact lenses, medications) were included. contactlens.abstract: Extreme early-onset axial myopia causes profound refractive disability and lifelong vitreoretinal vulnerability. We report approximately 20 years of follow-up in a woman with bilateral myopia of -8.00 diopters (D) at 1 year of age, axial lengths exceeding 30 mm at 6 years and 35 mm before adulthood. At 18 years, severe spectacle-related minification, peripheral distortion, and inconvenience persisted. After discussion of contact lenses, phakic intraocular lenses, and refractive lens exchange, she chose sequential bilateral refractive lens exchange with toric intraocular lenses and a residual myopic target of approximately -4.50 D. contactlens.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding contact lens-associated dry eye among contact lens wearers: a cross-sectional study.
contactlens.summary: Contact lens wearers demonstrated a moderate level of KAP related to CLADE. These results underscore the importance of enhanced education to promote positive attitudes and behavioral change. Future public health campaigns and clinical counseling should emphasize systematic education to improve CLADE-related knowledge and self-management.
contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Contact lens use is a significant modifiable risk factor for contact lens-associated dry eye (CLADE), a distinct and prevalent subtype of dry eye disease. This study aimed to describe CLADE symptoms using the 8-item Contact Lens Dry Eye Questionnaire (CLDEQ-8) and to quantify knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding CLADE. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in China between March 20 and May 22, 2025, among contact lens users. Participants completed two independent instruments: the CLDEQ-8 (symptom frequency and intensity; not a KAP scale) and a 25-item CLADE KAP questionnaire (knowledge 0-20, attitude 7-35, and practice 8-40). contactlens.summary: Background: Sjögren's disease (SjD) causes severe ocular surface desiccation, progressing from aqueous-deficient dry eye (ADDE) to vision-threatening corneal ulceration, stromal melting, and perforation. Recent consensus guidelines and therapeutic innovations have transformed ophthalmic diagnosis and management. …
contactlens.abstract: Background: Sjögren's disease (SjD) causes severe ocular surface desiccation, progressing from aqueous-deficient dry eye (ADDE) to vision-threatening corneal ulceration, stromal melting, and perforation. Recent consensus guidelines and therapeutic innovations have transformed ophthalmic diagnosis and management. Methods: A comprehensive narrative overview of PubMed and Google Scholar (July 2016-July2026) was conducted to evaluate updates in SjD diagnostics, ocular surface mechanics, topical/biological pharmacotherapies, neurostimulation, and meibomian gland interventions. Results: Diagnostic parameters have shifted towards non-invasive salivary metabolomics (lactate, alanine, malate), regulatory non-coding RNAs (H19 ICR hypomethylation), tear point-of-care MMP-9 testing, and salivary gland ultrasonography (SGUS). contactlens.summary: Isotretinoin is a highly effective treatment for moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris but is associated with a broad spectrum of ophthalmic adverse effects. While dry eye disease secondary to meibomian gland dysfunction is the most common ocular complication, less familiar manifestations include nyctalopia, corneal abnormalities, retinal chan …
contactlens.abstract: Isotretinoin is a highly effective treatment for moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris but is associated with a broad spectrum of ophthalmic adverse effects. While dry eye disease secondary to meibomian gland dysfunction is the most common ocular complication, less familiar manifestations include nyctalopia, corneal abnormalities, retinal changes, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, and optic neuritis. Current evidence suggests that isotretinoin induces structural and functional changes in the meibomian glands, resulting in tear film instability and evaporative dry eye disease. Although many of these changes appear reversible following treatment cessation, some patients may experience persistent symptoms. Methods: Nationwide cross-sectional survey with the participation of 100 ophthalmologists, including 50 ophthalmologists in emergency care and 50 ocular surface specialists. The study questionnaire assessed diagnostic approaches, treatment strategies, and factors influencing therapeutic decision making. A secondary objective was to evaluate the influence of CL-SAG measured at the ISO reference temperature (20 °C) and physiological ocular temperature (34 °C) on δ-sag-based fitting outcomes. METHODS: A prospective cohort study included 86 eyes of young adults (21.4 ± 1.9 years). In randomized, double-masked sessions, five hydrogel lenses with different CL-SAG values were fitted. contactlens.title: Contact lens-associated infectious keratitis in physicians: a retrospective observational study.
contactlens.summary: Physicians with contact lens-associated infectious keratitis may exhibit modifiable behavioral risk factors and occupation-related conditions relevant to disease presentation. …
contactlens.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the clinical spectrum, contact lens-related behaviors, occupation-related characteristics, and outcomes of physicians with contact lens-associated infectious keratitis. METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary referral center (Ege University, Department of Ophthalmology, Izmir, Turkiye) and included physicians diagnosed with contact lens-associated infectious keratitis between November 2012 and March 2026. Medical records were reviewed for demographic, occupational, contact lens-related, ocular surface, and clinical data. RESULTS: Eleven physicians (mean age 44.4 ± 16.3 years [range, 27-72]; 63.6% female) were included. Bacterial keratitis was diagnosed in 7 patients (63.6%), Acanthamoeba keratitis in 3 patients (27.3%), and fungal keratitis in 1 patient (9.1%). contactlens.abstract: Fungal keratitis, or keratomycoses, are corneal infections which must be considered in cases of corneal trauma, prior corneal surgery, chronic ocular surface disease, topical corticosteroids or contact lens wear. Filamentous fungi or yeasts may be involved. Presenting clinical features such as corneal infiltrates with feathery edges and/or raised surface, intact epithelium with deep stromal involvement, satellite lesions, endothelial plaques, lack of improvement with antibiotics and worsening with steroids are suggestive of fungal keratitis. Corneal scraping for laboratory examination is mandatory. Medical management with antifungal eye drops and systemic agents should be started as soon as possible. Surgical interventions are required in a significant number of cases to control the infection. The prognosis of fungal keratitis is worse than that of bacterial keratitis.

contactlens.abstract: Nowadays, keratitis, corneal infection due to wearing contact lens means an increasingly serious problem. Neglected cases may lead to corneal damage that can cause blindness in cases of otherwise healthy eyes. Early diagnosis based on the clinical picture and the typical patient history is an important way of prevention. Prophylaxis is substantial to avoid bacterial and viral infection that is highly essential in this group of diseases. Teaching contact lens wearers the proper contact lens care, storage, sterility, and hygiene regulations is of great importance. In case of corneal inflammation early accurate diagnosis supported by microbiological culture from contact lenses, storage boxes or cornea is very useful. Thereafter, targeted drug therapy or in therapy-resistant cases surgical treatment may even be necessary in order to sustain suitable visual acuity.

contactlens.abstract: "Red eye" is used as a general term to describe irritated or bloodshot eyes. It is a recognizable sign of an acute/chronic, localized/systemic underlying inflammatory condition. Conjunctival injection is most commonly caused by dryness, allergy, visual fatigue, contact lens overwear, and local infections. In some instances, red eye can represent a true ocular emergency that should be treated by an ophthalmologist. A comprehensive assessment of red eye conditions is required to preserve the patients visual function. Severe ocular pain, significant photophobia, decreased vision, and history of ocular trauma are warning signs demanding immediate ophthalmological consultation.

contactlens.abstract: Hyaluronan (HA) is a hydrophilic biopolymer that has been explored as a wetting agent in contact lens applications. In this study, HA was modified with siloxy or polyethylene glycol moieties using click chemistry to make it more soluble in monomer solutions used to synthesize model contact lens materials; unmodified HA was not soluble in the same monomer solutions. The water contents of the silicone hydrogels were not increased by the presence of modified HA, nor was there a decrease in the surface contact angle. However, modified HA did lead to a reduction in lysozyme adsorption in some cases. The leaching rate of HA modified with polyethylene glycol from a 78:22 DMA:TRIS(OH) hydrogel was significantly slower than for unmodified HA.

A great challenge in using contact lenses for drug delivery is to achieve a prolonged drug release profile within the therapeutic range for various eye-related problems and diseases. In general, desired release kinetics to avoid the initial burst release is the zero-order kinetics within the therapeutic range. contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantify tear elimination rate (ER) underneath silicone hydrogel (Si-Hy) and scleral gas permeable (GP) contact lenses (CLs). METHODS: Subjects successfully using either well-fitting soft Si-Hy CLs or scleral GP CLs were recruited. Most scleral GP CL wearers had irregular corneas (e.g., keratoconus). An objective fluorometer measured decay of fluorescein isothiocyanate dextran dye signal (70 kD MW) from which the tear ER in %/min was calculated. For GP scleral lenses, the ER was determined for both the initial settling period and the 30- to 60-min period, and without lenses. All ERs were calculated from 5 to 30 min to avoid reflex tearing effects. RESULTS: Fourteen soft Si-Hy CL and 12 scleral GP CL wearers completed the study. The ER for the scleral GP CL wearers averaged 0.57 (±0.6) %/min for the 0- to 30-min and 0.42 (±0.5) %/min for the 30- to 60-min period (P=0.515).

contactlens.abstract: Acanthamoeba keratitis (AK) is a rare protozoal infection of the cornea. At least eight species of Acanthamoeba are known to cause this sight-threatening disease of the ocular surface. Acanthamoeba spp. exist in a wide array of niches ranging from thermal springs to under ice and every conceivable habitat in between. Contact lens wear is the leading risk factor for AK and is practiced by over 30 million individuals in the United States, yet the incidence of AK is less than 33 cases per one million contact lens wearers. Serological studies have reported that 90%-100% of individuals with no history of AK possess antibodies specific for Acanthamoeba antigens indicating that exposure to this organism is commonplace, yet disease is remarkably rare. contactlens.abstract: The occurrence of Acanthamoeba keratitis is increasing in the United States because of an expanding population at risk of infection and sporadic outbreaks of infection. Such outbreaks are the result of lapses in contact lens wear and care and of alterations in water quality and water treatment procedures. Although improved techniques in diagnosis are available, better identification of infection alone does not explain an increase in the observed occurrence of the disease. Likewise, there does not appear to be an increase in the virulence or infectivity of the amoebae. Strategies for prevention, including patient education, improved decontaminating agents, maintenance of water treatment standards, and possible immunization of subjects at risk, are needed.

RESULTS: High Dk silicone hydrogel contact lenses became available for research and clinical practice almost 10 and 5 years ago respectively. During that time many studies have been conducted and it has been demonstrated repeatedly how much improvement there has been to the physiological response of the eye particularly when wearing the lenses on an overnight basis. CONCLUSIONS: Although silicone hydrogels only constitute about 2% of current wearers, their positive effects on the eye compared with low Dk hydrogel lenses should make them the most dominant lenses in the near future.

contactlens.abstract: For 30 years, contact lens research focused on the need for highly oxygen-permeable (Dk) soft lens materials. High Dk silicone hydrogel contact lenses, made available in 1999, met this need. The purpose of this review is to examine how silicone hydrogel lens wear affects the ocular surfaces and to highlight areas in which further research is needed to improve biocompatibility. Silicone hydrogel lenses have eliminated lens-induced hypoxia for the majority of wearers and have a less pronounced effect on corneal homeostasis compared to other lens types; however, mechanical interaction with ocular tissue and the effects on tear film structure and physiology are similar to that found with soft lens wear in general. With a worldwide resurgence of contact lens-related disease, this report illustrates the clinical characteristics and treatment challenges representative of this disease. This report describes Acanthamoeba keratitis in a 47-year-old female using extended wear silicone hydrogel contact lenses, with a history of swimming in a home pool and failure to subsequently disinfect the contact lenses. The diagnosis was based on clinical signs, disease course, and confocal microscopy results despite a negative result for corneal smear and culture. The corneal signs included an epithelial defect, epithelial irregularities, anterior stromal infiltrates, perineural infiltrates, an anterior stromal ring infiltrate, and hypopyon. contactlens.abstract: Though biofilms were first described by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, the theory describing the biofilm process was not developed until 1978. We now understand that biofilms are universal, occurring in aquatic and industrial water systems as well as a large number of environments and medical devices relevant for public health. Using tools such as the scanning electron microscope and, more recently, the confocal laser scanning microscope, biofilm researchers now understand that biofilms are not unstructured, homogeneous deposits of cells and accumulated slime, but complex communities of surface-associated cells enclosed in a polymer matrix containing open water channels. Further studies have shown that the biofilm phenotype can be described in terms of the genes expressed by biofilm-associated cells. contactlens.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are of concern because of their high persistence (or that of their degradation products) and their impacts on human and environmental health that are known or can be deduced from some well-studied PFAS. Currently, many different PFAS (on the order of several thousands) are used in a wide range of applications, and there is no comprehensive source of information on the many individual substances and their functions in different applications. Here we provide a broad overview of many use categories where PFAS have been employed and for which function; we also specify which PFAS have been used and discuss the magnitude of the uses. Despite being non-exhaustive, our study clearly demonstrates that PFAS are used in almost all industry branches and many consumer products. In total, more than 200 use categories and subcategories are identified for more

contactlens.title: Strategies for combating bacterial biofilms: A focus on anti-biofilm agents and their mechanisms of action
contactlens.summary: Biofilm refers to the complex, sessile communities of microbes found either attached to a surface or buried firmly in an extracellular matrix as aggregates. The biofilm matrix surrounding bacteria makes them tolerant to harsh conditions and resistant to antibacterial treatments. …
contactlens.abstract: Biofilm refers to the complex, sessile communities of microbes found either attached to a surface or buried firmly in an extracellular matrix as aggregates. The biofilm matrix surrounding bacteria makes them tolerant to harsh conditions and resistant to antibacterial treatments. Moreover, the biofilms are responsible for causing a broad range of chronic diseases and due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance in bacteria it has really become difficult to treat them with efficacy. Furthermore, the antibiotics available till date are ineffective for treating these biofilm related infections due to their higher values of minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), which may result in in-vivo toxicity. Hence, it is critically important to design or screen anti-biofilm molecules that can effectively minimize and eradicate biofilm related infections.

contactlens.abstract: This review presents the past and current efforts with a brief description on the featured properties of hydrogel membranes fabricated from biopolymers and synthetic ones for wound dressing applications. Many endeavors have been exerted during past ten years for developing new artificial polymeric membranes, which fulfill the demanded conditions for the treatment of skin wounds. This review mainly focuses on representing specifications of ideal polymeric wound dressing membranes, such as crosslinked hydrogels compatible with wound dressing purposes. But as the hydrogels with single component have low mechanical strength, recent trends have offered composite or hybrid hydrogel membranes to achieve the typical wound dressing requirements.

contactlens.abstract: Microorganisms commonly attach to living and nonliving surfaces, including those of indwelling medical devices, and form biofilms made up of extracellular polymers. In this state, microorganisms are highly resistant to antimicrobial treatment and are tenaciously bound to the surface. To better understand and control biofilms on indwelling medical devices, researchers should develop reliable sampling and measurement techniques, investigate the role of biofilms in antimicrobial drug resistance, and establish the link between biofilm contamination and patient infection.

contactlens.abstract: In humans, microbial cells (including bacteria, archaea, and fungi) greatly outnumber host cells. Candida albicans is the most prevalent fungal species of the human microbiota; this species asymptomatically colonizes many areas of the body, particularly the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts of healthy individuals. Alterations in host immunity, stress, resident microbiota, and other factors can lead to C. albicans overgrowth, causing a wide range of infections, from superficial mucosal to hematogenously disseminated candidiasis. To date, most studies of C. albicans have been carried out in suspension cultures; however, the medical impact of C. albicans (like that of many other microorganisms) depends on its ability to thrive as a biofilm, a closely packed community of cells. contactlens.summary: The members of the Tear Film Subcommittee reviewed the role of the tear film in dry eye disease (DED). The Subcommittee reviewed biophysical and biochemical aspects of tears and how these change in DED. …
contactlens.abstract: The members of the Tear Film Subcommittee reviewed the role of the tear film in dry eye disease (DED). The Subcommittee reviewed biophysical and biochemical aspects of tears and how these change in DED. Clinically, DED is characterized by loss of tear volume, more rapid breakup of the tear film and increased evaporation of tears from the ocular surface. The tear film is composed of many substances including lipids, proteins, mucins and electrolytes. All of these contribute to the integrity of the tear film but exactly how they interact is still an area of active research. Tear film osmolarity increases in DED. Changes to other components such as proteins and mucins can be used as biomarkers for DED. contactlens.title: Bacterial biofilm formation on implantable devices and approaches to its treatment and prevention
contactlens.summary: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. …
contactlens.abstract: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. Due to the antibiotic-resistant nature of biofilms, the use of antibiotics alone is ineffective for treating biofilm-related infections. In this review, we present a brief overview of concepts of bacterial biofilm formation, and current state-of-the-art therapeutic approaches for preventing and treating biofilms. Also, we have reviewed the prevalence of such infections on medical devices and discussed the future challenges that need to be overcome in order to successfully treat biofilms using the novel technologies being developed.

contactlens.title: Hydrogels: Properties and Applications in Biomedicine
contactlens.summary: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. …
contactlens.abstract: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. Research in recent years shows that hydrogels have been applied in various fields, such as agriculture, biomaterials, the food industry, drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Along with the underlying technology improvements of hydrogel development, hydrogels can be expected to be applied in more fields. contactlens.title: Wearable sensors: modalities, challenges, and prospects
contactlens.summary: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. …
contactlens.abstract: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. This adaptation has involved innovations in how to miniaturize sensing technologies, how to make them conformal and flexible, and in the development of companion software that increases the value of the measured data. However, chemical sensing modalities have experienced greater challenges in commercial adoption, especially for non-invasive chemical sensors. There have also been significant challenges in making significant fundamental improvements to existing mechanical, electrical, and optical sensing modalities, especially in improving their specificity of detection. lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopia is a worldwide health concern due to its increasing prevalence and associated pathology, visual dysfunction, societal and quality of life impacts. Despite widespread use of atropine in Taiwan to manage myopia, its prevalence has increased. It has been suggested that the efficacy of atropine in slowing myopia progression may be limited by binocular vision (BV) function. Furthermore, the long-term impacts of atropine are unknown. This study aimed to contrast the BV profile of young myopic adults following cessation of atropine therapy for myopia control, relative to myopic adults without this history. METHODS: From a pool of young myopic adults attending a vision screening (n = 1320), 204 myopic (≤-0.50 dioptres, D) adults were invited for further clinical evaluation. lens.title: Archetypal analysis of visual field patterns in an African population: a data-driven approach.
lens.summary: Archetypal analysis facilitates objective, data-driven extraction of prototypical VF patterns. Comparison with a North American HFA dataset showed substantial overlap (13/16 archetypes at cosine similarity > 0.7), alongside distinct differences that should be interpreted cautiously given differences in age distribution, referral character …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Visual field (VF) testing is essential for the evaluation of glaucoma, neurological, and retinal diseases. Interpretation, however, is subject to interindividual variability. Archetypal analysis, a type of machine learning, enables quantitative characterization of VFs. While prior studies have focused on predominantly Caucasian populations, no comparable investigation exists for an African population. METHODS: We conducted an archetypal analysis of 8,766 VF measurements obtained with a Humphrey field analyzer (HFA) from 4,096 patients attending an ophthalmic imaging referral center in Kumasi, Ghana. Patients were referred for glaucoma, neuro-ophthalmic, retinal, or other perimetry-requiring examinations. Measurements with > 33% fixation losses or > 15% false-positive rates were excluded. lens.title: A Metadynamics-Based Protocol for Sampling and Scoring Peptide Nanofibril Conformations.
lens.summary: The morphology of a cross-β nanofibril, ranging from ribbon to rod conformations, is commonly determined by the amino acid sequence of its constituent peptides in addition to environmental factors such as pH and salt concentration. …
lens.abstract: The morphology of a cross-β nanofibril, ranging from ribbon to rod conformations, is commonly determined by the amino acid sequence of its constituent peptides in addition to environmental factors such as pH and salt concentration. The use of all-atom molecular dynamics simulation of a given peptide nanofibril to explore its energetically favorable fibril conformations is a desirable but challenging goal, due to potential trapping in local energy minima. In this work, we explore a metadynamics-based approach to investigate morphologically distinct peptide nanofibrils, introducing collective variables based on supramolecular twist as a sampling coordinate. lens.title: Genetic Variants in Ciliary Body Development Genes and Their Association with Myopia: A Systematic Review.
lens.summary: Genetic variants identified in observational studies were distinct from those identified in GWAS and GWAS meta-analyses, which frequently examined overlapping cohorts. Further studies are required to validate these associations and clarify whether these variants influence myopia risk through an underlying mechanism involving ciliary muscl …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Numerous genetic variants have been implicated in myopia pathogenesis, yet their biological mechanisms remain unclear. One proposed mechanism is that variants in genes involved in ciliary body development may influence ciliary muscle structure and accommodative function, thereby influencing individual variation in myopia risk. The aim was to systematically evaluate published evidence linking myopia with genetic variants in genes implicated in ciliary body developmental pathways and identify candidate variants for comparison with ciliary muscle properties to validate this mechanistic pathway. METHODS: A comprehensive search of existing literature was conducted across PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, and Scopus on July 2 2025 and February 25 2026. lens.title: Revealing the benefit of eye motion for acuity under emulated cone loss.
lens.summary: Retinal degenerative diseases progressively erode the cone photoreceptor mosaic, reducing the retina's spatial sampling power, yet visual acuity is remarkably resilient to cone loss. …
lens.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases progressively erode the cone photoreceptor mosaic, reducing the retina's spatial sampling power, yet visual acuity is remarkably resilient to cone loss. Prior work has shown that clinically normal visual acuity (20/25 or better) can persist despite up to 50% of cone cells being lost (Ratnam et al., 2013; Foote et al., 2018). However, studies on individuals with retinal degeneration cannot control for patients' stage of disease progression, creating the need for an experimental paradigm that can mimic these diseases in healthy subjects. The Oz Vision system creates visual percepts through programmable, per-cell stimulation of thousands of cone cells. We reprogram this system to emulate cone loss in healthy eyes by withholding stimulation from a subset of randomly selected cones, rendering them inactive, in a method we term 'cone dropout'. lens.title: Endothelin 2-Mediated Neuroinflammation Drives Hypertensive Retinal Dysfunction.
lens.summary: Our findings establish endothelin 2 as an important, intraocular pressure-independent contributing factor to hypertension-associated retinal neurodegeneration and identify the endothelin-endothelin receptor type A axis as a potential therapeutic target to prevent vision loss in patients with hypertension.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a risk factor for glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, yet the mechanistic basis connecting the 2 conditions remains elusive. METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role. RESULTS: Hypertensive rats develop accelerated retinal degeneration marked by retinal thinning, functional impairment, reduced perfusion, and progressive neuroinflammation. lens.title: A Physiological Optics Characterization of the Bagolini bar for Testing Density of Suppression.
lens.summary: The 16 filters do not provide a uniformly graded progression of optical attenuation. The measured spectral and photometric transitions provide an optical basis for testable hypotheses concerning non-uniform perceptual responses, but their clinical consequences require psychophysical and clinical validation.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the spectral and photometric properties of the 16 filters of a commercial Bagolini bar and to determine whether successive filter numbers correspond to a uniform progression of spectral attenuation, illuminance, and interocular contrast. METHODS: An instrumental spectrophotometric characterization of the 16 filters of a commercial Bagolini bar was performed. Spectral measurements were acquired over the 320-810 nm instrumental range, with the 380-780 nm visible range used for the principal spectral analysis. RESULTS: Spectrophotometric analysis demonstrated non-linear, step-wise changes in the optical properties of successive Bagolini filters. The transmission spectrum peak with increasing filter number shifted from approximately 610 nm to 770 nm. lens.title: Computer vision syndrome among high school students using digital versus printed textbooks: prevalence and associated factors.
lens.summary: CVS prevalence was similar among students using digital and printed textbooks, and this pattern remained after adjustment for relevant covariates. However, appropriate optical compensation should be used when necessary to prevent an increase.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The increasing implementation of digital textbooks in schools raises concerns regarding their potential impact on the ocular and visual health of adolescents. However, the effect of this educational shift on computer vision syndrome (CVS) has not yet been assessed using validated measurement tools. OBJECTIVE: This study analyses the prevalence of CVS in adolescent students, comparing the use of printed versus digital textbooks, and considering sociodemographic, visual and digital devices exposure factors. METHODS: A longitudinal observational study with repeated assessments of the same participants and estimation of CVS at four time points was conducted during the second academic semester in two high schools in Alicante, Spain (n = 231 students, 15-17 years old). Causative factors and outcomes of pyogenic granulomas presenting to a hospital eye clinic.
lens.summary: Most ocular pyogenic granulomas can be safely managed in primary care. Given their expertise in slit-lamp differential diagnosis and intraocular pressure monitoring, community optometrists are ideally positioned to initiate first-line topical steroid therapy, reserving surgical referral for recalcitrant lesions. …
lens.abstract: CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Ocular pyogenic granulomas are benign vascular lesions that can be highly responsive to topical therapy in community optometry settings, helping to reduce unnecessary burden on tertiary eye care services. BACKGROUND: While their rapid onset and vascular appearance can be clinically alarming, the management of pyogenic granuloma primarily involves topical pharmaceuticals well suited to community-based care. This study analyses a 15-year cohort to establish the efficacy of topical management and define clear criteria for surgical referral. METHODS: A retrospective audit was performed on 49 cases of ocular pyogenic granuloma presenting to a hospital-based acute eye clinic between 2009 and 2024. lens.title: Accommodative balance in clinical versus metric-optimised prescriptions for adults with Down syndrome.
lens.summary: Inter-eye differences in VA and accommodative lag were not clinically meaningfully different for any experimental refraction, indicating each refraction was similarly balanced.
lens.abstract: CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Wavefront-guided objective refractions can be a useful tool for optimising refractions for patients who may have difficulties with subjective refraction. Since these objective refractions are monocularly derived, information about the binocular balance to accommodation is important when clinicians consider prescribing with this method. BACKGROUND: Wavefront-guided objective refractions have been investigated in patient populations that have highly aberrated optics and/or difficulty with subjective input, such as people with Down syndrome (DS). However, these objective refractions are determined for each eye individually, unlike a subjective refraction that considers both eyes. lens.title: Thirty-year follow-up of retinal vasculitis at a tertiary eye care center in India.
lens.summary: Retinal vasculitis has a chronic and unpredictable course, warranting long-term follow-up to detect late bilateral involvement and recurrence. While recurrence becomes less frequent over time, it may still occur after many years. Most patients continue to have idiopathic disease without subsequent identification of a systemic cause.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the clinical course of patients with retinal vasculitis over a three-decade follow-up. METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients with a minimum follow-up of 30 years at a tertiary eye care institute in India. RESULTS: A total of 37 patients were included. The mean follow-up duration was 34.3 ± 2.9 years (range: 30-44 years). The mean age of the patients at presentation was 31.05 ± 15.6 years, and 97% of them were male. In 54% of the patients, the involvement was bilateral. Five patients who initially presented with unilateral involvement subsequently developed involvement in the other eye. Presumed tuberculosis was diagnosed in five patients. None of the remaining patients developed ocular or extraocular manifestations of tuberculosis during the 30-year follow-up. lens.title: Diagnostic Performance of Integrated Tomographic-Biomechanical Indices Across Keratoconus Stages in a Chinese Population.
lens.summary: Integrated tomographic-biomechanical indices demonstrate reliable diagnostic performance for SKC and CKC in a Chinese population, although accurate discrimination of FFKC remains challenging. Population-adjusted metrics showed better overall performance at the specific cutoff value, driven by higher specificity despite lower sensitivity. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of integrated tomographic-biomechanical indices (specifically TBI, TBI for Chinese populations [cTBI], Corvis biomechanical index [CBI], and CBI for Chinese populations [cCBI]) across the different stages of keratoconus (KC) in a Chinese population and to explore a two-step approach for improving detection of early KC. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 642 eyes of 642 subjects (one eye per subject) classified into six groups: normal controls, forme fruste keratoconus (FFKC), subclinical keratoconus (SKC), and three clinical keratoconus (CKC) subgroups. A two-step workflow combining TBI and cTBI was additionally implemented in FFKC and SKC. lens.title: Effects of Combined Sound and Working Memory Therapy on Medial Olivocochlear System and Auditory Sensory Gating in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Preliminary Investigation Using Contralateral Suppression of Transient Evoked Otoacoustic Emission.
lens.summary: : SWMT appears to be a promising approach for enhancing auditory sensory gating in children with ASD, as evidenced by improvements in contralateral TEOAE suppression. Among the sound modalities tested, white noise combined with working memory training produced the greatest enhancement in TEOAE suppression.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: : This preliminary investigation evaluated the effectiveness of sound therapy and working memory training in improving auditory sensory gating in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), as measured by contralateral suppression of otoacoustic emissions. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: : Twenty-one children diagnosed with ASD participated in the study. Participants were randomly assigned to either a control group or an experimental group. The experimental group received a combined intervention consisting of sound and working memory training (SWMT). Within this group, participants were subdivided to receive one of three sound stimuli-white noise, waterfall sound, or Quranic recitation-along with working memory training. lens.title: PEDF alleviates autoimmune uveitis and reprograms Treg metabolism.
lens.summary: T cell-mediated autoimmune diseases remain difficult to manage owing to limited options and adverse effects of current immunosuppressants; safer, tolerance-preserving approaches are needed. We identify pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as an endogenous regulator of ocular immunity with therapeutic potential. …
lens.abstract: T cell-mediated autoimmune diseases remain difficult to manage owing to limited options and adverse effects of current immunosuppressants; safer, tolerance-preserving approaches are needed. We identify pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as an endogenous regulator of ocular immunity with therapeutic potential. PEDF expression was induced during autoimmune uveitis (AU) in patients and during experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU) progression, suggesting an endogenous compensatory response to inflammatory stress. Loss of PEDF did not substantially alter early peripheral immune activation but impaired inflammatory control during established disease, leading to persistent retinal inflammation and reduced Foxp3⁺ regulatory T (Treg) responses. lens.title: Biomimetic computational modelling of retinal ganglion cell responses to contact lens designs with refractive and opaque non-refractive features.
lens.summary: In this computational model, both BF and AR lens designs produced measurable changes in simulated RGC temporal activity relative to SV, with AR inducing greater and more configuration-independent modulation. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To computationally evaluate how single vision (SV), concentric bifocal (BF), and a contact lens with non-refractive opaque elements (AR) lens designs modulate retinal ganglion cell (RGC) activity. METHODS: Wide-field retinal simulations were generated using a schematic myopic eye corrected with SV, BF, and AR designs across three stimuli (Lena image, logMAR chart, dynamic gratings), three pupil diameters, and three residual accommodative error configurations. For each configuration, retinal image montages emulating blink-induced on-eye lens movement over one second were processed through a multilayer biomimetic virtual retina model to simulate RGC spike trains, quantified using median absolute deviation (MAD) and up-crossing rate (UCR). lens.title: Investigating the role of binocular vision in visuomotor control during the reciprocal Fitts's tapping task.
lens.summary: Vision provides critical sensory information for the planning and control of goal-directed actions. Relative to monocular viewing, binocular viewing results in superior speed, accuracy, and precision of upper-limb movements, indicating that binocular input facilitates movement planning and execution. …
lens.abstract: Vision provides critical sensory information for the planning and control of goal-directed actions. Relative to monocular viewing, binocular viewing results in superior speed, accuracy, and precision of upper-limb movements, indicating that binocular input facilitates movement planning and execution. Although the contribution of binocular vision to discrete actions is well established, its role in reciprocal movements remains poorly understood. Reciprocal tapping movements (i.e., Fitts' task) provide a useful model for examining movement execution because they place relatively lower demands on motor planning. Moreover, varying the index of difficulty (ID) alters the balance between feedforward and feedback control, with greater ID increasing reliance on feedback. lens.title: Clinical utility of pupil diameter cutoffs for detecting early presbyopia.
lens.summary: A difference in pupil diameter of 0.95mm could be the optimal cutoff value for assessing early presbyopia. As pupil dynamics have been previously related to presbyopia, this study proposes threshold pupil diameter measurement values to provide an alternative practical way to clinically screen for and assess presbyopia.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Little data exist on clinically relevant pupil diagnostic values for detecting early presbyopia (accommodative amplitude [AA]< 2.50D). This study aimed to determine the optimal cutoff value of pupil diameters for screening early presbyopia. STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study METHODS: 115 individuals aged ≥20 with visual acuity ≥20/25 who had attended one of two healthcare facilities in Japan between December 2020 and December 2021 were included. AA and near and distance pupillary diameters were measured by auto kerato-refractometer (ARK-1s; NIDEK Co.). Optimal cutoff values for early presbyopia were determined by receiver operating characteristic plots based on the Youden index. lens.title: Adsorption-Governed Plasmonic Sensing for Environmental Management and Monitoring Programs.
lens.summary: Plasmonic environmental sensors are often characterized by optical enhancement, but their field performance is fundamentally governed by adsorption at the sensing interface. …
lens.abstract: Plasmonic environmental sensors are often characterized by optical enhancement, but their field performance is fundamentally governed by adsorption at the sensing interface. This review examines adsorption-controlled plasmonic sensing across water, air, soil, and food-environment matrices, emphasizing environmental management rather than cross-domain plasmonic applications. This review evaluates surface plasmon resonance, localized surface plasmon resonance, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering in terms of pretreatment requirements, matrix interference, fouling, regeneration, reproducibility, validation against standard methods, and technology readiness. The review shows that plasmonic platforms are most valuable when used as rapid screening, distributed, or early-warning tools that complement, rather than replace, reference methods such as ICP-MS, GC-MS, and LC-MS/MS. lens.title: Polymeric Materials for Ophthalmic Lenses: A Systematic Review on Structure, Properties, Manufacturing and Sustainability.
lens.summary: Polymeric materials have largely replaced mineral glass in ophthalmic lenses owing to their low density, impact resistance, optical performance, and manufacturing versatility. …
lens.abstract: Polymeric materials have largely replaced mineral glass in ophthalmic lenses owing to their low density, impact resistance, optical performance, and manufacturing versatility. Despite their widespread use, the available literature remains fragmented, with individual studies primarily addressing specific polymer families, optical performance, manufacturing technologies, or surface coatings rather than providing an integrated overview of ophthalmic lens materials. This systematic review critically examines the relationships between chemical structure and molecular architecture of ophthalmic lens polymers and their optical, mechanical, thermal, and processing properties. The literature published between 2000 and 2026 was searched in Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and PubMed, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and 91 documents were included. lens.title: Systemic Medication Adjustment and Short-Term Relapse of Cytomegalovirus Retinitis After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Research Communication.
lens.summary: Background: Cytomegalovirus retinitis (CMVR) remains a sight-threatening complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). Systemic antiviral, immunosuppressive, and anti-infective regimens are often modified because of transplant-related complications, but the association between these modifications and o …
lens.abstract: Background: Cytomegalovirus retinitis (CMVR) remains a sight-threatening complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). Systemic antiviral, immunosuppressive, and anti-infective regimens are often modified because of transplant-related complications, but the association between these modifications and ocular relapse remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed a prospective cohort of 44 patients with CMVR after allo-HSCT (65 affected eyes) who were followed for three months after discontinuation of local antiviral therapy. The primary analysis used Cox proportional hazards regression at the eye level with robust standard errors clustered by patient. Exact dates of the first systemic medication adjustment were retrieved, and additional time-dependent Cox and patient-level time-to-first-relapse Cox analyses were performed. lens.title: The Effect of Different Auditory Conditions on Pattern-Reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (PVEPs) in Healthy Adults.
lens.summary: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of different auditory conditions on pattern-reversal visual evoked potential (PVEP) responses among healthy adults. …
lens.abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of different auditory conditions on pattern-reversal visual evoked potential (PVEP) responses among healthy adults. Methods: This repeated-measure design with a fixed baseline and randomized order of the two auditory conditions was conducted at the Retina Clinic, Ophthalmology Department, Tertiary Hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Healthy adults with no systemic or ocular diseases aged 20-60 years were included. All participants underwent comprehensive visual and ocular assessment, including best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), slit-lamp examination, optical coherence tomography (OCT), screening audiometry, and a PVEP test conducted under three auditory conditions: silence, Quran recitation, and music exposure. lens.title: RCNet: A Hybrid Network Adapted for OCTA Retinal Capillary Segmentation.
lens.summary: Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) provides clear visualization of ocular microvascular details, serving as a critical tool for assessing retinal and choroidal vascular systems. …
lens.abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) provides clear visualization of ocular microvascular details, serving as a critical tool for assessing retinal and choroidal vascular systems. However, the complex capillary structure and low capillary-to-background contrast in high-resolution OCTA images pose significant challenges for segmentation. To address the low segmentation accuracy of traditional methods, this paper proposes RCNet, a hybrid CNN-Transformer network. RCNet adopts an encoder-decoder architecture based on Bi-Level Routing Attention (BRA), where bi-level routing attention focuses on densely vascularized regions, optimizing global capillary feature extraction. A Convolutional Bottleneck Module (CBM) splits bottleneck features into two channel groups using a fixed ratio α. lens.title: Effect of Peripheral Defocus Contact Lens Residual Decentration After Six Months of Wear on the Astigmatic Component in Myopic Children.
lens.summary: Background/Objectives: To ascertain if the residual decentration of contact lenses with peripheral retinal defocusing geometry could be associated with alterations in the astigmatic refractive component over a six-month period of wear in children. …
lens.abstract: Background/Objectives: To ascertain if the residual decentration of contact lenses with peripheral retinal defocusing geometry could be associated with alterations in the astigmatic refractive component over a six-month period of wear in children. Methods: A total of 39 eyes from 39 participants (mean age: 11.1 ± 1.54 years, ranging from 6 to 13 years) were included. Participants underwent an eye examination and were assigned to one of three studied lenses: multifocal contact lenses with either non-adjustable (Biofinity Multifocal) or adjustable parameters (Gentle 80 Multifocal), or a contact lens designed for myopia control (MYLO). After six months of lens wear, a refractive assessment was performed and topographic images of the eye with the contact lens fitted were taken. lens.title: Neurovascular Retinomics for Noninvasive Profiling of Cancer Risk: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK Biobank.
lens.summary: Retinomics demonstrates predictive value for cancer incidence, with cancer type-specific biomarker selection enhancing accuracy. These findings highlight the transformative potential of retinal imaging as a scalable, noninvasive approach for early cancer risk profiling and proactive prevention.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate the predictive value of neurovascular retinal measurements for incident cancer. DESIGN: Population-based, prospective cohort study. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 41 424 participants with eligible color fundus photography and OCT data from the UK Biobank. METHODS: Retinomics were derived from multimodal retinal imaging of the UK Biobank, comprising 156 retinal features. Four Cox regression models were developed: model 1 (age and sex), model 2 (model 1 + ethnicity and lifestyle factors), model 3 (model 1 + retinomics), and model 4 (full model). Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression was used to select relevant retinal biomarkers, tailored to each cancer type. lens.title: The Cost-Of-Living Crisis and Suicide Rates.
lens.summary: Background: The cost-of-living crisis may be contributing to suicide rates, but this has not been adequately tested. Aims: We aimed to determine whether the cost-of-living crisis is associated with suicide rates in multiple countries and areas-within-countries. …
lens.abstract: Background: The cost-of-living crisis may be contributing to suicide rates, but this has not been adequately tested. Aims: We aimed to determine whether the cost-of-living crisis is associated with suicide rates in multiple countries and areas-within-countries. Method: We sourced country- and area-within-country-level monthly suicide data at a minimum from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2022 (and at a maximum from January 1, 2016, to June 30, 2023), and population denominator and monthly headline consumer price index (CPI) data. We calculated the yearly change in inflation as the percentage change in CPI for one month versus the equivalent month in the previous year. We estimated associations between yearly change in inflation (lagged by one month) and suicide rates for each country and area-within-country, using autoregressive negative binomial regression. lens.title: Contrast sensitivity and stereoacuity predict road traffic accidents among drivers in Ghana: a case-control study.
lens.summary: Contrast sensitivity and stereoacuity were independently associated with RTAs among drivers in Cape Coast. These findings suggest that assessments of contrast sensitivity and stereoacuity may provide useful complementary information beyond conventional visual acuity testing.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Road traffic accidents (RTAs) are a growing public health concern across sub-Saharan Africa, including Ghana. While human error is the leading cause, the role of visual function is often overlooked. This study investigates the relationship between visual function and accident involvement among drivers in Cape Coast, Ghana. METHODS: A comparative cross-sectional study involving 242 licensed drivers (121 cases, 121 controls) was conducted at the School of Optometry and Vision Science Eye Clinic, University of Cape Coast. Drivers aged 18 years and older were included in the study. Visual assessments included visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, stereoacuity, colour vision, visual fields, and refractive error. lens.title: HYALURONIC ACID (HA)-INDUCED INCREASE IN ANATOMICAL ACCOMMODATION RESPONSE IN PRESBYOPIC MONKEYS.
lens.summary: Our goal was to restore age related loss in HA levels in the vitreous of the presbyopic monkey eye to determine if intravitreal injection of HA restores the anatomical (i.e. …
lens.abstract: Our goal was to restore age related loss in HA levels in the vitreous of the presbyopic monkey eye to determine if intravitreal injection of HA restores the anatomical (i.e. accommodative lens thickening, forward movement of the posterior zonule insertion zone and thereby ciliary muscle forward movement etc.) and dioptric accommodative response and if so the duration of the response increase. We injected 0.3ml of HA (14mg/ml; Healon GV) into the vitreous near the optic nerve region, quantified the accommodative response to i.v. pilocarpine (2mg/kg wt) before and two weeks after HA injection, and compared accommodative responses at both time points and at 5, 8 and 16 months post HA. Accommodative amplitude was measured by Hartinger coincidence refractometry. lens.title: Adaptive Optics Simulation of Mini-monovision with Enhanced-monofocal Intraocular Lens Technology.
lens.summary: ABSTRACT: BACKGROUND: Enhanced monofocal intraocular lenses aim to improve intermediate vision while maintaining good distance visual acuity (VA), offering an alternative to multifocal IOLs. Mini-monovision can expand the range of vision without significantly compromising binocular quality. …
lens.abstract: ABSTRACT: BACKGROUND: Enhanced monofocal intraocular lenses aim to improve intermediate vision while maintaining good distance visual acuity (VA), offering an alternative to multifocal IOLs. Mini-monovision can expand the range of vision without significantly compromising binocular quality. This study evaluated the visual performance of the RayOne EMV (RAO200E) and Acunex Quantum (AN6Q) IOLs under mini-monovision conditions using the SimVis Gekko simulator. ABSTRACT: PATIENTS/METHODS AND MATERIAL: Six healthy volunteers underwent a simulation with the SimVis Gekko. Ocular dominance was determined using the "hole-in-the-hand" test. Mini-monovision was induced by applying -0.5 and -1.0 D of myopia to the nondominant eye. lens.title: A Smartphone-Based Digital Ruler to Automatically Measure Strabismus in Ophthalmologist-Level: A Prospective, Multicenter Cohort Study.
lens.summary: DRS enables strabismus assessment from videos recorded on consumer-grade smartphones. This approach may complement conventional clinic-based examinations and has the potential to expand access to strabismus screening and longitudinal monitoring, particularly in resource-limited settings. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Strabismus is a common condition that requires early screening to prevent amblyopia and stereopsis loss. Traditional methods are labor-intensive and costly, limiting their use. A smartphone-based approach for precise, automated strabismus measurement may offer a more accessible solution for early detection and management. METHODS: We developed the Digital Ruler of Strabismus (DRS), a system that employs three-dimensional reconstruction and deep learning algorithms to analyze 30-second videos of programmatic cover tests recorded by patients using smartphones. The diagnostic and quantitative performance of DRS was evaluated, and its consistency with manual prism measurements performed by ophthalmologists was compared. lens.title: Patient preferences for portable versus table-mounted visual field devices in rural Alabama: A mixed methods study within a telemedicine setting.
lens.summary: Rural underserved patients strongly preferred portable visual field devices, particularly VR-based, over table-mounted HFA. Comfort, ergonomic flexibility, immersive visual experience, and simplicity of interaction were central determinants of preference. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate patient satisfaction and preferences for portable versus table-mounted visual field (VF) devices in a rural telemedicine setting and identify influencing factors. METHODS: We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed methods study at three Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) within the Alabama Screening and Intervention for Glaucoma and eye Health through Telemedicine (AL-SIGHT) study. Participants completed VF testing with table-mounted Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA), tablet-based Melbourne Rapid Fields (MRF), and virtual reality (VR)-based VisuALL perimeters. Participants rated satisfaction, comfort, ease of use, and future testing preference. Chi-square tests assessed differences in device preferences. Wearable eye tracking may provide objective information about ocular behaviour during sport-specific performance, although evidence on blink behaviour and pupil diameter in elite players remains limited. METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study analysed blink-related and pupil-related variables during a standardised table tennis stroke-performance test in 17 elite male players. Participants completed a 56-ball robot-based protocol, consisting of six familiarisation trials followed by 50 analysed forehand topspin strokes. lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The Bonferroni correction adjusts probability (p) values because of the increased risk of a type I error when making multiple statistical tests. The routine use of this test has been criticised as deleterious to sound statistical judgment, testing the wrong hypothesis, and reducing the chance of a type I error but at the expense of a type II error; yet it remains popular in ophthalmic research. The purpose of this article was to survey the use of the Bonferroni correction in research articles published in three optometric journals, viz. Ophthalmic & Physiological Optics, Optometry & Vision Science, and Clinical & Experimental Optometry, and to provide advice to authors contemplating multiple testing. lens.abstract: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. Definitions of presbyopia are inconsistent and varied, so we propose a redefinition that states "presbyopia occurs when the physiologically normal age-related reduction in the eye's focusing range reaches a point, when optimally corrected for distance vision, that the clarity of vision at near is insufficient to satisfy an individual's requirements". lens.abstract: Ophthalmic lens design concerns the control of spectacle lens aberrations which occur when the eye rotates away from the optical centre of the lens. The most significant aberrations are oblique astigmatism and mean oblique error (power error). A brief review of these aberrations is given, explaining how the lens designer can control them using just the bending of the lens, and what results can be achieved using simple spherical and toroidal surfaces. Before 1985, aspherical surfaces were used only for post-cataract spectacle lenses and high-power magnifiers. Today, aspherical surfaces are used by all major lens manufacturers to produce thinner, lighter and more attractive best-form lenses in the normal power range. lens.abstract: A novel portable device has been developed and built to dynamically, and automatically, correct presbyopia by means of a couple of opto-electronics lenses driven by pupil tracking. The system is completely portable providing with a high range of defocus correction up to 10 D. The glasses are controlled and powered by a smartphone. To achieve a truly real-time response, image processing algorithms have been implemented in OpenCL and ran on the GPU of the smartphone. To validate the system, different visual experiments were carried out in presbyopic subjects. Visual acuity was maintained nearly constant for a range of distances from 5 m to 20 cm.

Progressive senescent changes in the lens ultimately lead to a complete loss of this ability by about age 50, which then requires alternative strategies to generate high-quality retinal images for far and close viewing distances. lens.summary: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. …
lens.abstract: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. Here, we report that blur differences cause a previously unknown motion illusion that makes people dramatically misperceive the distance and three-dimensional direction of moving objects. The effect occurs because the blurry and sharp images are processed at different speeds. For moving objects, the mismatch in processing speed causes a neural disparity, which results in the misperceptions. We performed a secondary analysis of a site-randomized quality improvement project on transitioning from chart-based to instrument-based vision screening for 3- to 5-year-old children in primary care. lens.abstract: As humans age, they gradually lose the ability to accommodate, or refocus, to near distances because of the stiffening of the crystalline lens. This condition, known as presbyopia, affects nearly 20% of people worldwide. We design and build a new presbyopia correction, autofocals, to externally mimic the natural accommodation response, combining eye tracker and depth sensor data to automatically drive focus-tunable lenses. We evaluated 19 users on visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, and a refocusing task. Autofocals exhibit better visual acuity when compared to monovision and progressive lenses while maintaining similar contrast sensitivity. On the refocusing task, autofocals are faster and, compared to progressives, also significantly more accurate. lens.abstract: Bifocal and multifocal optical devices are intended to get images into focus from objects placed at different distances from the observer. lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Stereoscopic vision (or stereopsis) is the ability to perceive depth from binocular disparity - the difference of viewpoints between the two eyes. Interestingly, there are large individual differences as to how well one can appreciate depth from such a cue. The total absence of stereoscopic vision, called 'stereoblindness', has been associated with negative behavioural outcomes such as poor distance estimation. Surprisingly, the prevalence of stereoblindness remains unclear, as it appears highly dependent on the way in which stereopsis is measured. RECENT FINDINGS: This review highlights the fact that stereopsis is not a unitary construct, but rather implies different systems. The scientific basis for and efficacy of optometric vision therapy in nonstrabismic accommodative and vergence disorders.
lens.summary: The findings clearly support the validity of optometric vision therapy. Furthermore, the results are consistent with the tenets of general motor learning.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: For nearly 75 years, optometric vision therapy has been an important mode of therapy for both children and adults who manifested a range of nonstrabismic accommodative and vergence disorders. METHODS: In this article, the scientific basis for, and efficacy of, optometric vision therapy in such patients will be discussed. Using bio-engineering models of the oculomotor system as the conceptual framework, emphasis will be focused on studies that used objective recording techniques to directly assess therapeutically related changes in oculomotor responsivity. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The findings clearly support the validity of optometric vision therapy. Furthermore, the results are consistent with the tenets of general motor learning.

lens.title: The relationship between moderate hyperopia and academic achievement: how much plus is enough?
lens.summary: Statistical analysis indicated significantly lower achievement test scores among hyperopic children whose refractive errors exceeded 1.25 D (ANOVA F = 12.51; df = 4; p = 0.014).
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is evidence linking uncorrected hyperopia in children with academic learning problems. METHODS: This study was designed to test that hypothesis and--given supportive data--to then address a second topic: the minimal amount of uncorrected hyperopia that appears to impede elementary school performance. RESULTS: The refractive status and achievement test scores of 782 first-through-fifth grade children were compared. CONCLUSIONS: Statistical analysis indicated significantly lower achievement test scores among hyperopic children whose refractive errors exceeded 1.25 D (ANOVA F = 12.51; df = 4; p = 0.014).

lens.title: Corneal and refractive error astigmatism in Singaporean schoolchildren: a vector-based Javal's rule.
lens.summary: Our vector-based Javal's rule gives closer predictions of refractive astigmatism than the original Javal's rule and the simplified Javal's rule and can be applied in cases of corneal oblique astigmatism.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traditional approaches to Javal's rule do not use data from subjects with oblique astigmatism and have not been used to make predictions about subjects with oblique astigmatism. Vector approaches to analyzing refractive error can circumvent these problems. METHODS: Subjects were 993 Singaporean schoolchildren. We performed linear regression of refractive error astigmatism on corneal astigmatism, using J0 vectors to describe with-the-rule and against-the-rule astigmatism and J45 vectors to describe oblique astigmatism. RESULTS: We obtained the following statistically significant regression relationships: RJ0 = 0.931 x CJ0 - 0.276 and RJ45 = 0.638 x CJ45 + 0.010, where R and C denote refractive error astigmatism and corneal astigmatism, respectively. CONCLUSION: Our vector-based Javal's rule gives closer predictions of refractive astigmatism than the original Javal's rule and t

lens.title: Wavelength dependence of the optomotor response in zebrafish (Danio rerio).
lens.summary: The action spectrum of motion detection in zebrafish (Danio rerio) was measured using the optomotor response in the light adapted state. The function has a single maximum at 550-600 nm, and is similar to the spectral sensitivity function of the L-cone type in the mid and long wavelength range. …
lens.abstract: The action spectrum of motion detection in zebrafish (Danio rerio) was measured using the optomotor response in the light adapted state. The function has a single maximum at 550-600 nm, and is similar to the spectral sensitivity function of the L-cone type in the mid and long wavelength range. At shorter wavelengths the values of three of the five fish tested are lower. As in goldfish [Vis. Res. 36 (1996) 4025], the result indicates a dominance of the L-cone type with an inhibitory influence of M- or S-cones. Experiments with a red/green striped cylinder showed that the optomotor response was at minimum whenever the L-cone type was not modulated by the moving pattern. This demonstrates that motion vision in zebrafish is "color blind", using mainly one of the four cone types probably involved in color vision.

lens.title: The eye as an optical instrument: from camera obscura to Helmholtz's perspective.
lens.summary: The era of modern vision research can be thought of as beginning in the seventeenth century with Johannes Kepler's understanding of the optics of the camera obscura with a lens and its relation to the eye. …
lens.abstract: The era of modern vision research can be thought of as beginning in the seventeenth century with Johannes Kepler's understanding of the optics of the camera obscura with a lens and its relation to the eye. During the nineteenth century, Helmholtz used "The eye as an optical instrument" as the title for one of his Popular Lectures, and such a conception of the eye is now accepted as a fundamental feature of visual science. In analysing the optics of the eye, Helmholtz constructed some novel optical instruments for studying the eye. The development of optometers, ophthalmometers, and ophthalmoscopes is presented historically, with emphasis on how these instruments and camera analogies helped scientists to understand the functions of the eye, especially the enigma of accommodation.
