lens.title: Predicting prescribed magnification.
lens.summary: The magnification necessary to perform normal visual tasks can be predicted in the majority of cases using visual acuity measures, although measuring the effect of proximal magnification demonstrates the effect of stronger glasses and identifies those in whom prescribed magnification is more difficult to predict.
lens.abstract: AIM: To determine the best method of estimating the optimum magnification needed by visually impaired patients. METHODS: The magnification of low vision aids prescribed to 187 presbyopic visually impaired patients for reading newspapers or books was compared with logMAR distance and near acuity (at 25 cm) and magnification predicted by +4 D step near additions. RESULTS: Distance letter (r = 0.58) and near word visual acuity (r = 0.67) were strongly correlated to the prescribed magnification as were predictive formulae based on these measures. Prediction using the effect of proximal magnification resulted in a similar correlation (r = 0.67) and prediction was poorer in those who did not benefit from proximal magnification. lens.title: The effect of experience on the detection of small eye movements.
lens.summary: The results indicate that during ideal conditions, little or no training is required for efficient detection of small eye movements.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to determine whether experience improves detection of small eye movements similar to those seen in the cover test during ideal conditions. METHODS: Three groups of examiners with varying amounts of experience in eye movement detection tasks were studied. Eight examiners were 1st-year optometry students, six were 4th-year optometry students, and six were practicing optometrists. To determine thresholds for eye movement detection, examiners indicated the horizontal direction in which the eyes of one of the experimenters moved. The direction and extent of each eye movement was randomly selected. The extent of the eye movement was one of eight logarithmic steps from a maximum that was determined through an initial session where the approximate sensitivity of the examiners was found (generally +/- 1.75 prism diopters). lens.title: The underachieving child.
lens.summary: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. …
lens.abstract: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. Additionally, there are several optometric correlates of SpLD which may, in some cases, contribute to the learning difficulty. These correlates include binocular instability and a low amplitude of accommodation. Some people with reading difficulties and perceptual distortions/eyestrain can be helped by individually prescribed coloured filters. A visual processing anomaly is also often present in the form of a deficit of the transient visual system. The role of the optometrist is discussed.

lens.title: [Logarithmic visual acuity charts: reasons to use and how to design it].
lens.summary: Visual acuity represents the visual angle or the smallest distance between two points that allows their discrimination as separated points. Although it is the most common clinical measurement of visual function, it is often misunderstood, especially due to the variety of charts and different notation systems employed for its quantificatio …
lens.abstract: Visual acuity represents the visual angle or the smallest distance between two points that allows their discrimination as separated points. Although it is the most common clinical measurement of visual function, it is often misunderstood, especially due to the variety of charts and different notation systems employed for its quantification. This article reviews some concepts about visual acuity measurement, the main notation systems, type of charts and discuss the advantages of using logarithmic scales.

lens.summary: With the rapid development of modern ophthalmology and optometry, people put in higher claim for visual quality. However, the application and penetration of the optometry knowledge and research achievement in every domain of ophthalmology are bound to affect the elevation of visual quality, which is one of the highlights our future work.

lens.summary: Variations of power errors in the periphery of concave aspheric lenses were assessed as a function of vertex distance. Comparisons were made between the performance of different types of spherical lenses and that of aspheric lenses (-6.00 and -8.00 D lenses were used). …
lens.abstract: Variations of power errors in the periphery of concave aspheric lenses were assessed as a function of vertex distance. Comparisons were made between the performance of different types of spherical lenses and that of aspheric lenses (-6.00 and -8.00 D lenses were used). Off-axis measurements were made by means of a modified focimeter, which enabled rotation of the lens around the center of the vertex sphere. Reduction of the vertex sphere's radius from 27 to 23 mm simulated a 4-mm decrease in vertex distance. Results of the measurements are compared with a computed model. These results indicate that off-axis performance is more affected by a reduction of vertex distance in the case of aspheric lenses compared to spherical lenses. lens.abstract: We assessed the repeatability and validity of the PowerRefractor and the Nidek AR-600A autorefractor. This is the first independent study conducted on adults to evaluate the performance of these instruments in a laboratory setting. Fifty subjects (23 males and 27 females) aged 16 to 61 years (mean, 37 +/- 12) participated in the study. The validity of the PowerRefractor and the Nidek autorefractor readings were determined by comparing them to subjective refraction. Measurements of refractive error were obtained from the two instruments on two separate occasions to assess their repeatability. The measured refractive error was converted into a dioptric power matrix for data analysis. No significant difference was found between the measurements obtained with the two instruments and the subjective refraction. lens.title: [Discussion on logarithmic visual acuity chart and five grade notation].
lens.summary: To explore the scientific aspect of logarithmic visual acuity chart and five grade notation, a visual test-type ten times large as the test-type of 4.0 grade was put 0.5 m before the eye, if the eye saw it, then the visual acuity was 2.0 grade (visual angle 1000' = 16.67 degrees). …
lens.abstract: To explore the scientific aspect of logarithmic visual acuity chart and five grade notation, a visual test-type ten times large as the test-type of 4.0 grade was put 0.5 m before the eye, if the eye saw it, then the visual acuity was 2.0 grade (visual angle 1000' = 16.67 degrees). If moving this test-type to 0.05 m before the eye, 1.0 grade (visual angle 10 000' = 166.7 degrees) was obtained. They are more scientific than original records: hand movement for 2.0 grade and light perception for 1.0 grade. These test-type theoretically satisfy the demand of 5 grade notation. Logarithmic visual acuity chart and 5 grade notation is more superior subject created in China.

lens.title: Defining myopia using refractive error and uncorrected logMAR visual acuity >0.3 from 1334 Singapore school children ages 7-9 years.
lens.summary: The cut-off points of -0.75D and -0.5D in SE refraction are appropriate for the prediction of uncorrected logMAR VA worse than 0.3, which is the criterion for the US common state adult driver licensing standard.
lens.abstract: AIM: To determine the association of spherical equivalent (SE) with low uncorrected visual acuity (VA) along with a proposed definition for myopia using logMAR VA >0.3 as the criteria. METHODS: 1334 Chinese schoolchildren (mean age 7.8; range 7-9 years) were enrolled in the study after those who had hyperopia > or =+2.00 dioptres (D) and astigmatism > = -2.00 D were excluded. Uncorrected logMAR VA was measured for both eyes. Cycloplegia autorefraction was achieved by the instillation of three drops of 1% cyclopentolate 5 minutes apart. lens.summary: Measurement of off-axis wavefront aberrations of a model eye over a restricted range of eccentricities is possible with the COAS clinical wavefront aberrometer and auxiliary lenses to correct astigmatism. lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical aberrometers are accurate, robust instruments for measuring wavefront aberrations for foveal vision, but several practical concerns arise when performing aberrometry of the peripheral field. The purpose of this study was to evaluate these concerns experimentally using a physical eye model. METHODS: A physical model eye was constructed to provide a stable test case that resembled a human eye. Aberrations were measured with a commercial Shack-Hartmann aberrometer along lines-of-sight ranging from zero to 45 degrees of eccentricity. Commercial software for wavefront reconstruction and Zernike analysis was adapted for use with elliptical entrance pupils encountered off-axis. lens.title: Glaucoma screening during regular optician visits: can the population at risk of developing glaucoma be reached?
lens.summary: By conducting glaucoma screening during regular optician visits, a large section of the population at risk of developing glaucoma can be reached.
lens.abstract: AIM: To determine the percentage of the population at risk of developing glaucoma, which can potentially be reached by conducting glaucoma screening during regular optician visits. METHODS: 1,200 inhabitants aged >40 years were randomly selected from Dutch community population databases. A questionnaire was mailed to these inhabitants with questions on their latest optician visit and risk factors for glaucoma. A second questionnaire was sent to their opticians, who were asked about their willingness to conduct an additional glaucoma screening programme in the future. RESULTS: The questionnaire was returned by 959 of 1,200 inhabitants and 37 of 50 opticians. lens.title: Decision making in chronic glaucoma--optometrists vs ophthalmologists in a shared care service.
lens.summary: An audit model of decision-making in shared care is demonstrated that in this case supported the apprenticeship model of training utilised in the clinic.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Shared care schemes have become popular in glaucoma management in the UK over the past 20 years. Published audits of decision making processes by non-ophthalmologists working in such schemes are however rare. Our aim was to audit the appropriateness of optometrists' decision-making when working in an in-house shared care glaucoma scheme. METHODS: A single masked comparison study utilising retrospective consensus decisions by two ophthalmologists compared with 'live' optometrist decisions from three optometrists who reviewed patients with glaucoma, suspect glaucoma and ocular hypertension. RESULTS: Comparisons were made on management decisions on 140 consecutive eligible patients. lens.title: Awareness of diabetic retinopathy among physicians and optometrists in a district of West Bengal.
lens.summary: A cross sectional study was done to ascertain the current knowledge among physicians and optometrists regarding diabetic retinopathy in a district of West Bengal. We obtained response from 242 physicians and 36 optometrists working in government health units. …
lens.abstract: A cross sectional study was done to ascertain the current knowledge among physicians and optometrists regarding diabetic retinopathy in a district of West Bengal. We obtained response from 242 physicians and 36 optometrists working in government health units. The questionnaire comprised of three sections covering magnitude of problem, risk factors and management. The responses were analysed and graded. In different sections, knowledge of 74 - 78% physicians and 83 - 86% optometrists was graded as not acceptable. Existing lack of knowledge among physicians and optometrists regarding diabetic retinopathy needs correction.

lens.title: Barriers perceived by UK-based community optometrists to the detection of primary open angle glaucoma.
lens.summary: In general, UK optometrists believed that their ability to detect POAG in the community is hampered by time and financial constraints. However, barriers were significantly fewer in Scotland, where optometrists have different contractual terms of service with the NHS than their counterparts in the rest of the UK.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: This paper aims to identify the barriers to case-finding for primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) as perceived by community optometrists in the United Kingdom (UK). METHODS: An anonymous, online survey to investigate the current mode of optometric practice for the detection of POAG was developed. The survey included a free-text question relating to barriers to case-finding for the disease. Optometrists on the Association of Optometrists (AOP) electronic database were invited to participate. The survey was open for 16 weeks between April and July 2008. RESULTS: A total of 1680 responses was received to the survey, of which 1293 (77%) answered the free-text question relating to perceived barriers. lens.title: Reading with low vision: the impact of research on clinical management.
lens.summary: The past 40 years has seen a great expansion in low-vision research, which has changed low-vision teaching and our clinical management of people with low vision. Australian optometrists have contributed significantly to this research and the development of multidisciplinary low-vision services. …
lens.abstract: The past 40 years has seen a great expansion in low-vision research, which has changed low-vision teaching and our clinical management of people with low vision. Australian optometrists have contributed significantly to this research and the development of multidisciplinary low-vision services. This paper reviews the research that has shaped our clinical assessment and patient management for reading by adults with low vision. The major improvements in clinical assessment of low vision for reading were brought about by the improvements in distance and near visual acuity measurements during the 1970s and research during the 1980s and 1990s showing the factors affecting the reading rate. lens.title: Visibility of motion in infant vernier displays, using adult subjects.
lens.summary: Motion is frequently incorporated in stimuli used for psychophysical testing of vernier acuity in infants and young children. In such stimuli, detection of the vernier offset is necessary in order to perceive the motion. …
lens.abstract: Motion is frequently incorporated in stimuli used for psychophysical testing of vernier acuity in infants and young children. In such stimuli, detection of the vernier offset is necessary in order to perceive the motion. Research described in this report tested whether the perception of a vernier offset is sufficient to signal the stimulus motion in adults. We measured how motion detectability changed as a function of vernier offset for two adult subjects, using a stimulus similar to that employed by other authors to measure vernier acuity in infants and children. Motion visibility varied with offset size, achieving a detectability of motion (d') of 0.95 (comparable to two-alternative forced-choice thresholds) at stimulus offsets of 16-19 s arc. lens.summary: Purpose Myopia is a common cause of vision loss, with uncorrected myopia the leading cause of distance vision impairment globally. Individual studies show variations in the prevalence of myopia and high myopia between regions and ethnic groups, and there continues to be uncertainty regarding increasing prevalence of myopia. lens.summary: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. …
lens.abstract: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the Yale Precipitating Events Project cohort study, based in New Haven CT. Non-disabled people aged 70 years or older (n = 754) were enrolled and re-contacted every 18 months. The database includes variables on function, cognition, co-morbidity, health attitudes and practices and physical performance measures. Data came from the baseline cohort and those available at the first 18-month follow-up assessment. refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ciliary body cysts are common incidental findings during preoperative screening for implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation. Although their presence is generally not considered a contraindication to surgery, cysts extending into the ciliary sulcus may influence haptic seating. The potential contribution of cyst morphology to postoperative ICL behavior remains insufficiently described. CASE PRESENTATION: We report two myopic patients with ciliary body cysts protruding into the ciliary sulcus who underwent posterior chamber ICL implantation. Preoperative ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) was used to evaluate cyst anatomy. Case 1 had a single, qualitatively thin-walled, unilocular cyst and achieved an adequate postoperative vault of 445 μm at 3 months. refractive.title: Prevalence of self-reported dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among Saudi adults: A cross-sectional survey.
refractive.summary: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disea …
refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disease index (OSDI) questionnaire in Saudi Arabia. Four hundred and thirty nine participants were included. Dry eye OSDI scores compared across different epidemiological risk factors, focusing on refractive surgery type and postoperative duration. Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) or Femtosecond (FS)-LASIK, and small incision lenticule extraction procedures were performed on 201 (45.79%), 222 (50.56%), and 16 (3.65%) participants, respectively. refractive.title: Methyl aminolevulinate-PpIX mediated fluorescence-guided mapping of high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a pilot prospective clinical trial (PhotoDiVin).
refractive.summary: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. …
refractive.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. We conducted a pilot clinical study to assess the fluorescence-based cartography of VIN lesions using methyl aminolevulinate (m-ALA), which is a prodrug of the fluorophore protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). A prospective, single-center, single-arm clinical trial included 17 women with histologically confirmed high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN or vHSIL). refractive.title: Total Lower Eyelid Reconstruction With Auricular Cartilage-Perichondrium Graft and Upper Eyelid Rotation Flap.
refractive.summary: Reconstruction of large full-thickness lower eyelid defects remains a complex challenge in oculoplastic surgery because restoration of both functional integrity and aesthetic appearance is required. …
refractive.abstract: Reconstruction of large full-thickness lower eyelid defects remains a complex challenge in oculoplastic surgery because restoration of both functional integrity and aesthetic appearance is required. Successful reconstruction depends on adequate replacement of the posterior lamella to provide structural support and reconstruction of the anterior lamella to ensure appropriate coverage and mobility. The study presents a sample of 10 patients who presented with a basocellular carcinoma of the lower lid. A full-thickness resection with wide margins was performed and medial, lateral, and deep margins were subjected to extemporaneous histologic examination. In all 10 patients, to attain complete resection with 3 mm negative margins, following NCCN recommendations, a full-thickness total lower eyelid resection was performed. refractive.title: Comparative Refractive and Vector Outcomes of PRK in Moderate and High Astigmatism: A 12-Month Retrospective Study.
refractive.summary: PRK is an effective and predictable method for the correction of moderate to high astigmatism.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) results in patients with moderate to high astigmatism. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: One hundred twelve eyes of 71 patients with a cylindrical component of greater than 3 diopters (D) (moderate: 3.00 to 3.99 D; high: ≥4.00 D) undergone PRK were reviewed. UDVA, CDVA, and subjective refraction before and after surgery (1, 3, 6, 12 months) were extracted. RESULTS: The preoperative mean spherical equivalent (SE) was -3.39 ± 1.82 D (range -9.00 to 2.50 D), and the mean cylinder was -3.76 ± 0.78 D (range -3.00 to -6.00 D). The mean postoperative cylinder values were -0.73 ± 0.49 D, -0.72 ± 0.46 D, -0.58 ± 0.48 D, and -0.4 ± 0.63 D at 1- month, 3-month, 6-month, and 12-month visits, respectively. refractive.title: Extensively Drug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Keratitis After Photorefractive Keratectomy Because of Contaminated Eye Drops: Experience With Colistin-Based Therapy.
refractive.summary: This series highlights early recognition of extensively drug-resistant infections after PRK surgery, source identification, and prompt, microbiology-guided therapy, resulting in favorable outcomes.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to report the clinico-microbiological characteristics of cases of infectious keratitis caused by extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) and to identify the source of infection. METHODS: Retrospective review of 7 eyes from 4 patients presenting with infectious keratitis after bilateral PRK performed at different centers and time points, evaluated at a tertiary eye care center in India between March 2024 and August 2025. We analyzed demographic, clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data. RESULTS: The study included 7 eyes from 4 patients. Patients presented, on average, after 2.5 days (range, 1-4 ), and visual acuity ranged from 20/50 to perception of light with inaccurate projection of rays. refractive.title: OPTIMIZ: A Constraint-Driven Tool for Decision-Making in Full- Arch Rehabilitation.
refractive.summary: OPTIMIZ is a practical tool developed to simplify decision-making and improve treatment predictability in full-arch rehabilitation while minimizing avoidable surgical intervention. The tool should be used in conjunction with comprehensive patient evaluation, individualized treatment planning, and professional clinical judgment.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To present OPTIMIZ, a clinical tool developed to simplify restorative decision-making in full-arch implant rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla. OVERVIEW: Decision-making remains one of the most challenging aspects of full-arch implant rehabilitation. Implant-supported fixed complete prostheses (iFCPs) may provide highly favorable biologic, functional, and esthetic outcomes. However, their success depends on appropriate case selection and careful evaluation of esthetic, prosthetic, functional, soft tissue and bone-related factors. Inappropriate treatment selection may result in compromised esthetics, avoidable bone reduction, or overtreatment through extensive augmentation procedures. refractive.title: Surgical Treatment of Congenital Facial Palsy: A Retrospective Analysis of More than 20 Years' Experience in Smile Surgery.
refractive.summary: Background and Objectives: Congenital facial palsy, either isolated or associated with syndromic conditions such as Moebius syndrome, is a rare disorder that poses significant functional and psychological challenges for patients, families, and healthcare teams. …
refractive.abstract: Background and Objectives: Congenital facial palsy, either isolated or associated with syndromic conditions such as Moebius syndrome, is a rare disorder that poses significant functional and psychological challenges for patients, families, and healthcare teams. Dedicated care pathways and a multidisciplinary approach are essential for optimal management. This study presents our experience of more than 20 years in smile surgery, highlighting clinical outcomes with an objective analysis of facial symmetry and movement as well as a review of our progressive improvements of surgical techniques and patient management over time. Materials and Methods: Patients diagnosed with congenital facial palsy who were referred to our institution for rehabilitative treatment and surgical management between January 2003 and December 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. refractive.title: Parent-Reported Orofacial Health in Preterm- and Term-Born Children: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
refractive.summary: Longer reported pacifier use was associated with a broad parental perception of smile abnormality after FDR correction; causality and clinical significance cannot be established. The findings require confirmation using clinically verified perinatal data and standardized orofacial assessment.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early feeding experiences and non-nutritive sucking habits coexist with the development of orofacial functions and occlusion. This study compared the duration of breastfeeding, bottle feeding, and mixed feeding, as well as parent-reported orofacial outcomes in preterm- and term-born children, and exploratorily assessed associations among these variables. METHODS: A cross-sectional parent/caregiver survey used open convenience recruitment in online prematurity-related groups. The main comparison included 108 children (88 preterm and 20 term). Unambiguous duration records for all three feeding modes were available for 92 children and were analyzed as separate quantitative variables. refractive.title: Anterior vault as a risk stratification marker for trabecular-iris angle reduction after implantable collamer lens implantation.
refractive.summary: This study identified AV, WTW/ACD ratio, and preoperative angle metrics as key markers associated with postoperative TIA500 ≤20° after ICL implantation. AV proved to be a simple, clinically valuable marker to enhance risk stratification.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical utility of the anterior vault (AV), as measured by anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), as a risk stratification marker for a postoperative trabecular-iris angle (TIA) ≤ 20° following Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) implantation. Additionally, this study investigated postoperative alterations in iridocorneal angle dynamics after ICL placement. METHODS: This retrospective, observational study was conducted at a single private hospital and included 185 eyes from 185 patients who underwent ICL implantation between January 2018 and December 2023. The primary endpoint was to evaluate the discriminative performance of AV for identifying eyes with postoperative TIA500 ≤20°. refractive.title: Comparison of toric implantable collamer lens and bioptics for correction of high myopia with astigmatism.
refractive.summary: Both TICL and Bioptics are excellent options for correction of high myopia with astigmatism, Both showing comparable refractive and visual results and satisfaction scores.
refractive.abstract: AIM OF THE WORK: This work aims to offer a comparison of toric implantable collamer lens and bioptics for correction of high myopia with astigmatism, focusing on their clinical efficacy, safety profiles, complications and patient satisfaction. BACKGROUND: High myopia with astigmatism poses significant challenges to visual correction, affecting not only the quality of life but also daily functioning. Toric Implantable Collamer Lenses (TICL) and Bioptic (implantation of spherical ICL followed by laser vision correction to the residual astigmatism) procedures, represent two effective surgical interventions for correction of high myopia with astigmatism. METHODS: This study was designed as a prospective interventional case study. refractive.title: The Stomatognathic System as an Expanding Frontier for Botulinum Toxin Therapy.
refractive.summary: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) therapy has expanded from focal chemodenervation to a versatile therapeutic modality used across multiple medical specialties. The stomatognathic system is particularly suited to BoNT therapy because motor, sensory, articular, secretory, and aesthetic functions converge within a compact anatomical region. …
refractive.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) therapy has expanded from focal chemodenervation to a versatile therapeutic modality used across multiple medical specialties. The stomatognathic system is particularly suited to BoNT therapy because motor, sensory, articular, secretory, and aesthetic functions converge within a compact anatomical region. Current and emerging applications include oromandibular dystonia, dyskinesia, bruxism, tremor, hemimasticatory spasm, embouchure dystonia, masticatory muscle and temporomandibular disorder-related pain, trigeminal neuralgia, recurrent temporomandibular joint dislocation, sialorrhea, Frey syndrome, masseter prominence, gummy smile, and perioral wrinkles. Evidence and regulatory status vary substantially among indications, and many applications remain off-label. Dentistry and oral and maxillofacial surgery have historically played a limited role in BoNT therapy

refractive.title: Short- and Long-Term Dynamics of Endothelial Cell Density and Vault Changes After Implantable Collamer Lens Implantation.
refractive.summary: Background/Objectives: Endothelial cell density (ECD) and vault height are essential safety metrics in implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery, yet their reported decay rates vary. This study assessed short- and long-term changes in ECD and vault height. …
refractive.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endothelial cell density (ECD) and vault height are essential safety metrics in implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery, yet their reported decay rates vary. This study assessed short- and long-term changes in ECD and vault height. Methods: Medical records of patients undergoing V4c ICL implantation between 2014 and 2024 were reviewed. ECD loss was evaluated across three periods: early (baseline to 6 months), late (6 months to last visit), and total (baseline to last visit). Vault was measured at day 1 and months 3, 6, 12, and the last visit and decay rate was calculated for the entire follow-up period. Results: A total of 631 eyes of 323 patients were analyzed. The early, late, and total ECD losses per year were 1.81 ± 8.56% (95% CI 0.43 to 3.19), 0.68 ± 2.11% (95% CI 0.34 to 1.03), and 1.21 ± 2.58% (95% CI 0.83 to 1.59), respectively. refractive.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the eHealth-faciLitated SMILe-integrated care model on treatment burden, quality of life and graft-versus-host disease after allogeneic stem cell transplantation: results of two European randomized controlled implementation studies.
refractive.summary: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). …
refractive.abstract: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). To complement these findings and provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the intervention's effects, we evaluated patient-reported and clinical secondary outcomes from two RCTs. Data from two hybrid effectiveness-implementation RCTs conducted at two European alloSCT centers (Germany, Switzerland) were analyzed. Adult alloSCT recipients were randomized 1:1 to usual care (UCG) or the SMILe-ICM, a multicomponent intervention combining eHealth with advanced practice nurse-led self-management support. refractive.title: 4-Octyl Itaconate Suppresses Virulence of Multidrug-Resistant Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli via Cysteine Alkylation of LuxS, Icl, and OmpA.
refractive.summary: Avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) is the cause of avian colibacillosis, which leads to huge economic losses in poultry production worldwide, and presents significant zoonotic antimicrobial resistance (AMR) risk. …
refractive.abstract: Avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) is the cause of avian colibacillosis, which leads to huge economic losses in poultry production worldwide, and presents significant zoonotic antimicrobial resistance (AMR) risk. Cell-permeable itaconate derivatives exhibit dual antibacterial and immunomodulatory properties; however, they have not been systematically evaluated against APEC, and their underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined for this pathogen. In the present study, we systematically explored the anti-APEC therapeutic potential and mechanism of action of 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI) using an integrated approach of in vitro phenotypic, ex vivo macrophage, biochemical genetic, and dual in vivo infection models. refractive.title: Stability and outcome after two approaches for counterclockwise mandibular setback in patients with skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion: a prospective study.

refractive.abstract: Patients of skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion have different clinical entities. This prospective study aimed to compare stability and outcomes following two approaches for counterclockwise mandibular setback in bimaxillary rotational surgery to correct skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion. Fifty-six adult patients with skeletal class III high-angle malocclusion who underwent surgery-first bimaxillary surgery with counterclockwise mandibular setback were analyzed. Patients were grouped by different direction of mandibular distal segment: posterior-shortening (n = 25) and posterior-lengthening (n = 31). refractive.title: The Potential Role of Postbiotics in Periodontitis Treatment and Preventive Dentistry.
refractive.summary: Postbiotics, the bioactive molecules of probiotics and inactive microbial cells, have emerged as promising supplementary method in dental health treatment, specifically targeting disorders such as periodontitis. …
refractive.abstract: Postbiotics, the bioactive molecules of probiotics and inactive microbial cells, have emerged as promising supplementary method in dental health treatment, specifically targeting disorders such as periodontitis. The definition, mechanisms of action and therapeutic potential of postbiotics in periodontitis are discussed in detail in this review. The capacity of postbiotics to control pathogenic bacteria development, increase immune responses and restore microbial balance, demonstrates the many roles of postbiotics in antimicrobial activity and anti-inflammatory effects in controlling the oral microbiome. Importantly, postbiotics have potential advantages over live probiotics such as greater stability and safety, without the need for microbial colonization. refractive.title: Intermediate and near vision outcomes with an advanced monofocal aspheric Swiss Phob intraocular lens.
refractive.summary: The Swiss Phob advanced monofocal IOL provides good distance and intermediate visual acuity with functional near vision. The significant reciprocal association between uncorrected intermediate and near visual acuity suggests an extended range of functional vision across intermediate and near distances.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate postoperative visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near and determine correlation between intermediate and near vision following implantation of an advanced monofocal aspheric Swiss Phob intraocular lens (IOL). METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 60 eyes of 30 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery with Swiss Phob IOL implantation before May 2024. Postoperative evaluation at 6-12 months included uncorrected distance (UDVA), intermediate (UIVA), and near visual acuity (UNVA). refractive.title: Topical Losartan in the Management of Corneal Scarring from Trauma and Infection: A Case Series.
refractive.summary: Topical losartan may be an effective treatment for corneal scarring secondary to trauma or infection either following or in conjunction with corticosteroid therapy. Patients with such scarring should be considered for inclusion in future clinical trials which investigate the efficacy and safety of topical losartan treatment.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Losartan inhibits ERK-mediated signaling in the noncanonical transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) pathway, which may play a role in corneal fibrosis. Rabbit studies have shown that topical losartan can reduce stromal scarring, fibrosis, and myofibroblast formation after corneal injuries and other clinical insults. Its use in humans has since been reported for corneal scarring and haze following LASIK, corneal cross-linking, and herpes simplex and varicella-zoster virus infections. Here, we present several additional clinical scenarios in which topical losartan has demonstrated potential efficacy in reducing corneal scarring. refractive.title: Keratorefractive Surgery in Patients with Systemic Isotretinoin Exposure: A Propensity-Score-Matched Analysis of LASIK and PRK.
refractive.summary: Outcomes of LASIK and PRK were comparable between eyes with documented preoperative isotretinoin exposure and matched unexposed eyes across all cessation intervals observed, including surgery within days of documented use. These preliminary findings warrant prospective confirmation with ocular-surface endpoints.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether documented preoperative systemic isotretinoin exposure affects LASIK and PRK outcomes and complications. SETTING: Care Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel. DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study. METHODS: Consecutive primary myopic LASIK and PRK procedures (January 2013 to June 2024), excluding retreated and monovision eyes, were reviewed. Exposure was ascertained from clinical notes and a preoperative medication questionnaire; patients whose exposure began after surgery were excluded. Exposed patients were propensity-score matched 1:4 to controls on age, sex, year of surgery, and preoperative spherical equivalent (SEQ), cylinder, and central corneal thickness. refractive.title: Facial esthetic medicine in dentistry: botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid fillers for smile-face harmonization.
refractive.summary: Orofacial treatment planning is being redefined by the convergence of minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine and aesthetic dentistry. Specifically, hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) are being employed more frequently as adjuncts to maximize smile-lip-face harmony. …
refractive.abstract: Orofacial treatment planning is being redefined by the convergence of minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine and aesthetic dentistry. Specifically, hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) are being employed more frequently as adjuncts to maximize smile-lip-face harmony. The scope of non-invasive or minimally invasive facial aesthetic medicine for dentists has also been clarified by regulatory changes in Italy, underscoring the importance of competency-based training and organized risk management. The objective is to give a narrative summary of BoNT-A and HA fillers' indications, clinical procedures, integration into dental workflows, and safety concerns in dental practice, with a focus on perioral applications and complication management. refractive.title: HuKSA: A Machine-Learning-Based Framework for Predicting Human Kinome Selectivity and Polypharmacology.
refractive.summary: Off-target polypharmacology across the conserved kinase ATP pocket can limit the safety and efficacy of kinase-directed compounds. refractive.abstract: Off-target polypharmacology across the conserved kinase ATP pocket can limit the safety and efficacy of kinase-directed compounds. HuKSA is a transparent ligand-based framework that predicts kinase targets and estimates measured-kinome selectivity from a SMILES string while exposing the reference activities behind each estimate. Selectivity is summarized by the S-score, the fraction of measured kinases with pActivity above 6. refractive.title: Unilateral macrostomia repair using modified muscle reconstruction: Long-term anthropometric evaluation of static and smile symmetry.
refractive.summary: Long-term postoperative assessment results indicated that the modified muscle reconstruction technique was associated with favorable static and smile symmetry.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrostomia, or transverse facial cleft, substantially impairs facial esthetics and oral function. Although various repair techniques have been reported, achieving satisfactory bilateral symmetry, particularly during dynamic expressions such as smiling, continues to be a challenge. Here, we introduce our modified muscle reconstruction technique for unilateral macrostomia repair and evaluate long-term outcomes in static and smile symmetry using anthropometric measurements. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on all patients who underwent unilateral macrostomia repair at our institution between December 2008 and December 2019. The key surgical procedure involved anatomical separation of the pars marginalis and pars peripheralis of the orbicularis oris and approximation of the inferior orbicularis oris to superior orbicularis oris and buccinator. refractive.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
refractive.summary: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. …
refractive.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer to capture the sequential nature of these patterns. This architecture also exploits an attention mechanism that computes attention weights across the sequence, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant molecular substructures for toxicity prediction. refractive.title: Hydrophobic Acrylic Trifocal IOL in Post-Laser Refractive Surgery Eyes: Visual Performance, Predictability, and Patient-Reported Outcomes.

METHODS: This single-center, ambispective study included 94 eyes of 47 patients with previous myopic LRS undergoing CP implantation. refractive.title: Comparison of outcomes after SMILE using VISUMAX 800 and VISUMAX 500 for correcting myopia and myopic astigmatism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
refractive.summary: Within the limitations of this study, we did not detect evidence of statistical difference between SMILE and SMILE Pro surgical procedures when used for the treatment of myopia and astigmatism. SMILE Pro using VISUMAX 800 provided more accurate refractive cylinder outcomes. …

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched up to February 2026 to identify relevant studies. The PRISMA guidelines were followed. Primary outcomes were postoperative efficacy, safety, and predictability at the end of follow-up. Secondary outcomes were the postoperative high-order aberrations (HOAs) parameters and the vector analysis parameters. refractive.title: Functional and Aesthetic Outcomes of Trans-Mastoid Decompression for Facial Paralysis After Retroauricular Hyaluronic Acid Injection.
refractive.summary: Trans-mastoid facial nerve decompression is safe and effective for persistent facial paralysis secondary to retroauricular HA injection, yielding significant functional improvement and high patient satisfaction.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Retroauricular hyaluronic acid (HA) injection for aesthetic enhancement can precipitate immediate-onset facial nerve palsy. The underlying mechanism remains unclear, and no consensus exists on the next step when prolonged conservative therapy fails. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the pathogenesis of persistent facial paralysis following retroauricular HA injection and to evaluate the functional and aesthetic outcomes of trans-mastoid facial nerve decompression in affected patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 17 patients (16 females, 1 male; mean age 33.65±7.91 years) who developed immediate-onset unilateral facial paralysis after retroauricular HA injection and showed no improvement after 4 weeks of conservative therapy. refractive.title: Health and economic benefits of air quality improvements in France through diverse net-zero transition scenarios by 2050.
refractive.summary: Net-Zero transition can deliver substantial health and economic co-benefits across diverse policy pathways. These findings support integrating co-benefits into climate policy frameworks to strengthen the evidence base for ambitious mitigation action.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate mitigation can deliver substantial air quality co-benefits, yet these remain poorly quantified across pathways ranging from sufficiency-to technology-driven transitions. This study compares four French energy-transition scenarios for 2030 and 2050 against a 2019 baseline under fixed meteorology, evaluating annual PM2.5 and NO2 concentration changes and health and economic co-benefits. METHODS: PM2.5 and NO2 concentrations for 2030 and 2050 were estimated with the CHIMERE chemistry-transport model using scenario-specific emission projections. refractive.title: Impact of Laser Vision Correction on Readiness and Operational Performance Among Active Duty Service Members.
refractive.summary: LVC is associated with substantial self-reported improvements in visual readiness and operational task performance, with exceptionally high, comparable satisfaction across PRK, LASIK, and SMILE cohorts. …
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Optimal visual performance is essential for modern military operations. Traditional forms of vision correction, including spectacles and contact lenses, may present operational limitations during deployment or field training. The Department of Defense established the Warfighter Refractive Eye Surgery Program (WRESP) to provide laser vision correction (LVC) to improve operational readiness by reducing reliance on corrective eyewear among active duty service members (ADSM). This study evaluated ADSMs' perceptions of overall satisfaction, visual outcomes, operational performance, and military readiness following LVC performed at the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA)-Lackland, Joint Warfighter Refractive Surgery Center (JWRSC). refractive.summary: During the 3-year follow-up of ICL V4c implantation, a gradual increase in ACD-ICL was significantly associated with vault reduction.

SETTING: A tertiary specialized eye hospital in Shanghai, China. DESIGN: Prospective, non-randomized, consecutive case series. METHODS: This study included 32 eyes of 20 patients with high myopia who underwent ICL V4c implantation with a 3-year follow-up. Preoperative assessments included standard biometry and anterior segment parameters. Postoperative evaluations were conducted at 1 day, 1 month, 3 months, and 3 years. Parameters assessed included corneal endothelium-anterior capsule distance (ACD-L), corneal endothelium-ICL distance (ACD-ICL), ICL-anterior capsule distance (ICL-L), anterior chamber angle (ACA) parameters, and iris metrics. However, existing computational methods rely on single-modality inputs and lack complementary molecular information to sufficiently enhance the accuracy and efficiency of neurotoxicity risk assessment. Here, we present NeuroToxPredictor, a scalable and interpretable multimodal framework built on a curated chemical neurotoxicity dataset for accurate and efficient chemical neurotoxicity prediction. It integrates graph attention networks and molecular fingerprints with ChemBERTa, a pretrained chemical language model that provides contextual encoding of SMILES. refractive.title: Etidronate-enhanced sodium hypochlorite irrigation in root canal therapy: A scoping review of efficacy and safety.
refractive.summary: Preclinical evidence suggests that NaOCl + HEDP may improve apical cleaning while maintaining antimicrobial activity and acceptable compatibility. However, because the evidence is predominantly laboratory-based and only one clinical trial was identified, clinical superiority and safety cannot yet be established. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous chelation with sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) and etidronic acid (HEDP) has been proposed for root canal irrigation. However, its efficacy and safety compared with sequential regimens remain unclear. To map evidence on the efficacy and safety of NaOCl + HEDP in root canal treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Virtual Health Library were searched up to October 31, 2025. Of 576 records, 10 studies were included (6 in vitro, 3 ex vivo, and 1 clinical). Data were charted on study design, irrigation protocols, comparators, antimicrobial effects, cleaning outcomes, material compatibility, biomarkers, and postoperative pain.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional study was performed on patients who underwent PRK. refractive.summary: The SMILE-Stroke score was feasible, reproducible, and associated with established functional and discharge outcomes in selected MT-treated patients with pre-stroke disability. It may complement the mRS by identifying preserved or regained patient-centered functional domains within poor mRS categories.
refractive.abstract: AIM: The benefit of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischemic stroke in patients with pre-stroke moderate-to-severe disability is difficult to evaluate using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) alone. We developed and evaluated the SMILE-Stroke score as a patient-centered outcome measure. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 31 patients with pre-stroke mRS scores of 3-5 who underwent MT. The 10-point SMILE-Stroke score, comprising Speech, Mobility, Ingestion, Lavatory, and Engagement domains, was assessed at discharge; a score ≥ 4 was prespecified as favorable. refractive.title: Visual and refractive outcomes of implantable phakic contact lens implantation in myopia and myopic astigmatism.

refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the visual, refractive, and safety outcomes of posterior chamber Implantable Phakic Contact Lens (IPCL) implantation for the correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism in a large cohort. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis including patients who underwent IPCL implantation for myopia or myopic astigmatism and completed a minimum of 24 months of follow-up. Preoperative and postoperative assessments included uncorrected and corrected distance visual acuity (UDVA and CDVA), manifest refraction, intraocular pressure measurement using Goldmann applanation tonometry, mean vault, and endothelial cell density (Topcon SP-1A). Visual outcomes, predictability, stability, and complications were evaluated over follow-up at 1, 6, 12, and 24 months. refractive.summary: The Eyecryl pIOL is a safe, effective, and predictable option for the correction of myopia and astigmatism, demonstrating refractive stability over a 2-year follow-up period.

SETTING: Tertiary eye care hospital in South India. DESIGN: Retrospective study. refractive.summary: Topo-guided LASIK induces central/paracentral epithelial thickening with reduced uniformity. The EUI is a useful tool to quantify remodeling. Cyclosporine did not significantly enhance epithelial uniformity.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate epithelial remodeling after topo-guided LASIK using a novel Epithelial Uniformity Index (EUI) and to assess whether topical cyclosporine improves postoperative epithelial uniformity compared to standard care. METHODS: In this retrospective comparative study, we analyzed 122 eyes of 62 patients undergoing topo-guided LASIK, divided into cyclosporine ( n = 60) and non-cyclosporine ( n = 62) groups. Epithelial thickness was measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography across four corneal zones (central, inner, middle, outer) preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months. refractive.abstract: Background: Moderate-to-high refractive error generates long-term direct and indirect costs through corrective devices, complications, and productivity losses. The economic value of implantable collamer lens (ICL) surgery relative to contact lens (CL)-based correction with backup spectacles remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the 25-year cost-effectiveness of posterior chamber phakic ICL implantation versus CL-based correction across four refractive subgroups from a Norwegian societal perspective. Methods: A Markov cohort model followed patients aged 25-50 years with high myopia, high myopia with astigmatism, high hyperopia, or high hyperopia with astigmatism. refractive.summary: In real-world practice, ab-interno canaloplasty performed using iTrack Advance in mild-to-moderate uncontrolled OAG achieved significant and sustained reductions in IOP and medication burden over 12 months with a favorable safety profile.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective, observational, multicenter study reviewed consecutive ab-interno canaloplasty procedures performed using the iTrack Advance (Nova Eye Medical, US) across 11 US sites between 2022 and 2024. Eligible eyes had mild-to-moderate OAG, uncontrolled baseline intraocular pressure (IOP) ≥18 mmHg and <36 mmHg and at least 12 months of follow-up. Outcome measures included IOP and topical medication burden at 1, 6 and 12 months postop. Secondary outcomes included surgical success according to American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) criteria. refractive.abstract: Impact sensitivity under mechanical stimuli is one of the most crucial safety properties of energetic materials. The drop-weight test is a common method for evaluating the impact sensitivity of explosives, with results typically reported as the 50% initiation height (H 50) or drop energy (E 50 (cm)). In this study, three quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) models were developed and assessed to predict the logarithm drop-weight impact sensitivity (log E 50) of various types of explosive materials using a Monte Carlo algorithm implemented via CORAL software. The descriptor of correlation weight (DCW) was computed from the SMILES notations of the compounds. refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) comprises a group of inherited conditions affecting enamel formation and mineralization, with significant esthetic, functional, and psychosocial consequences. Management of adolescents with hypocalcified AI remains challenging because of the compromised enamel structure, ongoing craniofacial growth, and need to preserve future restorative options. This report describes a staged direct and indirect composite approach in an adolescent with hypocalcified AI and concomitant Bartter syndrome, including its short-term clinical performance and limitations. refractive.summary: ICL implantation alters biometric measurements and theoretically predicted Δ-pSEQ; although these changes are statistically significant, their clinical significance is negligible. refractive.title: Trends of menopausal hormone therapy across Canadian provinces in 2018-2023.
refractive.summary: MHT use in Canada is increasing but remains modest and variable across formulations and provinces. Markedly higher use of MHT in Quebec may be partly explained by a more comprehensive drug coverage. …
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is guideline-recommended as the first-line treatment for vasomotor symptoms in women without contraindications. Despite this, use of MHT remains low with persistent concerns about safety following the Women's Health Initiative. Contemporary population-level data on the trends of MHT use in Canada over the years, as well as differences across provinces, are limited. This study examines recent trends and interprovincial variation in MHT expenditure among Canadian provinces. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time-series study of MHT dispensing trends across Canadian provinces (December 2017-November 2023) using IQVIA CompuScript. Laser refractive surgery procedures (such as laser in-situ keratomileusis), surface ablation techniques (such as laser epithelial keratomileusis), and photorefractive keratectomy have now been established as fairly safe procedures that produce excellent visual outcomes for patients with low-to-moderate amounts of ametropia. refractive.abstract: UNLABELLED: This review looks at the benefits, limitations, complications, and future applications of the small-incision lenticule extraction procedure. Using the search terms small incision lenticule extraction and femtosecond lenticule extraction, we obtained data from 56 articles (omitting German and Chinese articles) from the PubMed database. Small-incision lenticule extraction has shown efficacy, predictability, and safety that are proportionate to those of laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), with the additional benefit that it eliminates flap creation and the attendant risks. The potential advantages of the procedure related to improved biomechanical stability, postoperative inflammation, and dry-eye symptoms have not been fully established. refractive.summary: Refractive surgery refers to any procedure that corrects or minimizes refractive errors. Today, refractive surgery has evolved beyond the traditional laser refractive surgery, embodied by the popular laser in situ keratomileusis or 'LASIK'. …
refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery refers to any procedure that corrects or minimizes refractive errors. Today, refractive surgery has evolved beyond the traditional laser refractive surgery, embodied by the popular laser in situ keratomileusis or 'LASIK'. New keratorefractive techniques such as small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) avoids corneal flap creation and uses a single laser device, while advances in surface ablation techniques have seen a resurgence in its popularity. Presbyopic treatment options have also expanded to include new ablation profiles, intracorneal implants, and phakic intraocular implants. With the improved safety and efficacy of refractive lens exchange, a wider variety of intraocular lens implants with advanced optics provide more options for refractive correction in carefully selected patients. refractive.abstract: Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) keratorefractive surgery technique is a laser surgery alternative to common methods that doesn't require laser ablation of the cornea. Despite its novelty, SMILE technique has already demonstrated positive clinical results comparable to Photorefractive Keratectomy (PRK) and Laser-Assisted in Situ Keratomileusis (LASIK), which led to its widespread application in clinical practice. Compared with other keratorefractive techniques, SMILE has a number of distinct advantage including high biomechanical stability of the cornea, low risk of dry eye syndrome, absence of a corneal flap and associated complications, preservation of corneal epithelium. The article describes the most common SMILE modifications, its weak points and possible complications, as well as methods of additional correction of remaining ametropy.

refractive.abstract: Dry eyes is one of the most common complications after laser vision correction. Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) is a flapless procedure with a smaller corneal incision, less corneal nerves are transected during, making it theoretically less prone to dry eyes. Both SMILE and femtosecond-laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) induce a transient worsening in dry eye parameters, but there is evidence showing that SMILE holds promises to have fewer negative impacts on the ocular surface parameters and allow an earlier recovery. SMILE-treated eyes may also have shown less corneal denervation and better corneal sensitivity compared with FS-LASIK eyes. refractive.title: Dry Eye After LASIK.
refractive.summary: Post-LASIK dry eye is the most common postoperative dry eye after ophthalmic surgeries. The clinical signs of post-LASIK dry eye include positive vital staining of the ocular surface, decreased tear breakup time and Schirmer test values, reduced corneal sensitivity, and decreased functional visual acuity. …
refractive.abstract: Post-LASIK dry eye is the most common postoperative dry eye after ophthalmic surgeries. The clinical signs of post-LASIK dry eye include positive vital staining of the ocular surface, decreased tear breakup time and Schirmer test values, reduced corneal sensitivity, and decreased functional visual acuity. The symptoms and signs usually last for about 1 month after LASIK. A small number of patients continue to experience symptoms more than 1 year postoperatively. It has been suggested that the loss of corneal innervation caused by flap-making is the major cause, affecting the corneal-lacrimal gland, corneal-blinking, and blinking-meibomian gland reflexes, resulting in decreased aqueous and lipid tear secretion and mucin expression. refractive.abstract: Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) was introduced in the recent decade for the treatment of myopia and myopic astigmatism. This flap-free technique has a high efficacy and safety profile and also carries potential advantages over laser in situ keratomileusis such as a better corneal biomechanical stability, reduction in dry eyes rate, and the avoidance of flap complications. However, there have been concerns regarding the precision of astigmatism correction that undercorrection has been reported to be apparent. Various factors that affect astigmatism correction have been identified in the literature. The purpose of this review is to discuss the factors that affect astigmatism correction in SMILE and several techniques to improve the refractive outcomes.

refractive.summary: Refractive lenticule extraction is a corneal surgical technique that uses a femtosecond laser exclusively to create an intrastromal refractive lenticule for the correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism. In small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) the generated refractive lenticule is subsequently extracted through a small incision. …
refractive.abstract: Refractive lenticule extraction is a corneal surgical technique that uses a femtosecond laser exclusively to create an intrastromal refractive lenticule for the correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism. In small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) the generated refractive lenticule is subsequently extracted through a small incision. The reported efficacy, predictability and safety of the flap-less SMILE procedure is similar to those of femtosecond laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK). Advantages of SMILE over LASIK include less iatrogenic dry eye, fewer induced higher-order aberrations, and potentially less biomechanical weakening of the cornea. However, there is a steeper surgeon learning curve for SMILE as the procedure is technically more challenging than LASIK. METHODS: One hundred eyes of 50 patients (age, 21-41 years) with low and moderate myopia were enrolled in this prospective case series. Visual, refractive, ocular aberrometric, ocular scattering index (OSI) and patient satisfaction outcomes were evaluated after a 90-day follow-up period. Astigmatic changes were evaluated by vector analysis. refractive.title: Femtosecond laser in refractive corneal surgery.
refractive.summary: The introduction of the femtosecond (fs) laser has revolutionized ophthalmic surgery. With the worldwide application of fs-lasers, clinical outcomes and safety in corneal procedures have improved significantly and they have become an ideal tool for ultra-precise corneal refractive surgery. …
refractive.abstract: The introduction of the femtosecond (fs) laser has revolutionized ophthalmic surgery. With the worldwide application of fs-lasers, clinical outcomes and safety in corneal procedures have improved significantly and they have become an ideal tool for ultra-precise corneal refractive surgery. Flap creation in laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common use of this laser. It can also be used for other corneal refractive procedures including channel creation for the insertion of intrastromal corneal ring segments (ICRS), performing astigmatic keratotomies (AK), femtosecond lenticule extraction including small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE), and the insertion of corneal inlays. This article summarizes recent advanced applications of fs laser technology in corneal refractive surgery.

refractive.title: Intraocular Pressure After Corneal Refractive Surgery.
refractive.summary: The reduction of IOP after LASIK refractive surgery is significant. This reduction is about 1mmHg per 1 diopter. This should be taken into account in the future in these patients because, due to the underestimation of the IOP, the glaucoma disease may be overlooked.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), a refractive surgery procedure is being performed in a large number among people with refractive errors. In all the people undergoing the procedure, there is a potential risk to misdiagnose the glaucoma disease due to changes in central corneal thickness (CCT). In subjects who have undergone laser refractive interventions, intraocular tension may be lower and underestimated, and this can lead to later detection of glaucoma. AIM: The objective of this study was to analyze the intraocular pressure (IOP) after LASIK in patients with myopia. METHODS: Thirty-seven patients underwent LASIK intervention to treat myopia. refractive.abstract: One of the leading challenges in refractive surgery today is the presence of underlying subclinical early-stage keratoconus (KC), which can lead to iatrogenic post laser in situ keratomileusis ectasia. Timely detection of this condition could aid the refractive surgeons in better decision-making. This includes being able to defer refractive surgery in subclinical cases as well as providing treatment for the same in the form of appropriate corneal collagen crosslinking treatments. Corneal topography is considered the gold standard for the diagnosis of corneal ectatic disorders. However, there is a likelihood that topographers are overlooking certain subclinical cases. The corneal epithelium is known to remodel, which may mask underlying stromal irregularities. refractive.title: Small incision lenticule extraction for the correction of high myopia.
refractive.summary: We found equally good visual and refractive outcomes after small incision lenticule extraction for the correction of high and of moderate myopia combined with an astigmatic correction of up to 3 D, respectively.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: Excimer laser-based refractive procedures can have less predictable results when used for correcting high myopia than when used for moderate myopia. Small incision lenticule extraction might overcome this weakness. However, small incision lenticule extraction is only Food and Drug Administration approved for use in myopic eyes up to -8 D with astigmatism of -3 D or less. We report outcomes of small incision lenticule extraction in highly and moderately myopic eyes and compare these to modern laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis. METHODS: Retrospective, observational consecutive case series. Inclusion criteria: attempted myopic spherical correction ⩾-8 or-3 to -7.75 D with astigmatism ⩽-3 D, and corrected distance visual acuity of 1.0 (decimal scale) or better. METHODS: This prospective study of 60 consecutive hyperopic SMILE procedures used the VisuMax femtosecond laser and matched LASIK procedures with the VisuMax and MEL 80 excimer lasers (Carl Zeiss Meditec AG, Jena, Germany). Inclusion criteria were maximum attempted hyperopic meridian of between +1.00 and +7.00 diopters (D) and astigmatism up to 6.00 D. refractive.title: Risk Factors for Dry Eye After Refractive Surgery.

refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the factors associated with clinically significant dry eye after keratorefractive surgery. METHODS: This is a large database retrospective study that included consecutive cases of myopic laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) or photorefractive keratectomy performed between 2008 and 2016 at Care-Vision Laser Center, Israel. Patients were divided into 2 groups according to whether they developed clinically significant dry eye. RESULTS: A total of 25,317 right eyes of 25,317 patients, with a mean age of 27.0 ± 8.3 years, were included. Postoperative dry eye developed in 1518 eyes (6.0%). refractive.title: Refractive Eye Surgery: Helping Patients Make Informed Decisions About LASIK.
refractive.summary: A variety of refractive surgery techniques, which reshape the corneal stroma using laser energy, have been marketed as simple and safe alternatives to glasses or contact lenses. Laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common of these procedures. …
refractive.abstract: A variety of refractive surgery techniques, which reshape the corneal stroma using laser energy, have been marketed as simple and safe alternatives to glasses or contact lenses. Laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common of these procedures. Although there are few high-quality prospective studies of long-term outcomes, complications, or stability for refractive surgery procedures, there is at least general agreement that more than 90% of appropriately selected patients achieve excellent uncorrected distance vision. In addition to well-recognized contraindications (e.g., unstable refraction, pregnancy and lactation, chronic eye disease, systemic illness, corneal abnormalities), there are other conditions that warrant caution (e.g., excessively dry eyes, contact lens intolerance, chronic pain syndromes). refractive.summary: Refractive surgery in the late adulthood population of our cohort was a relatively safe procedure, yet manifesting lower efficacy and requiring more retreatments. In adolescents, results were comparable to those achieved in young adults.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: Most refractive surgeries are performed in the young-adult age group, and less is known about the clinical outcomes of patients in late adulthood and of adolescents. The purpose of this study was to describe the outcomes of refractive surgery in patients over the age of 60 years and under the age of 18 years compared with a control group of patients aged 20-40 years. METHODS: This retrospective cohort analysis consisted of 64,970 consecutive cases of 32,074 patients who underwent laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis and photorefractive keratectomy during a 10-year period in a single center. refractive.summary: There has been a trend toward treating residual LASIK refractive error through surface ablation. This review suggests that flap lift may result in a more accurate refractive outcome, albeit with an expected greater risk of epithelial ingrowth. [J Refract Surg. 2020;36(1):6-11.].
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To review safety and efficacy outcomes following re-treatment for residual refractive errors in eyes with prior laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and determine the most appropriate course of action for patients. METHODS: A review of all patients undergoing LASIK enhancement at a single refractive surgery center between 2012 and 2017 was undertaken. RESULTS: A total of 108 eyes were included in the analysis; 58 eyes underwent flap lift and 50 underwent surface ablation retreatment with mean times to enhancement of 22.3 and 53.2 months, respectively. Although there remains a number of similarities to existing techniques in terms of patient selection and treatment parameters, consideration is required to optimise patient outcomes and satisfaction. Here, we review the selection criteria, contraindications, indications and existing published safety and efficacy outcomes.

refractive.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Refractive surgery is one of the most popular elective procedures performed in the world. Given that dry eye is a common complaint following keratorefractive surgery, evaluation, and treatment of periocular conditions that further predispose the patient to dry eye symptoms is an important part of the presurgical assessment. Periocular conditions and surgeries can also affect the ocular surface and keratometry, and should be addressed. For example, ptosis, orbital fat herniation, ectropion, and eyelid masses have been shown to induce corneal topography changes and astigmatism. The oculoplastic considerations for refractive surgery include both the contribution of eyelid position on dry eye, ocular surface damage, refractive error, and outcomes, as well as the timing of oculoplastic surgery in relation to the refractive surgery. refractive.abstract: Laser refractive surgery (LRS) is one of the most demanding areas of ophthalmic surgery and high level of precision is required to meet outcome expectations of patients. Post-operative recovery is of vital importance. Keratitis occurring after LRS can delay visual recovery. Both surface ablations [Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK)] as well as flap procedures [Laser in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK)/Small incision lenticule extraction] are prone to this complication. Reported incidence of post-LRS infectious keratitis is between 0% and 1.5%. The rate of infections after PRK seems to be higher than that after LASIK. Staphylococci, streptococci, and mycobacteria are the common etiological organisms. About 50-60% of patients present within the first week of surgery. refractive.summary: This is the first long-term study evaluating refractive surgery outcomes up to 17 years in a military population. Our study demonstrates safety after refractive surgery in the military with less than 0.1D increase in myopia per year and strong keratometric stability. …

refractive.summary: Refractive enhancement after SMILE is currently mostly performed by surface ablation, CIRCLE cap-to-flap conversion or thin-flap LASIK, which all offer safety and efficacy comparable to LASIK retreatments. In this review, a detailed overview over each method, its technical aspects, and specific advantages and disadvantages is given.

refractive.abstract: Corneal refractive surgeries are one of the commonly performed procedures for correction of refractive errors. Tear film abnormality is the most common postoperative complication of corneal refractive surgeries. Consequently, these procedures represent a clinically significant cause of dry eye disease. The mechanisms which lead to dry eye disease include corneal sensory nerve dysfunction, ocular surface desiccation, glandular apoptosis and ocular surface inflammation. Although transient tear film abnormalities occur in almost all patients following surgery, patients with pre-existing dry eye symptoms or dry eye disease are at significant risk of developing more severe or long-term ocular surface disease. refractive.abstract: Laser subepithelial keratomileusis (LASEK) has become a viable alternative to photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) and laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in selected patients. LASEK may decrease the complications associated with PRK, including postoperative pain and slow visual rehabilitation. In this article, the authors present the visual outcomes and complication rates of LASEK based on the retrospective case review of 101 consecutive patients (163 eyes) treated with LASEK surgery over the past 6 years. Seventy-eight percent of these eyes showed complete epithelial healing by day 3, and there were no incidents of recurrent erosions. As with LASIK, the achieved correction for LASEK was greater than the treatment dose (requiring undercorrection nomogram adjustments). Mean logMAR UCVA was 0.03 (20/20) at 1 year. refractive.abstract: Laser-in-situ-keratomileusis (LASIK) has become a popular technique of refractive surgery because of lower postoperative discomfort, early visual rehabilitation and decreased postoperative haze. Compared to photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), LASIK involves an additional procedure of creating a corneal flap. This may result in complications related to the flap, interface and underlying stromal bed. The common flap-related complications include thin flap, button holing, free caps, flap dislocation and flap striae. The interface complications of diffuse lamellar keratitis, epithelial ingrowth and microbial keratitis are potentially sight threatening. Compared to PRK, there is less inflammation and faster healing after LASIK, but there is a longer period of sensory denervation leading to the complication of dry eyes.
