glaucoma.abstract: The major active ingredient of marijuana, delta 9-tetrahydrocannabinol (delta 9-THC), has been used as a psychoactive agent for thousands of years. Marijuana, and delta 9-THC, also exert a wide range of other effects including analgesia, anti-inflammation, immunosuppression, anticonvulsion, alleviation of intraocular pressure in glaucoma, and attenuation of vomiting. The clinical application of cannabinoids has, however, been limited by their psychoactive effects, and this has led to interest in the biochemical bases of their action. glaucoma.title: Prostaglandins and inflammation
glaucoma.summary: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. …
glaucoma.abstract: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. They are generated from arachidonate by the action of cyclooxygenase isoenzymes, and their biosynthesis is blocked by nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, including those selective for inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2. Despite the clinical efficacy of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, prostaglandins may function in both the promotion and resolution of inflammation. This review summarizes insights into the mechanisms of prostaglandin generation and the roles of individual mediators and their receptors in modulating the inflammatory response. Prostaglandin biology has potential clinical relevance for atherosclerosis, the response to vascular injury and aortic aneurysm.

There is no consensus on the efficacy of medical treatment in delaying or preventing the onset of POAG in individuals with elevated IOP. Therefore, we designed a randomized clinical trial, the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study. Objective To determine the safety and efficacy of topical ocular hypotensive medication in delaying or preventing the onset of POAG. glaucoma.summary: Microglia are resident cells of the brain that regulate brain development, maintenance of neuronal networks, and injury repair. glaucoma.abstract: Microglia are resident cells of the brain that regulate brain development, maintenance of neuronal networks, and injury repair. Microglia serve as brain macrophages but are distinct from other tissue macrophages owing to their unique homeostatic phenotype and tight regulation by the central nervous system (CNS) microenvironment. They are responsible for the elimination of microbes, dead cells, redundant synapses, protein aggregates, and other particulate and soluble antigens that may endanger the CNS. Furthermore, as the primary source of proinflammatory cytokines, microglia are pivotal mediators of neuroinflammation and can induce or modulate a broad spectrum of cellular responses. Alterations in microglia functionality are implicated in brain development and aging, as well as in neurodegeneration. retina.title: Occult Optic Disk Pit Maculopathy Masquerading as Exudative Age-Related Macular Degeneration in an Elderly Patient: A Case Report.
retina.summary: Occult ODPM can closely mimic exudative AMD and may go unrecognized for many months in elderly patients with coexisting retinal disease, resulting in repeated unnecessary anti-VEGF treatment.
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Occult optic disk pit maculopathy (ODPM) is a rare cause of macular retinoschisis in which no pit is visible on funduscopic examination. Optic disk pits are congenital cavitary anomalies thought to arise from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure during ocular development. CASE PRESENTATION: This report presents an 83-year-old woman with a history of exudative AMD of the left eye (OS) and low-tension glaucoma having received 11 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections over approximately 18 months without resolution of macular fluid. Fluorescein angiography demonstrated no macular leakage and no macular neovascularization. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography revealed multilayered peripapillary retinoschisis with fluid extending from the optic disk to the fovea. Dedicated optic disk OCT confirmed a deep crater-like excavation consistent with an occult optic disk pit.

retina.abstract: PURPOSE: The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in the foveal avascular zone (FAZ), vascular density (VD), and electrophysiological parameters in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) following intravitreal bevacizumab therapy. METHODS: The study comprised 27 eyes of 22 patients with treatment-naive DME who received a loading phase of three consecutive monthly intravitreal bevacizumab injections, together with 30 eyes of 15 healthy controls. All participants underwent optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), pattern electroretinography (PERG) and visual evoked potentials (VEP) at baseline and at one and three months. As both eyes of some participants were included, all comparisons used generalized estimating equations clustered on subject, with cluster-robust variance estimation. retina.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.
retina.summary: Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial. DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156). METHODS: Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema. RESULTS: In the aITT populatio

retina.title: Bridging Mechanism and Therapy in Ocular Disease: Mitochondrial, Vascular, and Immune Pathways in the Eye.
retina.summary: There is an increasing global burden of ocular disorders, with an estimated 43.3 million people worldwide currently blind and a further 295 million living with moderate-to-severe vision impairment, driven by a complex pathogenesis that involves multiple cascade failures ranging from mitochondrial dysfunction to chronic neuroinflammation a …
retina.abstract: There is an increasing global burden of ocular disorders, with an estimated 43.3 million people worldwide currently blind and a further 295 million living with moderate-to-severe vision impairment, driven by a complex pathogenesis that involves multiple cascade failures ranging from mitochondrial dysfunction to chronic neuroinflammation and blood-retinal barrier breakdown. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature identified through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, prioritizing publications from the last five years and supplemented by foundational studies where necessary, to examine molecular mechanisms underlying both anterior and posterior segment pathologies, including Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), diabetic macular edema (DME), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and antibody-mediated optic neuritis. retina.title: Generative Forecasting of Longitudinal 3D-OCT Under Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. …
retina.abstract: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. Direct volumetric generation is difficult because treatment-associated change is local while most of the retina is stationary, so generative models regress to the mean and blur retinal layers. Methods: We propose a two-stage framework that decouples baseline anatomy from longitudinal change in 3D-OCT. A Retinal Response Tokenizer compresses the latent residual between baseline and follow-up volumes into discrete action tokens via Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ), and a conditional decoder renders the follow-up volume from baseline features and these tokens. retina.title: Changes in expression of DNA-methyltransferase in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: Anti-VEGF response or disease severity?
retina.summary: We hereby report varying DNMTs expression in nAMD patients with different disease manifestations giving new insights into the dynamic nature of epigenetic modifications in response to anti-VEGF treatment.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Recent studies suggest distinct patterns of DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) expression across different stages of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). However, whether these variations can be modulated by conventional therapeutic approaches remains unexplored. This study investigates DNMT expression dynamics in two patients with exudative neovascular AMD (nAMD) during the initial months of anti-VEGF treatment. OBSERVATIONS: Case 1, a female in her 90s was seen for sudden loss of vision secondary to macular hemorrhage. During type 1 macular neovascularization (t1MNV) anti-VEGF treatment, DNMT analysis revealed sustained upregulation of DNMT1 (+116%) and DNMT3b (+179%) while exudative MNV remained presisted.Case 2, a female in her 70s and asymptomatic subretinal fluid secondary to t1MNV showed a distinct DNMT expression pattern, with a more modest increase in DNMT1 (+28.9%) and DN

retina.title: Longitudinal Quantitative Analysis of Ultra-Widefield Fluorescein Angiography Leakage Metrics: Analysis of the KINGFISHER Clinical Trial.
retina.summary: Both brolucizumab and aflibercept substantially reduced UWF-FA leakage in DME over 52 weeks. Brolucizumab achieved a more pronounced early reduction in leakage within the posterior pole, although the final residual leakage at week 52 was comparable between the 2 agents.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To longitudinally quantify changes in retinal vascular leakage in diabetic macular edema (DME) using ultra-widefield fluorescein angiography (UWF-FA) in patients receiving brolucizumab versus aflibercept. DESIGN: Retrospective post hoc analysis of the phase 3, randomized, masked KINGFISHER clinical trial. SUBJECTS: Eyes with center-involved DME enrolled in KINGFISHER with gradable late-phase UWF-FA images at baseline and follow-up (week 24 and/or week 52). METHODS: Two independent masked graders manually assessed late-phase UWF-FA images at baseline, week 24, and week 52 using OptosAdvance software. The leakage area, defined as regions of increased fluorescence relative to background, was manually segmented and quantified in 3 regions: the posterior pole zone (defined as the central 15-mm ring), the peripheral zone (all analyzable areas outside the posterior pole), and the total

retina.title: Noninfectious intraocular inflammation with hypopyon after intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection for neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a case report.
retina.summary: Noninfectious IOI with hypopyon may occur after an intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection. Even when hypopyon is present after an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injection, noninfectious IOI should be included as a differential diagnosis in addition to infectious IOI.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Herein, we report a case of noninfectious intraocular inflammation (IOI) with hypopyon after an intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injection for neovascular age-related macular degeneration. CASE PRESENTATION: An 87-year-old Japanese man with neovascular age-related macular degeneration in the right eye was switched from intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg to aflibercept 8 mg to extend the treatment interval. Three days after the third aflibercept 8 mg injection, the patient presented with decreased vision without ocular pain. Slit-lamp examination revealed mild conjunctival injection and anterior chamber cells. Despite treatment with topical corticosteroids, the inflammation worsened the following day, with increased anterior chamber cells accompanied by a highly mobile hypopyon that shifted with head position. Smear microscopy of the aqueous humor showed neutrophils without detectable

retina.title: Outcomes of Intravitreal Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Kazakhstan.
retina.summary: In this real-world cohort, anti-VEGF therapy was associated with significant anatomical improvement, as measured by CRT reduction, while functional outcomes were characterised by visual stabilisation rather than substantial gains.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss among older adults. Although randomised controlled trials have demonstrated the robust efficacy of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, real-world outcomes often differ markedly from trial findings. This study aimed to evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of anti-VEGF therapy in a clinical cohort of nAMD patients, including a subgroup that received adjunctive rescue photodynamic therapy (PDT) with verteporfin. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational cohort study included 568 patients (634 eyes) with nAMD treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. Bevacizumab was used in 49% of eyes, ranibizumab in 44%, and aflibercept in 7%. Best recorded visual acuity (BRVA) and central retinal thickness (CRT) measured by opt

retina.title: Temporal, Phenotypic, and Treatment-Context Heterogeneity in Retinal Vasculitis Reporting with Pegcetacoplan: A United States Pharmacovigilance Study.
retina.summary: Background/Objectives: Pegcetacoplan slows geographic atrophy (GA) progression, but postmarketing retinal vasculitis remains an important safety concern. We evaluated whether retinal vasculitis reporting changed over time, whether the reported phenotype changed with respect to occlusive coding, and whether vasculitis was associated with i …
retina.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pegcetacoplan slows geographic atrophy (GA) progression, but postmarketing retinal vasculitis remains an important safety concern. We evaluated whether retinal vasculitis reporting changed over time, whether the reported phenotype changed with respect to occlusive coding, and whether vasculitis was associated with identifiable treatment contexts. Methods: We analyzed the United States (US) Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 17 February 2023 through 31 December 2025. Strict retinal vasculitis reports required pegcetacoplan to be coded as the primary-suspect drug. Faricimab was used as a descriptive contemporaneous intravitreal comparator because US exposure estimates could be constructed over the same period; it was not treated as a safety-neutral control. Separately, within all US primary-suspect Syfovre reports, we examin

retina.title: AI-Based OCT Assessment of Anatomic Response During the Loading Phase of Anti-VEGF Therapy in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
retina.summary: All agents improved functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase in treatment-naive nAMD. Baseline-adjusted analyses showed differences in anatomic response patterns across treatments. Exploratory AI-based OCT biomarkers may help characterize short-term anatomic response; however, these findings require external validation.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase of intravitreal bevacizumab, aflibercept 2 mg, or faricimab in treatment-naive neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), using artificial intelligence (AI)-based optical coherence tomography (OCT) analysis. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 224 eyes. Patients received three monthly injections of bevacizumab (n = 80), aflibercept 2 mg (n = 78), or faricimab (n = 66). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and spectral-domain OCT were assessed at baseline and week 12. AI-based segmentation quantified volumetric measurements of intraretinal fluid (IRFv), subretinal fluid (SRFv), and pigment epithelial detachment. The primary outcome was qualitative dry macula (absence of intraretinal fluid and subretinal fluid). An exploratory composite OCT biomarker (ΔCOMBO), defined as the less

retina.title: Outcomes of subthreshold diode micropulse laser and anti-VEGF vs anti-VEGF monotherapy for diabetic macular edema: a meta-analysis.
retina.summary: In patients with DME, SDMLP and anti-VEGF combination therapy appears comparable, and possibly modestly superior to anti-VEGF monotherapy, with a reduced injection burden over 12 months. BCVA and CMT differences were below clinically important thresholds and supported by low-certainty evidence.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare visual and anatomic outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema treated with subthreshold diode micropulse laser photocoagulation (SDMLP) and anti-VEGF combination therapy versus anti-VEGF injection monotherapy. DESIGN: Meta-analysis. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library between January 2005 and April 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) after SDMLP and anti-VEGF combination therapy versus anti-VEGF monotherapy. The primary outcome was change in BCVA (∆BCVA). Secondary outcomes included absolute BCVA and CMT at all time points, change in CMT (∆CMT) from baseline to all time points, and the number of anti-VEGF injections over 12 months. Outcomes were reported as a weighted mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

retina.title: The potential of ruxolitinib as a senomorphic therapy in alleviating neovascular age-related macular degeneration : Ruxolitinib inhibits CNV.
retina.summary: Our study identifies the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway as a key regulator of the SASP in senescent RPE and confirms its activation in nAMD and experimental CNV. Pharmacologic inhibition of this pathway with ruxolitinib effectively attenuates CNV progression with a favorable short-term safety profile, supporting its potential as a senomorphic thera …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cellular senescence plays a key role in the pathogenesis of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). Senomorphic therapy, which targets the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), holds promise for treating age-related diseases; however, effective senomorphic treatments for nAMD remain lacking. METHODS: We screened a panel of senomorphic agents in bleomycin- and ionizing radiation (IR)-induced senescent ARPE-19 cells to identify a lead compound for nAMD. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to explore JAK-STAT signaling activation. Ruxolitinib and siRNA were used to validate the role of the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway in senescent retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). A laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV) model was established in Brown-Norway rats for in vivo studies. RESULTS: Ruxolitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, most effectively suppress

retina.title: Development full-thickness macular hole and exudative retinal detachment in central retinal vein occlusion after intravitreal ranibizumab.
retina.summary: Although vitrectomy combined with removal of the inner limiting membrane can reclose macular hole caused by intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF drugs, these cases of FTMH differ from those of idiopathic FTMH in having a poorer visual prognosis. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravitreal injection of anti‑vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has become a first-line treatment for macular oedema secondary to central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). However, there have been recent reports of a surprising complication associated with intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF. We report a case of full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) and exudative retinal detachment (ERD) after intravitreal injection of ranibizumab for macular oedema. CASE PRESENTATION: A 21-year-old patient with macular oedema secondary to CRVO developed FTMH and ERD in her left eye after the first intravitreal injection of ranibizumab. A 25 G vitrectomy was performed, during which the internal limiting membrane was peeled off followed by filling with silicone oil tamponade. One week after the operation, optical coherence tomography showed closure of the macular hole. CONCLUSION: Although

retina.title: Choroidal structural changes following intravitreal injection of faricimab or aflibercept 8 mg in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
retina.summary: Aflibercept 8 mg was associated with reduced overall choroidal thickness, whereas faricimab was associated with reduced luminal choroidal proportion. These findings may indicate differences in choroidal structural changes between the two agents during the first three injections, although further studies with larger sample sizes are needed …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare choroidal structural changes following the initial three injections of faricimab or high-dose (8 mg) aflibercept in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). METHODS: This retrospective study included 38 eyes (comprising both treatment-naïve and switch cases) that received three consecutive intravitreal injections of either faricimab (n = 24) or aflibercept 8 mg (n = 14). Subfoveal choroidal area was manually segmented on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography and binarized using Niblack's method. The evaluated parameters were central choroidal thickness (CCT) and the luminal-to-choroidal area ratio (L/C ratio). RESULTS: CCT significantly decreased in the aflibercept 8 mg group (P < 0.001), whereas the faricimab group showed no significant post-hoc pairwise differences. Conversely, faricimab was associated with a significant longitudinal red

retina.title: Recalcitrant Diabetic Macular Edema Case Report despite Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Therapy during Pregnancy.
retina.summary: This report presents a severe case of DME that was recalcitrant to treatment with anti-VEGF treatment during pregnancy. The fetal loss is likely attributable to underlying medical conditions, including poorly controlled diabetes, hypertension, and congestive heart failure exacerbations requiring hospitalizations, rather than IVB. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is often the first-line treatment for diabetic macular edema (DME), but during pregnancy, focal laser photocoagulation is often preferred. We aim to report a case of anti-VEGF use during pregnancy for DME. CASE PRESENTATION: A 37-year-old pregnant female with a history of insulin-dependent, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and proliferative diabetic retinopathy with macular edema presented with decreased vision. She had previously undergone focal laser therapy, but due to the appearance of symptomatic scotomas, had declined further focal laser treatment. Despite receiving intravitreal bevacizumab (IVB) injections, the patient's DME worsened during pregnancy. retina.title: From bench to bedside: translational advances, therapeutic targets, and delivery strategies in diabetic retinopathy.
retina.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness in adults of working age. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is the reference standard for diabetic macular edema (DME), yet in randomized cohorts, approximately 30-40% of DME eyes still show central macular thickening after six months of contin …
retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness in adults of working age. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is the reference standard for diabetic macular edema (DME), yet in randomized cohorts, approximately 30-40% of DME eyes still show central macular thickening after six months of continuous treatment. In proliferative DR (PDR), the corresponding limitation is recurrence after treatment interruption rather than primary non-response, and these two patterns should not be conflated. This review examines translational research in DR across four domains. First, we review mechanistic work on the neurovascular unit, metabolic memory and its epigenetic substrate, the gut-retina axis, and human platforms including induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived retinal organoids and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)

retina.title: Mapping the methodological framework of diabetic retinopathy interventional trials: a scoping review on trial design, execution, and reporting practices.
retina.summary: This review represents the first comprehensive assessment of current DR clinical research, exposing key design weaknesses in existing trials. Future meta-analyses and systematic evaluations, informed by the methodological gaps identified in this review, are urgently needed to generate robust evidence that can guide optimal treatment strat …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a prevalent and sight-threatening ocular complication of diabetes, and one of the leading causes of vision loss and blindness among the working-age population worldwide. Driven by a growing understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying DR, treatment strategies have evolved from a sole focus on glycemic control to comprehensive, multi-targeted, and multimodal therapies. This study systematically summarizes the characteristics of current clinical trials focused on DR treatment and evaluates the employed research methodologies. The aim of this review is to explore methodological trends in specific domains, with the hope that such insights may inform future efforts to optimize trial design and improve trial quality. METHODS: This study followed the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and th

retina.title: Real-world injection burden, treatment switching, and visual outcomes in diabetic macular edema: a 563-eye cohort study.
retina.summary: In real-world clinical practice, anti-VEGF therapy for DME was associated with meaningful visual improvement despite a moderate injection frequency. Visual outcomes were primarily associated with baseline visual acuity rather than treatment intensity. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate real-world injection burden, treatment switching patterns, and visual outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) receiving intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included 563 eyes with DME treated with anti-VEGF agents and followed for at least 12 months. All eyes received an initial loading phase of three monthly bevacizumab injections followed by a pro re nata regimen. Primary outcomes were the number of injections and outpatient visits during the first year. Secondary outcomes included change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), distribution of visual outcomes, and treatment switching patterns. Multivariable linear regression and generalized estimating equation (GEE) analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of visual outcomes.

retina.title: Progressive intraocular inflammation with anterior scleritis following intravitreal Faricimab for neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a case report.
retina.summary: This case highlights that initially mild anterior segment inflammation following Faricimab injection can progress to more severe ocular inflammation, such as scleritis, despite early topical therapy. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To report a rare and instructive case of intraocular inflammation following intravitreal Faricimab (Vabysmo) injection that progressed to anterior scleritis despite early intervention. While Faricimab is widely used for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), understanding its potential for delayed, progressive inflammatory complications is crucial for clinical vigilance. CASE PRESENTATION: A 74-year-old Asian male with nAMD developed intraocular inflammation following his fifth intravitreal injection of Faricimab, after four prior uneventful injections. The patient initially presented with corneal edema, anterior uveitis, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). Although initial treatment with topical corticosteroids and IOP-lowering agents led to partial improvement, the inflammation subsequently progressed, manifesting as persistent vitritis and the developmen

retina.title: Predictive factors of functional and anatomical response to dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema.
retina.summary: Baseline SD-OCT biomarkers are significant predictors of treatment response in refractory DME and may support individualized therapeutic decision-making.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To identify clinical and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) biomarkers predictive of functional and anatomical response to intravitreal dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 185 eyes of 98 diabetic patients with center-involving DME refractory to a mean of 7.1±2.8 prior aflibercept (2mg) injections. All eyes received a 0.7mg intravitreal dexamethasone implant and were followed for at least 6 months, with a mean follow-up of 12.9±2.1 months. Functional outcome was assessed by best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) and anatomical outcome by central macular thickness (CMT) on SD-OCT. retina.title: Three Nitrogen Atoms Turn Old Kinase Inhibitors Into New Targetable Remedy.
retina.summary: Pathological neovascularization in the eye is a significant contributor to vision loss in diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy. While anti-VEGF biologics are effective, they require repeated intravitreal injections. …
retina.abstract: Pathological neovascularization in the eye is a significant contributor to vision loss in diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy. While anti-VEGF biologics are effective, they require repeated intravitreal injections. Here, we report a novel principle for designing photoactivatable VEGFR2 inhibitors, along with two examples, EYE1090 and EYE1118. Azido-functionalization in these molecules enables light-triggered receptor binding while preserving potent inhibition in the dark. Both compounds exhibit significantly enhanced activity upon exposure to green light that reaches the human retina, also in the elderly. In vitro, the compounds robustly inhibited angiogenesis and endothelial migration that was further potentiated by light. retina.title: Real-World Longitudinal Outcomes of First-Line Aflibercept 8 mg for Treatment-Naïve Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: Aflibercept 8 mg resulted in a meaningful improvement in BCVA and significant reduction in CRT. The estimated marginal probability of center-involving macular edema suggests that sustained therapy is required during the first 300 days of treatment. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We sought to evaluate longitudinal visual and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) treated with aflibercept 8 mg in routine clinical practice. METHODS: Treatment-naïve eyes with DME receiving aflibercept 8 mg as first-line therapy under an observe-and-plan regimen were evaluated. Medical records were retrospectively reviewed, collecting data on best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central retinal thickness (CRT), and follow-up visits. Longitudinal changes in BCVA and CRT were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with random effects to account for repeated measurements. Analyses were restricted to the first 300 days after baseline. RESULTS: A total of 95 eyes from 77 patients were eligible for evaluation. In the linear mixed-effect model, the estimated marginal mean BCVA improved by 3.6 ETDRS letters (95% CI 1.7-5.6) at 300 days

retina.title: Clustering and Treatment Patterns in Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration and Diabetic Macular Edema: US Claims Database Study.
retina.summary: This study evaluated ophthalmic health care utilization patterns among United States patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) using Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health care claims from July 1, 2016, to July 31, 2020. …
retina.abstract: This study evaluated ophthalmic health care utilization patterns among United States patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) using Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health care claims from July 1, 2016, to July 31, 2020. Patients aged ≥ 50 years for nAMD or ≥ 18 years for DME with ≥ 1 diagnosis record and ≥ 1 anti-VEGF intravitreal injection, and continuous enrollment in medical and pharmacy plans for ≥ 6 months before and ≥ 24 months after the first injection were included. Descriptive summaries and unsupervised machine-learning cluster analysis were conducted based on treatment frequency, intervals, monitoring visits, and corticosteroid use (DME only). Three clusters for nAMD and DME were identified, representing varying treatment intensities from high to low. The differing cluster characteristics suggest that socioeconomic sta

retina.title: Patient and Physician Perspectives on Oral Treatment in Ophthalmology.
retina.summary: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal (IVT) therapy injections are routinely used to treat retinal diseases, including diabetic macular edema (DME), proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), and neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD [nAMD]). …
retina.abstract: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal (IVT) therapy injections are routinely used to treat retinal diseases, including diabetic macular edema (DME), proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), and neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD [nAMD]). Despite their robust efficacy, IVTs may not be effective for all patients and can impact patient quality of life due to the need for frequent injections, ocular adverse events (AEs), and challenges around the injection itself. Oral therapy enabling fewer injections may have a beneficial impact on patients' lives. Several are currently in development for retinal diseases, and existing data suggest that patients would prefer oral to injectable therapies. However, challenges around this possible paradigm shift include potential systemic AEs, adherence and polypharmacy issues, and difficulties specifically targeting

retina.title: Correction: Aflibercept 8 mg in neovascular age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular oedema: Translating clinical trials into clinical practice.
Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
retina.summary: Baseline PED morphology, particularly increased height, is the most consistently reported association with RPE tear in nAMD. Because the evidence is predominantly retrospective, largely unadjusted, and of very low certainty, these are associations rather than validated predictive markers. …
retina.abstract: TOPIC: To identify and synthesize clinical, imaging, and treatment-related risk factors associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) tears in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). CLINICAL RELEVANCE: RPE tears are a vision-threatening complication of nAMD, occurring most often in eyes with pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and frequently temporally associated with initiation of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. Improved recognition of high-risk PED features may enhance counseling and risk stratification. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251075278). retina.title: Visual and anatomical outcomes of early versus delayed anti-VEGF switching after bevacizumab loading in diabetic macular oedema.
retina.summary: PurposeTo compare 24-month visual and anatomical outcomes associated with early versus delayed switching from bevacizumab in treatment-naive eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (DME) and suboptimal early response.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 87 eyes with inadequate response (<5 ETDRS-letter gain and/or <20% cent …
retina.abstract: PurposeTo compare 24-month visual and anatomical outcomes associated with early versus delayed switching from bevacizumab in treatment-naive eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (DME) and suboptimal early response.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 87 eyes with inadequate response (<5 ETDRS-letter gain and/or <20% central macular thickness [CMT] reduction) after three monthly bevacizumab injections. In a month-3 landmark analysis, eyes were classified by the month-3 treatment decision as immediate switch (n = 37) or continued bevacizumab with later switching (n = 50). An observed-timing comparison excluded eyes switched at months 4-5 (n = 7) and compared early switch (month 3; n = 37) with delayed switch (month ≥6; n = 43) to aflibercept 2 mg or ranibizumab. retina.title: A retrospective analysis of treatment switch from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg in nAMD.
retina.summary: This retrospective analysis did not show statistically significant changes in central retinal thickness or best-corrected visual acuity after treatment switch from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Macular neovascularization is one of the most common causes of irreversible vision loss. Intravitreal injections with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor are the treatment of choice. In recent years, new drugs such as faricimab and aflibercept 8 mg have paved the way for longer intervals between intravitreal injections. However, there are currently very few comparative studies on these longer-acting drugs. METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients with at least three consecutive intravitreal injections of faricimab due to neovascular age-related macular degeneration who were subsequently switched from faricimab to aflibercept 8 mg in 2024. The primary outcome was the change in central retinal thickness as measured by optical coherence tomography. The secondary outcome was best-corrected visual acuity. RESULTS: 41 eyes of 38 patients were included. There were no

retina.title: Efficacy of Intravitreal Faricimab for Diabetic Macular Edema and Analysis of Influencing Factors.
retina.summary: In real-world DME treated with a T&E faricimab regimen, patients achieve sustained functional and anatomical improvements with a favorable safety profile. VEGF causes a breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier by influencing the tight junctions of retinal endothelial cells and leading to accumulation of fluid in the macula. In this review, the DDSs developed up to date regarding intravitreal anti-VEGF drugs have been summarised, which include systems as hydrogels, liposomes, microparticles, nanoparticles or implants. retina.abstract: The issue of macular retinal degeneration is one of the key areas of ophthalmology. Recent advances in the targeted delivery of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) suppressants have significantly impacted the patient's prognosis in the form of a significant deceleration in disease progression. Some of the drugs have gradually found their use in other indications (central retinal vein occlusion or diabetic macular edema). The following text gives a brief look at the physiology of VEGF, but not only in the eye, but throughout the human body, particularly in the context of adverse effects resulting from systemic inhibition of its effects.

retina.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME), defined as a retinal thickening involving or approaching the center of the macula, represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. In the last few years, many diagnostic tools have been proven useful in the detection and the monitoring of the features characterizing DME. On the other hand, several therapeutic approaches can now be proposed on the basis of the DME-specific characteristics. The aim of the present chapter is to thoroughly delineate the clinical and morpho functional characteristics of DME and its current treatment perspectives. The pathogenesis and the course of DME require a complex approach with multidisciplinary intervention both at the systemic and local levels.

retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) is a key cytokine in the development of normal blood vessels as well as the development of vessels in tumors and other tissues undergoing abnormal angiogenesis. Here, we review the molecular engineering of two humanized antibodies derived from a common mouse anti-VEGF antibody--bevacizumab, a full-length IgG1 approved for the treatment of specified cancer indications, and ranibizumab, an affinity-matured antibody Fab domain approved for use in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). In clinical trials and as FDA-approved therapeutics, these two anti-VEGF antibodies, bevacizumab (Avastin anti-VEGF antibody) and ranibizumab (Lucentis anti-VEGF antibody), have demonstrated therapeutic utility in blocking VEGF-induced angiogenesis.

retina.abstract: Blood vessels deliver oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body, but also nourish diseases such as cancer. Over the past decade, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of angiogenesis (blood vessel growth) has increased at an explosive rate and has led to the approval of anti-angiogenic drugs for cancer and eye diseases. So far, hundreds of thousands of patients have benefited from blockers of the angiogenic protein vascular endothelial growth factor, but limited efficacy and resistance remain outstanding problems. Recent preclinical and clinical studies have shown new molecular targets and principles, which may provide avenues for improving the therapeutic benefit from anti-angiogenic strategies.

retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is an endothelial cell-specific mitogen in vitro and an angiogenic inducer in a variety of in vivo models. Hypoxia has been shown to be a major inducer of VEGF gene transcription. The tyrosine kinases Flt-1 (VEGFR-1) and Flk-1/KDR (VEGFR-2) are high-affinity VEGF receptors. The role of VEGF in developmental angiogenesis is emphasized by the finding that loss of a single VEGF allele results in defective vascularization and early embryonic lethality. VEGF is critical also for reproductive and bone angiogenesis. Substantial evidence also implicates VEGF as a mediator of pathological angiogenesis. In situ hybridization studies demonstrate expression of VEGF mRNA in the majority of human tumors. retina.abstract: In 2008, we published the first set of guidelines for standardizing research in autophagy. Since then, this topic has received increasing attention, and many scientists have entered the field. Our knowledge base and relevant new technologies have also been expanding. Thus, it is important to formulate on a regular basis updated guidelines for monitoring autophagy in different organisms. Despite numerous reviews, there continues to be confusion regarding acceptable methods to evaluate autophagy, especially in multicellular eukaryotes. Here, we present a set of guidelines for investigators to select and interpret methods to examine autophagy and related processes, and for reviewers to provide realistic and reasonable critiques of reports that are focused on these processes. retina.abstract: In the 10 years that have passed since the Nobel prize-winning discovery of RNA interference (RNAi), billions of dollars have been invested in the therapeutic application of gene silencing in humans. Today, there are promising data from ongoing clinical trials for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration and respiratory syncytial virus. Despite these early successes, however, the widespread use of RNAi therapeutics for disease prevention and treatment requires the development of clinically suitable, safe and effective drug delivery vehicles. retina.summary: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. …
retina.abstract: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. This Review presents new cellular and molecular mechanisms for the resolution of inflammation, revealing key roles for eicosanoids, such as lipoxins, and recently discovered families of endogenous chemical mediators, termed resolvins and protectins. These mediators have anti-inflammatory and pro-resolution properties, thereby protecting organs from collateral damage, stimulating the clearance of inflammatory debris and promoting mucosal antimicrobial defence.

retina.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are the leading platform for gene delivery for the treatment of a variety of human diseases. Recent advances in developing clinically desirable AAV capsids, optimizing genome designs and harnessing revolutionary biotechnologies have contributed substantially to the growth of the gene therapy field. Preclinical and clinical successes in AAV-mediated gene replacement, gene silencing and gene editing have helped AAV gain popularity as the ideal therapeutic vector, with two AAV-based therapeutics gaining regulatory approval in Europe or the United States. Continued study of AAV biology and increased understanding of the associated therapeutic challenges and limitations will build the foundation for future clinical success.

Patients who developed Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 grade ≥ 2 ocular toxicity with complete oncologic and ophthalmologic records were analysed. dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: Insular infraorbital neurovascular pedicle labial salivary gland transplantation (IINPLSGT) is an innovative procedure for the treatment of severe dry eye disease (DED). We aim to evaluate changes in clinical parameters, tear osmolarity, inflammatory cytokine levels, and proteomic profiles following IINPLSGT for severe dry eye patients. METHODS: A single-center, prospective exploratory study was conducted in 10 patients diagnosed with severe DED who underwent IINPLSGT surgery. The Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), tear break-up time (TBUT), Schirmer I test (SIt), corneal fluorescein staining (CFS), ocular manifestations and tear osmolarity were assessed before and after treatment. dryeye.abstract: The corneal nerve plexus is essential to ocular surface homeostasis through sensory detection, trophic support, epithelial repair, blinking, and lacrimal reflexes. In dry eye disease (DED), chronic hyperosmolar, inflammatory, mechanical, and age-related stressors alter nerve morphology and function, contributing to reduced nerve density, aberrant regeneration, microneuroma formation, sensory loss, and peripheral or central sensitization. This review summarizes the ultrastructure of corneal innervation and the molecular basis of corneal sensory transduction, with emphasis on TRPM8, TRPV1, TRPA1, Piezo2, and acid-sensing ion channels. It then examines bidirectional neuroimmune signaling involving dendritic cells, cytokines, neuropeptides, and diminished neurotrophic support. dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial inflammatory eye disease caused mainly by immune dysregulation through JAK/STAT, which leads to a turbulent tear film, damage to the corneal epithelia, and poor visualization. Topical therapies of the conventional type show less ocular bioavailability with quick precorneal excretion. This research was done to design and test a new NanoMiLens system loaded with Tofacitinib Citrate (TFC), which is a selective JAK inhibitor, in order to have a controlled and prolonged contact lens delivery manageable with DED. TFC Polymeric Nano-Micelles (PoT-PNMs) were prepared using a thin-film hydration method employing Poloxamer 407 as the amphiphilic polymer and Tween 80 as the stabilizing surfactant in acetone, then rehydrated with simulated tear fluid. dryeye.abstract: The BCMA×CD3 bispecific T cell engager (TCE) transforms targeted immunotherapy but remains constrained by ex vivo manufacturing and systemic delivery, limiting its application in autoimmune disorders. Here, we use a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector (T-IDLE) to program endogenous T cells to secrete BCMA×CD3 TCEs directly in vivo. In a murine model of Sjögren's syndrome-associated dry eye, a single intravenous administration of T-IDLESTCE achieves deep but time-limited depletion of plasmablasts and plasma cells, reverses lacrimal gland inflammation, and restores tear production without detectable off-target transduction. Longitudinal studies in cynomolgus monkeys demonstrate plasma cell clearance and a favorable safety profile. Human corneal epithelial cells (HCEC) were subjected to hyperosmotic stress and treated with graded rlysozyme. Cell viability, wound healing, barrier integrity, oxidative stress, cytokines, and mitochondrial function were evaluated by MTS and scratch assays, immunofluorescent staining, ELISA, qRT-PCR, and flow cytometry. Results: No cytotoxicity was observed at any of the tested concentrations (2.76 × 10-9-2.76 × 10-4 M) in HCEC. In hyperosmolarity-induced DED cells, rlysozyme at the highest concentrations (2.76 × 10-4 M) significantly increased cell viability by 12.30% (p < 0.001) and promoted corneal repair by 45.04% (p < 0.05), which were compar

dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) is an ocular condition that significantly impairs quality of life. In mild cases, it is commonly treated with artificial tears (ATs), while more advanced cases are managed with immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory drugs. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical anti-inflammatory drugs, immunomodulatory drugs, AT, and their combination in adults with DED. Methods: The protocol was registered in the PROSPERO database (CRD420251245079). Intervention studies were searched in MEDLINE and Scopus databases. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed with the R software (version 4.5.2). Results: A total of 42 studies were included in the meta-analysis of efficacy and 46 in the analysis of safety. dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic topical antiglaucoma therapy may affect the ocular surface. We assessed documented dry eye disease (DED) and its associations with active-ingredient burden, treatment duration, and preservative exposure. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 357 adults receiving topical antiglaucoma therapy at a tertiary center who had complete treatment and ocular-surface data. Ocular-surface testing was prompted by symptoms or clinical judgment. The first eligible visit identified during chronological record review was analyzed for each patient. DED was based on the treating ophthalmologist's documented diagnosis. Logistic regression evaluated treatment-related factors. dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by lacrimal and salivary gland dysfunction, leading to dry eye and dry mouth. This study aimed to explore the potential associations between oxidative stress-mediated immune and apoptotic responses in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye (SSDE) and to computationally predict theoretical interacting candidates. Methods: We enrolled 16 SSDE patients and 15 healthy controls to assess key clinical parameters. The study utilized conjunctival impression cytology, RNA-seq, and bioinformatics to identify exploratory transcriptomic signatures. Gene expression levels were then assessed using real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Data regarding the frequency and spectrum of ocular involvement among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases in Pakistan remain limited. This study aimed to determine the frequency and spectrum of documented ocular manifestations among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. METHODS: A retrospective, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, using medical records from May 2026 to August 2026. dryeye.summary: Motugivatrep 0.3% ophthalmic suspension, as monotherapy or in combination, was well tolerated over 52 weeks, with improvements in both symptoms and signs of DED maintained throughout treatment.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the long-term safety and clinical outcomes of motugivatrep (SJP-0132) 0.3% ophthalmic suspension in patients with dry eye disease (DED). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this open-label, multicenter, 52-week Phase 3 study, patients aged ≥18 years with a ≥6-month history of DED, at least one question scored ≥1 on the Dry Eye-related Quality-of-Life Score questionnaire, eye dryness Visual Analog Scale score ≥40, 5-item Dry Eye Questionnaire score ≥6, and tear break-up time ≤5 seconds received motugivatrep 0.3% (1 drop/eye) four times daily for 52 weeks, as monotherapy or in combination with diquafosol sodium, rebamipide, or sodium hyaluronate. Primary endpoints were the incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). dryeye.title: Patient perception of dry eye disease and treatment: a multinational, cross-sectional, digital survey.
dryeye.summary: The survey data indicated a gap between self-reported dry eye symptoms and self-reported HCP diagnosis and opportunities for improved awareness and knowledge among people with dry eye. …
dryeye.abstract: AIMS: Despite the prevalence and burden of dry eye disease (DED), there are potential gaps in diagnosis, professional assessment and treatment engagement. To better understand individuals’ perspective of dry eye, a multinational survey was conducted to ask about symptoms, interactions with healthcare professionals (HCPs) and treatments. METHODS: Two cohorts were recruited to complete an online survey during 2025 in five countries (France, Germany, Poland, Saudi Arabia and the UK), one representing the general population and the other people with dry eye. No formal diagnosis of DED was required. Data were descriptive, and no inferential statistical analyses were conducted or formal between-country comparisons were made. dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular surface disorder with diverse clinical presentations, yet the comparative efficacy of various Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations remains unclear. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative effects and baseline response relationships of TCM classes for DED across 33 randomized controlled trials retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and CNKI. Primary outcomes included Schirmer I test (SIT), tear film break-up time (TBUT), and corneal fluorescein staining (FL). Random-effects models estimated weighted mean differences (WMD) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs); for FL, which was measured on heterogeneous grading scales and standardized mean differences (SMD) were used. dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Pediatric ocular surface disease associated with ocular rosacea, chronic blepharitis and meibomian gland dysfunction may result in significant corneal morbidity. In refractory cases, the limitations of conventional therapy have stimulated interest in adjunctive treatment modalities, including intense pulsed light (IPL) therapy. METHODS: We report the case of a 10-year-old female patient with cutaneous rosacea, recurrent chalazia and chronic blepharitis who was referred for specialized ocular surface evaluation due to persistent ocular surface disease despite previous treatment. RESULTS: At presentation, slit-lamp examination revealed diffuse keratitis, eyelid telangiectasia, inferior corneal neovascularization and corneal scarring. dryeye.title: "Old is gold" hydralazine, a magic bullet for dry eye disease.
dryeye.summary: Dry eye disease (DED) is a highly prevalent ocular condition characterized by insufficient tear production or poor tear quality, leading to inflammation, discomfort, and potential vision impairment. …
dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a highly prevalent ocular condition characterized by insufficient tear production or poor tear quality, leading to inflammation, discomfort, and potential vision impairment. Current treatments, primarily artificial tears and limited prescription options like steroids, often provide only partial or temporary relief, underscoring the critical need for more effective and safer therapeutic strategies. A key pathological driver of DED is oxidative stress, which generates reactive aldehyde species (RASP) like malondialdehyde and 4-HNE. These cytotoxic electrophiles form adducts with cellular macromolecules, causing widespread damage. This work explores a therapeutic approach focused on scavenging RASP to mitigate this damage. dryeye.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Rebamipide Versus Diquafosol in the Treatment of Dry Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
dryeye.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and tolerability of rebamipide (REB) and diquafosol (DQS), two widely used mucin secretagogues, in the treatment of dry eye disease. …
dryeye.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and tolerability of rebamipide (REB) and diquafosol (DQS), two widely used mucin secretagogues, in the treatment of dry eye disease. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, identifying six comparative studies enrolling 277 patients across South Korea and Japan. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models, standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes and risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). dryeye.title: Depressive and PTSD symptoms are associated with regional differences in light-evoked brain responses in chronic ocular pain.

dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Chronic ocular pain (COP) often co-occurs with depression or post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), but whether these comorbidities confer a distinct biological signature is unknown. Thus, we compared light-evoked blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) responses in individuals with COP, stratified by the presence or absence of clinically relevant depressive and/or PTSD symptoms. SUBJECTS/METHODS: 43 individuals with COP (pain intensity ≥ 1/10 for ≥ 3 months) underwent event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging using bright-light. Thirty participants were classified as COP with mental health comorbidity (COP + MHC+) based on a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score ≥ 5 and/or a PTSD Checklist-Military Version (PCL-M) ≥ 33; 13 were classified as COP without MHC (COP + MHC-). dryeye.title: Trastuzumab and Pertuzumab Suspected Therapy-Induced Ocular Toxicity in Patient Living with HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.
dryeye.summary: Given the limited knowledge regarding the long-term ocular adverse events of HER2-targeted therapies, medical oncologists should routinely ask patients about new-onset or worsening ophthalmic symptoms.
dryeye.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Trastuzumab and pertuzumab, in combination with chemotherapy, are first-line anti-human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2) therapies in the treatment of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer. Although these therapies have been shown to improve the overall survival of patients, they can also be associated with adverse events; ocular toxicities have not been well-documented. CASE PRESENTATION: This report outlines the case of a patient with a spectrum of new-onset transient ocular symptoms on pertuzumab-trastuzumab combination therapy that improved with cessation of the drug and recurred with trastuzumab monotherapy rechallenge. She developed ocular symptoms 2 years into her treatment course. Her principal ophthalmologic diagnosis was dry eye syndrome of bilateral lacrimal glands and keratoconjunctivitis sicca. dryeye.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
dryeye.summary: DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract. SETTING: Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China. DESIGN: Prospective, single-center study. METHODS: A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. dryeye.title: The prevalence of ocular dryness associated with systemic isotretinoin in acne patients in Iraq.
dryeye.summary: Conclusions: This research reveals that ocular dryness may occur during the course of systemic isotretinoin. This research contributes to the raise the awareness of the effects of isotretinoin use on the health of the ocular surface. …
dryeye.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Aim: This research was conducted to assess the prevalence of ocular dryness during the course of systemic isotretinoin in acne patients in Iraq. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: 64 acne patients using systemic isotretinoin in doses ranging from 20mg to 60 mg were enrolled in this study. All patients had been checked for ocular dryness by using Schirmer's test before starting therapy and after each month regularly for 6 times. RESULTS: Results: 64 acne patients were included in this study with a high percentage of the female gender (81.75%) with a mean age of 21.2± 3.4. The mean duration of systemic isotretinoin is 4.3 months while the mean total cumulative dose is 5.8 grams. dryeye.summary: Periocular application of a liposome-based spray on closed eyelids resulted in measurable short-term improvements in tear film stability and patient-reported symptoms without inducing ocular surface irritation. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: Spray-based formulations have been proposed as an alternative approach for ocular surface treatment, particularly to improve ease of administration. However, limited data are available regarding their ability to reach and persist on the ocular surface when applied to closed eyelids. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study evaluated the presence and short-term persistence on the ocular surface of a liposome-based periocular spray in patients with dry eye disease. A total of 20 patients (40 eyes) were included. Tear film parameters were assessed using the Keratograph® 5M at baseline and at 15, 30, and 60 minutes after spray application. Outcome measures included non-invasive Keratograph break-up time (NIKBUT), tear meniscus height, bulbar conjunctival redness and patient-reported ocular discomfort. dryeye.summary: To our knowledge, this appears to be the first reported case of bilateral neurotrophic keratitis during CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and the first ribociclib-associated ocular adverse event refractory to standard topical therapy that improved after procedural intervention. …

The ribociclib label lists dry eye and increased lacrimation among ocular reactions in under 10% of patients, and isolated vortex keratopathy, epithelial keratopathy, and palinopsia are described. dryeye.title: Beyond motor recovery: subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may improve blinking and dry eye symptoms without restoring tear film homeostasis in Parkinson's disease.
dryeye.summary: STN-DBS was associated with increased spontaneous blinking and significant improvement in subjective dry eye symptoms in patients with PD, whereas objective measures of tear film stability, tear production, and ocular surface integrity remained unchanged during short-term follow-up. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the longitudinal effects of subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS) on objective and subjective dry eye parameters in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD). METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 34 patients with advanced PD who underwent STN-DBS. Comprehensive ophthalmic examinations were performed were performed before surgery and at postoperative week 1, month 1, and month 4. Outcome measures included spontaneous blink rate, tear break-up time (TBUT), Schirmer I test, Oxford corneal staining score, and the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Longitudinal changes were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE). dryeye.title: Belumosudil-associated neurological adverse events: evidence from FAERS and experimental validation.
dryeye.summary: This study provides a real-world safety evaluation of belumosudil and identifies potential unlisted neurological AEs. Integration of network pharmacology and neuronal experiments provides preliminary support for the potential biological relevance of these findings and highlights the need for further monitoring of neurological AEs.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: Belumosudil, a first-in-class ROCK2 inhibitor, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in 2021 for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD). This study aimed to evaluate the real-world safety profile of belumosudil and investigate its potential neurological adverse effects (AEs). METHODS: Adverse events (AEs) related to belumosudil were extracted from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from Q3 2021 to Q2 2025. Signal detection was performed using four disproportionality methods: reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). dryeye.title: Hepatocyte growth factor alleviates dry eye disease by modulating the HMGB1/TLR4 signaling pathway: Potential mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
dryeye.summary: HGF protects against DED-associated corneal epithelial injury by suppressing HMGB1/TLR4-mediated inflammatory responses, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target for DED.
dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular surface disorder involving persistent inflammatory responses, redox imbalance, and impairment of corneal epithelial integrity. Despite the recognized regenerative and immunomodulatory functions of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), whether HGF contributes to the maintenance of ocular surface homeostasis during DED progression and the mechanisms involved remain largely undefined. METHODS: A hyperosmolar stress-induced HCEC injury model and a mouse model of experimental DED were established to evaluate the protective effects of HGF. Cell viability, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and apoptosis were assessed using CCK-8, ELISA, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, DCFH-DA staining, and flow cytometry. dryeye.title: Identification of key cell subpopulations and associated biomarkers for mouse dry eye disease based on the Scissor-CIBERSORTx algorithm integration strategy.

This study integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics combined with Scissor and CIBERSORTx algorithms to screen corneal key cell populations and biomarkers in murine …
dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is characterized by tear film instability and chronic inflammation, with the cornea serving as a key target site vulnerable to inflammatory damage. This study integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics combined with Scissor and CIBERSORTx algorithms to screen corneal key cell populations and biomarkers in murine DED. Corneal wing cells were identified as core disease-associated cells, among which interferon-response wing cells (IFN-response-wing) were the pivotal pathogenic subtype. Three IFN-response-wing signature biomarkers Upk3b, Dusp1 and Ly6e were screened, enriched in immune pathways including antigen processing and presentation, primary immunodeficiency, and cytokine receptor interaction. We constructed a chemical-induced DED mouse model for multi-layered validation via immunofluorescence, Real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blot.

dryeye.summary: Androgen deficiency drives MGD through dual mechanisms: reprogramming of meibocyte cell fate toward non-lipogenic lineages and suppression of EMC-mediated stabilization of ER-resident lipogenic enzymes. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the cellular dynamics of androgen-deficient meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms limiting the structural regenerative efficacy of topical dihydrotestosterone (DHT) treatment. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on meibomian glands from sham-operated controls, castrated mice, and castrated mice receiving topical 0.08% DHT. We performed comparative analyses to quantify changes in cell composition, reconstruct differentiation trajectories, and systematically profile alterations in metabolic pathways and organelle homeostasis networks. RESULTS: Castration arrested meibocyte differentiation and redirected cell fate commitment. dryeye.title: Effectiveness of 0.05% cyclosporine A eye drops for dry eye disease in patients with thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy: a prospective, parallel-group cohort study.
dryeye.summary: 0.05% CsA eye drops were associated with improvement in tear film stability, tear secretion, and corneal epithelial integrity in participants with TAO-related DED, and were well tolerated over the 3-month follow-up period.
dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND: Thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO) is frequently accompanied by dry eye disease (DED), which can lead to ocular surface damage and decreased visual quality. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of 0.05% cyclosporine A (CsA) eye drops in the treatment of TAO-related DED. METHODS: This prospective, parallel-group cohort study included 86 participants diagnosed with TAO-related DED. Participants were divided into either the CsA group (n = 43) or the control group (n = 43). The CsA group received 0.05% CsA eye drops (twice daily), and control group received polyethylene glycol eye drops (four times daily). Ocular parameters were assessed pre-treatment and at 1, 2, and 3 months post-treatment. In this study, maltodextrin (MD) was covalently conjugated with pumpkin seed protein (PP) through wet-heating glycation to construct a core-shell nanocarrier for oral pterostilbene (PTE) delivery, designated as PTE@P-M. dryeye.abstract: ROS-related ophthalmic diseases span the ocular surface as well as the anterior and posterior segments of the eye. Dry eye disease (DED), glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy (DR) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) have distinct anatomical targets but share common pathophysiological features, including oxidative stress, inflammation, vascular dysfunction, epithelial injury or neurodegeneration. Conventional ocular drug delivery and therapeutic modalities are hindered by severe limitations, including low bioavailability in the posterior segment of the eye and the requirement for frequent invasive administration. Therefore we evaluated long-term ocular surface and corneal nerve findings after SARS-CoV-2 infection in previously hospitalised patients. METHODS: In this observational study, 26 patients from a cohort of reverse transcriptase-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 cases hospitalised during the first pandemic wave underwent one ophthalmic examination after a median follow-up of 2.77 years (1.67-3.86 years). Based on follow-up symptoms, patients were classified as the post-COVID ocular symptom group (P-COSG, n = 16) or the COVID-19 recovered without ocular symptoms group (CRWOS, n = 10). Tobacco smoke exposure has been associated with ocular discomfort and altered tear-film measures, although findings remain inconsistent. This study compared dry-eye symptoms and ocular-surface signs between tobacco smoke-exposed and non-exposed participants. METHODS: This cross-sectional reanalysis used a retrospective, de-identified dataset collected in Gaza in 2023. The sample comprised 81 participants: 40 tobacco smoke-exposed and 41 non-exposed controls. Exposure was defined by a pooled self-reported binary item encompassing cigarette smoking, shisha use, passive smoke exposure, or combinations thereof. METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, single-center study, 66 participants with newly diagnosed VDT-related dry eye and limited corneal staining were assigned to a full-spectrum screen-bar lamp plus artificial tears (intervention group, n = 34) or artificial tears alone with no study lamp (control group, n = 32). dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory disorder characterized by tear film instability, epithelial damage, and neurosensory abnormalities that compromise ocular surface (OS) homeostasis. Oxidative stress, immune dysregulation and metabolic imbalance contribute to epithelial damage and inflammation. Emerging evidence highlights nutrition as a modifiable adjunctive factor in DED management. This review examines the biological rationale and clinical evidence supporting the role of vitamins A, B12, C, D, and E, as well as polyunsaturated fatty acids, in OS health. Mainly, vitamin A maintains epithelial differentiation and mucin expression; vitamin B12 supports corneal nerve integrity; vitamins C and E mitigate oxidative stress; vitamin D and omega-3 fatty acids modulate inflammatory pathways. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. This focused narrative review integrates physiological, single-cell, spatial, organoid, and mechanistic studies identified through a structured PubMed search and targeted reference checking. We examine how remodeling of the lacrimal secretory niche affects acinar secretory competence, the capacity of viable acinar cells to convert stimulation into coordinated fluid, electrolyte, and protein secretion. Methods: In this pilot, prospective, controlled, non-randomized interventional study, fifteen patients with mixed DED refractory to first-line treatment received topical azithromycin for 30 days (twice daily for 3 days, then once daily for 27 days); ten healthy individuals served as controls. This structured narrative review with evidence mapping integrates clinical, epidemiologic, mechanistic, pharmacovigilance, and management data to define translational pathways from checkpoint blockade to ocular toxicity and treatment decisions. In a real-world cohort of 41,020 ICI-treated patients, ophthalmic irAEs occurred in 4.18% within 1 year, including dry eye disease in 2.00%, conjunctivitis in 0.87%, blepharitis in 0.51%, anterior uveitis in 0.39%, and keratitis in 0.38%. Management options reviewed in detail included treatments for tear insufficiency and lid abnormalities, as well as anti-inflammatory medications, surgical approaches, dietary modifications, environmental considerations and complementary therapies. Following this extensive review it became clear that many of the treatments available for the management of dry eye disease lack the necessary Level 1 evidence to support their recommendation, often due to a lack of appropriate masking, randomization or controls and in some cases due to issues with selection bias or inadequate sample size. dryeye.abstract: Digital eye strain, an emerging public health issue, is a condition characterised by visual disturbance and/or ocular discomfort related to the use of digital devices and resulting from a range of stresses on the ocular environment. This review aims to provide an overview of the extensive literature on digital eye strain research with particular reference to the clinical management of symptoms. As many as 90 per cent of digital device users experience symptoms of digital eye strain. Many studies suggest that the following factors are associated with digital eye strain: uncorrected refractive error (including presbyopia), accommodative and vergence anomalies, altered blinking pattern (reduced rate and incomplete blinking), excessive exposure to intense light, closer working distance, and smaller font size. dryeye.abstract: Meibomian gland dysfunction is the leading cause of evaporative dry eye disease and is one of the most common conditions encountered by eye care providers. The disorder is characterized by obstruction of the meibomian gland terminal ducts and/or changes in their glandular secretion, resulting in changes in tear film stability, inflammation, and symptoms of irritation. There is no gold standard treatment for meibomian gland dysfunction, but rather a diversity of options. Conservative measures include warm compresses and lid hygiene, but there is growing interest and need for medical treatments and procedures. Potential medical treatments include antibiotics, nonsteroidal and steroidal anti-inflammatory agents, essential fatty acid supplementation, hormone therapy, and control of Demodex infestation.
